i.ev: Tibetan "ཐབ་སྐྱོན་ལྡན་སེམས་ཀྱི་སྐད་ཅིག" renders Skt khila-doṣa; bo-mipham 5-33 glosses it as a mind-stream "རྒྱུད་མ་རུང་པ་དགེ་བའི་ས་བོན་མི་འཕེལ་བའི་ཐ་བ་ལྟ་བུ་སྐྱོན་དང་ལྡན་པའི་སེམས" (unfit, barren like ground where seeds of virtue do not grow), not simply hostility; the anger/dispute is the cause stated in the preceding lines.
i.fx: possessing the fault of barrenness

atts.t:
If any bodhisattva who has not obtained a prophecy
Becomes angry and initiates a dispute with one who has obtained a prophecy,
For however many moments of mind possessing the fault of barrenness there are,
For that many eons they must don the armor from the beginning anew.

judge.reason: A correctly translates "thab" as "barrenness" based on Mipham's commentary (tha ba - barren ground), while B misinterprets it as hostility ('thab).

atts.t:
"Buddhas touch awakening through the perfection of patience."
Generating mindfulness, thinking, "This mind is not good,"
They confess individually and restrain themselves in the future,
And do not rejoice in it—they train here in the qualities of a Buddha.

i.sp: "Buddhas touch awakening through the perfection of patience."
i.ev: Quotation marks enclose only line 1 and then a second quotation opens in line 2, so the premise "སངས་རྒྱས་བཟོད་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པས་བྱང་ཆུབ་རེག" reads as thought content. bo-mipham 5-34 and bo-khenrab 5-34 treat it as a stated fact (if buddhas touch awakening through patience, then this angry mind is not good); only "སེམས་འདི་བཟང་བ་མིན" is the thought.
i.fx: Buddhas touch awakening through the perfection of patience;

i.sp: confess individually
i.ev: "སོ་སོར་འཆགས་པ" is the locked term and is rendered "confess"; bo-mipham 5-34 "སྡིག་པའི་དངོས་པོ་དེ་སོ་སོར་འཆགས་པར་བྱེད" and bo-khenrab 5-34 give no sense of confessing "individually".
i.fx: They confess

atts.t:
Buddhas touch awakening through the perfection of patience;
Generating mindfulness, thinking, "This mind is not good,"
They confess and restrain themselves in the future,
And do not rejoice in it—they train here in the qualities of a Buddha.

i.sp: Buddhas touch awakening through the perfection of patience; Generating mindfulness, thinking, "This mind is not good," They confess and restrain themselves in the future,
i.ev: The Tibetan states the Buddhas' attainment as the premise ("སངས་རྒྱས་བཟོད་པའི་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པས་བྱང་ཆུབ་རེག"); the one who generates mindfulness, confesses and restrains is the practitioner, who "trains in this Buddha-dharma" ("དེ་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཆོས་འདིར་སློབ"). bo-mipham 5-34: Buddhas touch awakening by patience, so (one who thinks) "this angry mind of mine is not good" generates the mindfulness, confesses and restrains; bo-khenrab 5-34 same. The English participial "Generating mindfulness..." attaches to the Buddhas, making them the ones who confess.
i.fx: Since Buddhas touch awakening through the perfection of patience, whoever generates mindfulness, thinking "This mind is not good," confesses and also restrains themselves in future,

i.sp: do not rejoice in it
i.ev: "དགའ་བར་མི་བྱེད" has no stated object; bo-mipham 5-34 and bo-khenrab 5-34 specify the angry state and quarrelling ("རྩོད་པ་སོགས་ཀྱི་ངང་ཚུལ་ལ་དགའ་བར་མི་བྱེད"), which "it" does not make clear.
i.fx: do not take pleasure in such anger and quarrelling

i.sp: In order to obtain the qualities of a Buddha
i.ev: Tibetan "སངས་རྒྱས་ཅོས་མཉེས་བྱ་ཕྱིར" says "in order to please" (མཉེས); bo-rangjung 5-36 reads "སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་ཀྱིས་མཉེས་པར་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར", and bo-mipham 5-36 notes this reading ("སངས་རྒྱས་མཉེས་པའམ་དགྱེས་པར་བྱེད་པའི་ཆོས"), though bo-mipham and bo-khenrab prefer "obtain" (བརྙེས་པ). The English follows only the secondary reading and drops the verb of the Tibetan.
i.fx: In order to please the Buddhas by the qualities of a Buddha, they train in this

i.sp: Will never become one with degenerate training or faulty ethical discipline
i.ev: "བསླབ་ཉམས་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་འཆལ་མི་འགྱུར" means they will not come to have degenerated training or corrupt discipline (bo-mipham 5-36 "བསླབ་པ་ལས་ཉམས་པ་དང་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་འཆལ་བར་མི་འགྱུར"); "become one with" suggests union.
i.fx: Will never become one whose training degenerates or whose ethical discipline is faulty

judge.reason: B correctly reflects the context of obtaining (brnyes) Buddha qualities, matching the Sanskrit and commentaries, whereas A translates the literal misspelling 'mnyes' (please).

atts.t:
Training in this way in the wisdom of the wise light-makers,
They do not generate even a single non-virtuous mind;
Just as, when overwhelmed by the rays of the sun moving in the sky,
Darkness does not remain in the space before it.

i.sp: Just as, when overwhelmed by the rays of the sun moving in the sky, / Darkness does not remain in the space before it.
i.ev: Tibetan "ཟིལ་གནོན་པའི། མདུན་གྱི་བར་སྣང་ལ" makes the space before the sun the thing overpowered by the rays; bo-mipham 5-36 "ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་པར་གྱུར་པའི་མདུན་གྱི་བར་སྣང་ལ་ནི་མུན་པ་གཏན་མི་གནས". The English leaves the overwhelmed party unspecified.
i.fx: Just as darkness does not remain in the space before the sun moving in the sky, overpowered by its rays.

atts.t:
Training in this way in the wisdom of the wise light-makers,
They do not generate even a single non-virtuous mind;
Just as darkness does not remain in the space before the sun moving in the sky,
Which is overpowered by its rays.

i.sp: Which is overpowered by its rays.
i.ev: "ཉི་མ་མཁར་ལ་འགྲོ་བའི་ཟེར་གྱིས་ཟིལ་གནོན་པའི། མདུན་གྱི་བར་སྣང": the participle "ཟིལ་གནོན་པའི" qualifies the space ("བར་སྣང") overwhelmed by the sun's rays; bo-khenrab 5-37: "འོད་ཟེར་གྱིས་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་པར་གྱུར་པའི་མདུན་གྱི་བར་སྣང". In the English "Which" can attach to the sun, which would mean the sun is overpowered by its own rays.
i.fx: Just as darkness does not remain in the space before the sun moving through the sky, space overwhelmed by its rays.

judge.reason: A has correct syntax, accurately showing that the space/darkness is overwhelmed by the rays, whereas B mistakenly implies the sun is overpowered.

atts.t:
However many sentient beings there are in realms equal to the sands of the Ganges,
If all of them were to assume forms and become Māras,
And even if they emanated that many more from every single hair,
All of them could not create obstacles for the wise.

i.sp: were to assume forms and become Māras
i.ev: Tibetan "ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་པ་བཟུང་སྟེ་བདུད་གྱུར་ལ" has no word for "forms"; bo-rangjung 5-50 glosses it "ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་པའི་བསམ་པ་བཟུང་སྟེ། བདུད་དུ་གྱུར་པ" (taking up the intention, then becoming Māras); Skt "parikalpa bhaveyu māraḥ".
i.fx: were to take up the intention and become Māras

atts.t:
However many sentient beings there are in realms equal to the Ganges,
If all of them were to take up the intention and become Māras,
And even if they emanated that many more from every single hair,
All of them could not create obstacles for the wise.

i.sp: If all of them were to take up the intention and become Māras
i.ev: "ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་པ་བཟུང་སྟེ་བདུད་གྱུར་ལ" (Skt parikalpa ... bhaveyu māraḥ): a hypothetical supposition ("suppose they all became Māras"). bo-mipham 5-50 introduces it with "དཔེར་ན། གལ་ཏེ་བདུད་དུ་གྱུར་ལ" and bo-khenrab 5-50 "ཡོངས་སུ་བཏག་པ་བཟུང་སྟེ་བདུད་དུ་གྱུར་ལ"; "take up the intention" imports a volitional sense (bo-rangjung's "བསམ་པ") the Tibetan itself does not carry.
i.fx: If all of them were hypothetically to become Māras

i.sp: in realms equal to the Ganges
i.ev: "གང་གཱའི་ཀླུང་མཉམ་ཞིང": the comparison is in number to the grains of sand of the Ganges (Skt gaṅganadivālikasame; bo-mipham 5-50 "རྡུལ་གྱི་གྲངས་དང་མཉམ་པའི་ཞིང"; bo-rangjung 5-50 "བྱེ་མ་སྙེད་དང་མཉམ་པའི་ཞིང"). The English as written says the realms are equal to the river.
i.fx: in realms as numerous as the sands of the Ganges

judge.reason: A correctly translates "yongs su brtag pa" as "intention/concept" (parikalpa), whereas B's "assume forms" misses the mark.

atts.t:
When this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Tathāgatas,
Is taught, whichever bodhisattva aspires to it,
And exerts themselves in accomplishing it with sincere intent,
That noble one should be known to have entered into omniscience.

i.sp: That noble one should be known to have entered into omniscience
i.ev: The Tibetan has no 'noble'; དེས་པ (ངེས་པ, 'definitely') is rendered in bo-rangjung 5-52 as ངེས་པར་ཞུགས་པར་རིག་པར་བྱ ('should be known to have definitely entered'). The English adds 'noble one' and drops the sense of certainty.
i.fx: That one should be known to have definitely entered omniscience.

atts.t:
When this perfection of wisdom, the Mother of the Tathāgatas,
Is taught, whichever bodhisattva aspires to it,
And exerts themselves in accomplishing it with sincere intent,
That one should be known to have definitely entered omniscience.

judge.reason: B correctly translates "des pa" as "noble one" (sūrata), whereas A translates it as "definitely" (likely confusing it with "nges pa").

atts.t:
They do not dwell in the dharmadhātu or suchness,
But, for example, like a cloud in space, they dwell without dwelling.
A mantra-holder, traveling in space without a dwelling, wishing to dwell,
Through the power of mantra, brings forth out-of-season flowers and bestows a blessing.

i.sp: bestows a blessing
i.ev: བྱིན་གྱིས་རློབ in this context (bo-mipham 5-53, bo-khenrab 5-53: ཚལ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཇི་ལྟར་འདོད་པར་བྱིན་གྱིས་རློབ་ཅིང་སྣང་བར་བྱེད་) means empowering/transforming the place so it appears as wished (Sanskrit adhiṣṭhāna, 'mantra-bala-adhiṣṭhāna'), not bestowing a blessing on someone; the object is also left out.
i.fx: and empowers the place as he wishes

atts.t:
They do not dwell in the dharmadhātu or suchness,
But, for example, like a cloud in space, they dwell without dwelling.
A mantra-holder, traveling in space without a dwelling, wishing to dwell,
Through the power of mantra, brings forth out-of-season flowers and empowers the place as they wish.

judge.reason: B more accurately conveys "byin gyis rlob" (adhiṣṭhāna) in this specific context as magical empowerment rather than a religious "blessing" as in A.

i.sp: those who desire peace
i.ev: ཞི་འདོད: bo-mipham 5-54 glosses it as གཞན་སེམས་ཅན་རྣམས་ཀྱི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཞི་བར་འདོད་པ, desiring the pacification of other beings' suffering, so 'peace' for oneself is not meant; the English allows a self-interested reading.
i.fx: those who desire the pacification of beings' suffering

i.sp: an expounder, one who desires the Dharma, or one who views
i.ev: "འཆད་པར་བྱེད་དང་ཆོས་འདོད་ལྟ་བར་བྱེད་མི་དམིགས": bo-mipham 5-54 and bo-khenrab 5-53 read two items, the expounder and the one who desires Dharma, who is regarded as the object of the teaching ("ཆོས་འདོད་མཁན་ཏེ་ཆོས་བཤད་པའི་ཡུལ་ཉིད་དུ་ལྟ་བར་བྱེད་པ"); the Sanskrit likewise has two (deśika, paśyaka). The English makes "one who views" a stand-alone third item with no object.
i.fx: an expounder, or one who desires the Dharma and views [it as the object of teaching]

judge.reason: B is more faithful to the root text "zhi 'dod" (desire peace), avoiding A's unnecessary interpolation of "pacification of beings' suffering" from the commentaries.

atts.t:
Except for the liberation of the arhats and the Tathāgatas,
This dwelling, among those of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas—
Their dwellings in peaceful samādhi, profoundly peaceful and endowed with bliss,
Is the supreme and unsurpassed of all however many there are.

i.sp: Their dwellings in peaceful samādhi, profoundly peaceful and endowed with bliss, Is the supreme
i.ev: The subject of 'is the supreme' (གནས་པ་འདི་ནི ... མཆོག་དང་གོང་ན་མེད་པ་ཡིན) is 'this dwelling' (the bodhisattva's, bo-mipham 5-55 བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་གནས་པ་འདི), but the English makes the plural 'Their dwellings' the grammatical subject of a singular verb after a dash, obscuring the structure.
i.fx: This dwelling is the supreme and unsurpassed among all the dwellings of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas in peaceful samādhi, profoundly peaceful and endowed with bliss, however many there are.

atts.t:
Except for the liberation of the arhats and the Tathāgatas,
This dwelling is the supreme and unsurpassed among all
The dwellings of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas in peaceful samādhi,
Profoundly peaceful and endowed with bliss, however many there are.

judge.reason: A offers a much smoother, clearer English syntax that correctly links the clauses, avoiding the awkward, disjointed phrasing found in B.

i.sp: do not suffocate and die
i.ev: འཚུབས་ཏེ་འཆི་བ་མེད means 'are not disturbed/agitated and die'; bo-mipham 5-55 and bo-khenrab 5-56 explain ཆུས་རྣ་བ་དང་སྣ་སོགས་འཚུབས་ ('the ears, nose etc. are disturbed by water'). 'Suffocate' is a narrower gloss not in the text.
i.fx: are not disturbed and killed

judge.reason: A accurately translates "'tshubs" as "suffocate," which perfectly fits the analogy of fish in water and is supported by the commentaries.

atts.t:
Whoever wishes to reach the supreme qualities of all sentient beings,
And touch the supreme, most marvelous primordial wisdom of a Buddha,
And give the most excellent, supreme, and holy gift of Dharma,
Should rely on this supreme dwelling of the benefactors.

i.sp: reach the supreme qualities of all sentient beings
i.ev: སེམས་ཅན་ཀུན་གྱི་ཡོན་ཏན་མཆོག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བ means to become supreme among all sentient beings' qualities (bo-mipham 5-57: ཡོན་ཏན་ཇི་ཡོད་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་ཀྱི་མཆོག་ཏུ་འགྲོ་བ་ཉིད་དུ་འདོད་པ; Sanskrit sarvasattvaguṇa-agratu gantukāmo). The English reads 'supreme' as modifying the qualities.
i.fx: reach the pinnacle of the qualities of all sentient beings

atts.t:
Whoever wishes to reach the pinnacle of the qualities of all sentient beings,
And touch the supreme, most marvelous primordial wisdom of a Buddha,
And give the most excellent, supreme, and holy gift of Dharma,
Should rely on this supreme dwelling of the benefactors.

judge.reason: A translates 'mchog tu 'gro ba' accurately as 'reach the pinnacle', capturing the abstract noun form found in the Sanskrit and Tibetan commentary.

atts.t:
However many gateways, skillful means, and roots of primordial wisdom there are,
All these arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom;
When conditions assemble, the machine of karma fully emerges,
Yet the perfection of wisdom has no exhaustion and no increase.

i.sp: gateways, skillful means, and roots of primordial wisdom
i.ev: The Tibetan lists five items: ཡེ་ཤེས, ཚུལ, སྒོ, ཐབས, རྩ་བ (bo-mipham 5-63: Buddha's wisdom; meditation path; seeing path; preparation path; accumulation path as root; bo-rangjung 5-62 similarly). The English makes 'of primordial wisdom' govern all three nouns and loses 'primordial wisdom' as the first item.
i.fx: However many primordial wisdoms, approaches, gateways, skillful means, and roots there are

atts.t:
However many primordial wisdoms, approaches, gateways, skillful means, and roots there are,
All these arise from the supreme perfection of wisdom;
When conditions assemble, the machine of karma fully emerges,
Yet the perfection of wisdom has no exhaustion and no increase.

judge.reason: A aligns with Mipham's commentary, which parses the items as a list of distinct factors rather than as genitive modifiers of 'primordial wisdom'.

atts.t:
Any bodhisattva who, regarding dependent origination,
Knows this wisdom to be unborn and unexhausted,
Just as a cloudless sun dispels darkness by radiating light,
Will destroy dense ignorance and attain the self-arisen state.

i.sp: Knows this wisdom to be unborn and unexhausted
i.ev: What is unborn and inexhaustible is dependent origination (རྟེན་ཅིང་འབྲེལ་འབྱུང་), which the wisdom knows: bo-mipham 5-64 རྟེན་ཅིང་འབྲེལ་བར་འབྱུང་བའི་ཆོས་འདི་ལ ... སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པ་དང་ཟད་པ་མེད་པར ... ཤེས་རབ ... ཤེས་པར་བྱས་ཏེ; bo-rangjung 5-62 ངོ་བོ་རྟེན་ཅིང་འབྲེལ་བར་འབྱུང་བ་ལ། རང་བཞིན་སྐྱེ་བ་མེད་པ་དང་ཟད་ཅིང་འགག་པ་མེད་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་འདི་ཤེས. The English makes the wisdom itself the thing known as unborn.
i.fx: Knows dependent origination to be unborn and unexhausted, through this wisdom

i.sp: Just as a cloudless sun dispels darkness by radiating light, Will destroy dense ignorance
i.ev: The simile (ལྟར) is left without a connected main clause; the English line 'Just as ... Will destroy' is a fragment relative to the preceding lines.
i.fx: Just as a cloudless sun dispels darkness by radiating light, so such a one destroys dense ignorance and attains the self-arisen.

atts.t:
Any bodhisattva who, regarding dependent origination,
Knows it to be unborn and unexhausted through this wisdom,
Just as a cloudless sun dispels darkness by radiating light,
Will destroy dense ignorance and attain the self-arisen state.

i.sp: Knows it to be unborn and unexhausted through this wisdom
i.ev: "སྐྱེ་མེད་ཟད་པ་མེད་པར་ཤེས་རབ་འདི་ཤེས་ཏེ": "ཤེས་རབ་འདི" is the object known, not the instrument; bo-mipham 5-64 "ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་དོན་ཟབ་མོ་འདི་ལྟ་བུ་ཤེས་པར་བྱས" (knowing this profound meaning of the perfection of wisdom), with unborn and inexhaustible predicated of dependent origination. The English "through this wisdom" turns the object into a means.
i.fx: Knows dependent origination to be unborn and inexhaustible, and knows this wisdom,

judge.reason: B correctly identifies 'dependent origination' as the object that is known to be unborn and unexhausted, avoiding doctrinal error.

atts.t:
This is a wondrous marvel of those who accumulate qualities:
Abiding in meditative concentration and samādhi, they are signless;
If the bodies of those who abide in them should perish,
They are reborn in the desire realm exactly according to their intentions.

i.sp: they are signless
i.ev: མཚན་མ་མེད means no signs are apprehended in that samādhi: bo-mipham 5-67 ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱིས་དེ་ལ་མཚན་མ་མེད་པར་རྟོགས་སོ, bo-rangjung 5-67 མཚན་མར་འཛིན་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་རོ་མྱང་བ་མེད. The English predicates 'signless' of the persons.
i.fx: they are without signs (they do not apprehend signs)

atts.t:
This is a wondrous marvel of those who accumulate qualities:
Abiding in meditative concentration and samādhi, they realise them as signless;
If the bodies of those who abide in them should perish,
They are reborn in the desire realm exactly according to their intentions.

judge.reason: A's addition of 'realise them as' reflects the commentary ('rtogs so'), avoiding B's awkward implication that the meditators themselves are signless.

atts.t:
For example, it is like a person of Jambudvīpa who had never before
Visited the supreme city of the gods in the realm of the gods, but later goes there;
Having seen those fully possessed objects,
They do not become attached when they return here.

i.sp: those fully possessed objects
i.ev: ཡོངས་སུ་བཟུང་བའི་ཡུལ་ refers to the pleasing places (mansions, gardens) held by the gods: bo-mipham 5-68 ལྷ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་ཡོངས་སུ་བཟུང་བའི་ཁང་བཟང་དང་སྐྱེད་མོས་ཚལ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཡུལ་ཡིད་དུ་འོང་བ. 'Fully possessed objects' is opaque and omits the gods as holders; the singular 'person' is also followed by plural 'They'.
i.fx: those realms held by the gods; (and) he does not become attached when he returns here

atts.t:
For example, it is like a person of Jambudvīpa who had never before
Visited the supreme city of the gods in the realm of the gods, but later goes there;
Having seen those realms held by the gods,
He does not become attached when he returns here.

judge.reason: A's 'realms held by the gods' is much clearer and better supported by Mipham's gloss than B's literal but obscure 'fully possessed objects'.

atts.t:
Likewise, the wise bodhisattva, having attained the four peaceful
Samādhis of meditative concentration that bestow joy and bliss,
Relinquishes the attainment of the samādhis of meditative concentration endowed with the bliss of meditative concentration,
And endowed with compassion for beings, enters again into the desire realm.

i.sp:
the four peaceful
Samādhis of meditative concentration that bestow joy and bliss
i.ev: The Tibetan has དགའ་བ་དང་། བདེ་སྦྱིན་ as a predicate of the wise bodhisattvas (བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མཁས་པ་), not a relative clause on the samādhis. All three commentaries read the bodhisattvas as the ones who give joy and bliss: bo-mipham 5-72 བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་མཁས་པ་སེམས་ཅན་རྣམས་ལ་འཕྲལ་དུ་དགའ་བ་དང་ནམ་ཕུག་གི་བདེ་བ་སྦྱིན་པར་བྱེད་པ་དེ་དག་; bo-rangjung 5-71 གཞན་ལ་བདེ་བ་སྦྱིན་པ་; bo-khenrab 5-71 སེམས་ཅན་རྣམས་ལ་གནས་སྐབས་སུ་དགའ་བ་དང་ནམ་ཕུག་གི་བདེ་བ་སྦྱིན་པར་བྱེད་པ་. The English makes the samādhis the givers of joy and bliss (following the Sanskrit prīti-sukhadāṃ), so the bodhisattvas' giving of joy and bliss to beings is lost.
i.fx: Likewise, wise bodhisattvas, who bestow joy and bliss, having attained the four peaceful samādhis of meditative concentration,

atts.t:
Likewise, wise bodhisattvas who bestow joy and
Bliss, having attained the four peaceful samādhis of meditative concentration,
Relinquish the attainment of the samādhis of meditative concentration endowed with the bliss of meditative concentration,
And endowed with compassion for beings, enter again into the desire realm.

judge.reason: A follows the Tibetan commentaries (like Mipham), which attribute 'bestowing joy and bliss' to the bodhisattvas rather than to the samādhis.

atts.t:
If a bodhisattva abides in samādhi and meditative concentration,
But generates a mind desiring the vehicle of an arhat or pratyekabuddha,
They are not in meditative equipoise, but become agitated and have a distracted mind;
And the qualities of a Buddha completely decline, like a boatman whose boat is wrecked.

i.sp: They are not in meditative equipoise, but become agitated and have a distracted mind
i.ev: The Tibetan མཉམ་པར་མ་བཞག་རྒོད་ཅིང་སེམས་གཡེངས་གྱུར་པ་སྟེ lists three parallel faults (not in equipoise, agitated, mind distracted), as bo-mipham 5-73 མཉམ་པར་མ་བཞག་པ་དང་། རྒོད་ཅིང་སེམས་གཡེངས་པར་གྱུར་པ་ shows. The English 'but' wrongly sets agitation in contrast to not being in equipoise.
i.fx: They are not in meditative equipoise; they become agitated and have a distracted mind;

atts.t:
If a bodhisattva abides in samādhi and meditative concentration,
But generates a mind desiring the vehicle of an arhat or pratyekabuddha,
They are not in meditative equipoise; they become agitated and have a distracted mind;
And the qualities of a Buddha completely decline, like a boatman whose boat is wrecked.

judge.reason: The versions are nearly identical. A's 'but' and B's semicolon both effectively convey the syntactic relationship of the clauses.

atts.t:
Moreover, form and sound, and likewise smell and taste,
Touch, and the five qualities of desire—even if they intensely engage in them,
If they are free from the vehicle of the arhat and pratyekabuddha and delight in the mind of awakening,
The hero should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise.

i.sp: Touch, and the five qualities of desire
i.ev: Tibetan རེག་དང་འདོད་ཡོན་ལྔ་ presents the five (form, sound, smell, taste, touch) as the five qualities of desire. bo-mipham 5-74 རེག་བྱ་དང་བཅས་པ་སྟེ་འདོད་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་ལྔ་ and bo-khenrab 5-74 ... རེག་བྱ ... སོགས་འདོད་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་ལྔ་. The English 'and' lets the reader take the five qualities of desire as a further group beyond the five listed objects.
i.fx: Touch—the five qualities of desire—

atts.t:
Moreover, form and sound, and likewise smell and taste,
Touch—the five qualities of desire—even if they intensely engage in them,
If they are free from the vehicle of the arhat and pratyekabuddha and delight in the mind of awakening,
The hero should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise.

i.sp: free from the vehicle of the arhat and pratyekabuddha
i.ev: The Tibetan དགྲ་བཅོམ་རང་རྒྱལ་ཐེག་བྲལ་ is glossed in bo-mipham 5-74 as ཐེག་པ་འདོད་པ་དང་བྲལ་ (free from the wish for the vehicle of arhats and pratyekabuddhas) and in bo-khenrab 5-74 as འདོད་པ་དང་དོན་གཉེར་གྱི་བློ་དང་བྲལ་; the English could be read as simply not belonging to that vehicle.
i.fx: free from [the wish for] the vehicle of the arhat and pratyekabuddha

i.sp: even if they intensely engage in them, If they are free
i.ev: Lines 2-3 use 'they' with no antecedent; the subject །དཔའ་བོ་ (hero) only appears in line 4, so the conditional clauses are hard to parse.
i.fx: Even if the hero intensely engages in them, if he is free ... and delights ..., he should be known to be constantly in meditative equipoise

judge.reason: A correctly uses an em-dash to show that form, sound, smell, taste, and touch are the five qualities of desire, whereas B's 'and' makes them seem separate.

atts.t:
Whether she is scolded or even constantly beaten,
The servant woman does not speak a word in reply to her master;
Thinking, "He will even kill me,"
With an extremely terrified mind, she is overcome with fear.

i.sp: Thinking, "He will even kill me,"
i.ev: Tibetan འདི་ཡིས་བདག་ནི་བསད་པར་འགྱུར་དུ་འོང་སྙམ་ནས is a possibility ('by this he may come to kill me'), not a certainty, and it includes འདི་ཡིས ('by this'). bo-mipham 5-76 ཉེས་ན་འདི༷་ཡི༷ས་བདག༷་ནི༷་བསད༷་པར༷་འགྱུར༷་དུའང༷་འོང༷་ and bo-khenrab 5-76 སྟབས་ཉེས་ན་ ('if she errs') confirm the conditional sense. The English states it as a definite future and omits 'by this'.
i.fx: Thinking, "By this he might even kill me,"

i.sp: she is overcome with fear
i.ev: Tibetan འཇིགས་བཅས་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན is 'with fear, she is overpowered'. bo-mipham 5-76 བཀའ་ཉན་ལ་དེ་ཉིད་རྗེ་བོ་དེའི་ཟིལ༷་གྱིས༷་གནོན༷་པར་གྱུར་པ་ and bo-khenrab 5-76 རྗེ་བོ་དེས་ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན་པར་གྱུར་བ་ show that ཟིལ་གྱིས་གནོན is her being dominated by the master, which links to 'under the power of her master' in 5-75. The English reduces it to being afraid.
i.fx: fearful, she is utterly subdued by him.

atts.t:
Whether she is scolded or even constantly beaten,
The servant woman does not speak a word in reply to her master;
Thinking, "By this he might even kill me,"
Fearful, she is utterly subdued by him.

judge.reason: B accurately translates 'śin tu skrag pa'i yid kyis' as 'with an extremely terrified mind', whereas A drops 'yid' (mind).

i.sp: those who have entered into supreme awakening for the sake of awakening
i.ev: Tibetan བྱང་ཆུབ་ཆེད་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་མཆོག་ཞུགས་པ ('entered/set out on the supreme [path of] awakening for the sake of awakening'). bo-mipham 5-77 བླ་ན་མེད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་ཆེད་དུ་བྱང་ཆུབ་མཆོག་གི་ལམ་ལ་ཞུགས་པ་ and Sanskrit bodhivarapasthitu show that what is entered is the path to supreme awakening; those described have not yet attained it. 'entered into supreme awakening' suggests being in awakening itself.
i.fx: those who have set out on the path to supreme awakening for the sake of awakening

i.sp: burns them up
i.ev: Tibetan རྩྭ་དང་ཤིང་ལས་མེ་བྱུང་བས་ནི་དེ་ཉིད་སྲེག says fire born of grass and wood burns that very grass and wood. bo-mipham 5-77 རྩ་དང་ཤིང་ལས་མེ་བྱུང་བས་ནི་རྩ་ཤིང་དེ༷་ཉི༷ད་སྲེག་པ. The English 'them' has no clear antecedent and loses 'that very' (self-destruction by one's own fire).
i.fx: Fire arising from grass and wood burns that very grass and wood.

judge.reason: Both versions convey the meaning well. A is more concise, while B incorporates commentary glosses, making both academically acceptable.

i.sp: If they perceive them as long, they accomplish awakening with suffering
i.ev: Tibetan རིང་བར་འདུ་ཤེས་སྡུག་བསྔལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སྒྲུབ: both 'long' and 'suffering' are perceptions (འདུ་ཤེས). bo-mipham 5-80 རིང༷་བར༷་འདུ༷་ཤེས༷་པ་དང་། ... སྡུག༷་བསྔལ༷་བའི་འདུ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ནས་བྱང༷་ཆུབ༷་སྒྲུབ༷་པར་བྱེད་ན། and bo-khenrab 5-80 སྡུག་བསྔལ་བའི་འདུ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ནས་བྱང་ཆུབ་སྒྲུབ་པར་བྱེད་ན. The English renders suffering as an actual circumstance of accomplishing rather than a perception.
i.fx: If they perceive it as long and perceive it as suffering, and so accomplish awakening,

judge.reason: A better reflects the commentary's explanation of the dual perception (perceiving the time as long, perceiving the difficult deeds as suffering).

atts.t:
Whatever bodhisattva possesses the excellent dharma of patience—
Whoever fills the three thousandfold world system with jewels and offers them to the Knowers of the World,
The Buddhas, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas,
That mass of generosity cannot match a fraction of their merit.

i.sp:
offers them to the Knowers of the World,
The Buddhas, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas
i.ev: Tibetan འཇིག་རྟེན་མཁྱེན། སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་དང་དགྲ་བཅོམ་རང་རྒྱལ is 'the Knowers of the World, i.e. the Buddhas, and arhats and pratyekabuddhas'; འཇིག་རྟེན་མཁྱེན་པ is an epithet of the Buddhas only. bo-mipham 5-87 འཇིག༷་རྟེན༷་མཁྱེན༷་པ་སངས༷་རྒྱས༷་རྣམ༷ས་དང༷་། དགྲ༷་བཅོ༷མ་པ་རྣམས་དང་རང༷་རྒྱལ༷་རྣམས་ལ and bo-rangjung 5-87 འཇིག་རྟེན་མཁྱེན་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་དང་ཉན་ཐོས་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་དང་རང་རྒྱལ་རྣམས་. The English line break makes 'Knowers of the World' read as a heading for all three groups.
i.fx: offers them to the Buddhas, the Knowers of the World, and to arhats and pratyekabuddhas,

atts.t:
Whatever bodhisattva possesses the excellent dharma of patience—
Whoever fills the three thousandfold world system with jewels and offers them to the Buddhas, the Knowers of the World,
And to arhats and pratyekabuddhas,
That mass of generosity cannot match a fraction of their merit.

judge.reason: A correctly treats 'Knowers of the World' as an epithet in apposition to 'Buddhas', matching the Sanskrit and Tibetan syntax.

i.sp: Wandering beings will rejoice in this wise one endowed with patience.
i.ev: Tibetan འདི་ནི་བཟོད་ལྡན་དེ་ལ་འགྲོ་བ་དགའ་འགྱུར་མཁས: 'wise' (མཁས) is a separate result (མཁས་པར་འགྱུར) alongside beings' delight. bo-mipham 5-88 ... དེ༷་ལ༷་འགྲོ༷་བ༷་རྣམས་དགའ༷་བར་འགྱུར༷་ཞིང་ ... རྨོངས་པ་དང་བྲལ་བའི་མཁས༷་པར་འགྱུར་རོ and bo-khenrab 5-88 ... བླང་དོར་གྱི་གནས་ལ་མཁས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ. The English reduces 'becomes wise' to an epithet of the patient one.
i.fx: Beings will rejoice in this one endowed with patience, and they will become wise.

i.sp: and they will become wise
i.ev: In འགྲོ་བ་དགའ་འགྱུར་མཁས the 'wise' (མཁས) describes the patient one, not the beings. bo-mipham 5-88: བཟོད་པ་དང་ལྡན་པ་དེ་ལ་འགྲོ་བ་རྣམས་དགའ་བར་འགྱུར་... རྨོངས་པ་དང་བྲལ་བའི་མཁས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ (the patient one becomes wise, free of ignorance); bo-khenrab 5-88 likewise; bo-rangjung 5-87: འགྲོ་བ་དད་ཅིང་དགའ་བར་འགྱུར་བ་དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཉིད་ཤེས་པས་མཁས་པ་ཡིན་ནོ. Sanskrit: priyu bhoti sarvajagati kṣamamāṇu vijño (dear to all the world, the patient one, wise).
i.fx: Beings will rejoice in this one endowed with patience, who is wise.

atts.t:
If some sentient beings take a packet of sandalwood,
And with great respect rub it on the bodhisattva,
While another scatters burning coals on their head—towards both
They should generate an equal and even mind.

i.sp: They should generate an equal and even mind.
i.ev: Tibetan དེ་ཡིས་མཉམ་ཞིང་སྙོམས་པའི་ཡིད་ནི་བསྐྱེད་པར་བྱ: the agent is the bodhisattva. bo-mipham 5-89 བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ༷་ཡིས༷་ ... མཉམ༷་ཞིང༷་སྙོམས༷་པའི༷་ཡི༷ད་ནི༷་བསྐྱེ༷ད་པར༷་བྱའོ and bo-khenrab 5-89 བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་དེ་ཡིས་ .... In the English, 'some sentient beings', 'another' and the bodhisattva are all possible antecedents of 'They'.
i.fx: That bodhisattva should generate an equal and even mind.

atts.t:
If some sentient beings take a packet of sandalwood,
And with great respect rub it on the bodhisattva,
While another scatters burning coals on their head—towards both
That bodhisattva should generate an equal and even mind.

judge.reason: B uses 'That bodhisattva' to clearly disambiguate the subject of the final line, avoiding the potentially confusing pronoun 'they' used in A.

atts.t:
Having practiced patience in that way, the wise bodhisattva,
If they dedicate that generation of the mind to supreme awakening,
That hero, through patience towards the entire world, outshines the arhats,
The pratyekabuddhas, and however many diverse realms of sentient beings there are.

i.sp: however many diverse realms of sentient beings there are
i.ev: Tibetan སེམས་ཅན་ཁམས་མང་ཇི་སྙེད (locked 'realm of sentient beings') says 'however many [there are in] the realm of sentient beings'. bo-mipham 5-90 གཞན་སེམས༷་ཅ༷ན་གྱི་ཁ༷མས་མང༷་པོ་ཇི༷་སྙེད༷་པ and bo-rangjung 5-90 སེམས་ཅན་ཁམས་ཀྱི་དགེ་བ་ཇི་སྙེད་ཡོད་པ. Nothing corresponds to 'diverse', and the locked singular rendering 'realm of sentient beings' is not used.
i.fx: and however many there are in the realm of sentient beings.

atts.t:
Having practiced patience in that way, the wise bodhisattva,
If they dedicate that generation of the mind to supreme awakening,
That hero, through patience towards the entire world, outshines the arhats,
The pratyekabuddhas, and however many there are in the realm of sentient beings.

judge.reason: A is more faithful by avoiding the insertion of 'diverse' which is not present in the Tibetan source.

atts.t:
Whatever phenomena cause the qualities of certain awakening to arise,
This is the purpose of ethical discipline for those endowed with the phenomena of quality.
Whatever phenomena cause the awakening of benefactors to completely degenerate,
The Guide has stated that this is lacking ethical discipline.

i.sp: the qualities of certain awakening
i.ev: ངེས་པ in 'ཆོས་གང་ངེས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཡོན་ཏན་འབྱུང་འགྱུར་བ' is explained by bo-mipham 5-95 as certainty (the dharma that definitely brings about the qualities of supreme awakening: 'ཐོབ་བྱ་བྱང་ཆུབ་མཆོག་གི་ཡོན་ཏན་འབྱུང་བར་འགྱུར་བ'); 'certain awakening' reads as a kind of awakening rather than the certainty of the causal result.
i.fx: Whatever phenomena certainly cause the qualities of awakening to arise

i.sp: the awakening of benefactors
i.ev: 'ཕན་བྱེད' means those who benefit (others): bo-mipham 5-95 'ཕན་བྱེད་བྱང་སེམས་རྣམས'; bo-rangjung 5-95 'གཞན་ལ་ཕན་པར་བྱེད་པ་རྣམས'; Sanskrit hitaṃkarāṇām. 'Benefactors' suggests donors/patrons.
i.fx: the awakening of those who benefit others

atts.t:
Whatever phenomena certainly cause the qualities of awakening to arise,
This is the purpose of ethical discipline for those endowed with the phenomena of quality.
Whatever phenomena cause the awakening of those who benefit others to completely degenerate,
The Guide has stated that this is lacking ethical discipline.

i.sp: This is the purpose of ethical discipline
i.ev: Tibetan ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་དོན; bo-mipham 5-95 and bo-khenrab 5-95 read ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་ཀྱི་དོན་དུ་གསུངས / ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་ཀྱི་དོན་ཡིན་པར་གསུངས (this is taught as the meaning of ethical discipline), cf. Sanskrit śīlaartha; 'purpose' shifts the sense to a goal.
i.fx: This is the meaning of ethical discipline for those endowed with ...

judge.reason: B's 'those who benefit others' is a much better translation of 'phan byed rnams' in this context than A's 'benefactors'.

atts.t:
Even if a bodhisattva enjoys the sensory pleasure of the five qualities of desire,
If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha,
And direct their mind toward omniscience, thinking, "I will accomplish the state of a Buddha,"
The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.

i.sp: The wise should understand that they abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.
i.ev: In 'མཁས་པ་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་གནས་རིག་པར་བྱ' the wise one (མཁས་པ) is the bodhisattva who abides, and is the one to be recognised as abiding. bo-mipham 5-96: 'དོན་ལ་མཁས་པ་དེ་ནི་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་གནས་པར་རིགས་པར་བྱའོ'; bo-rangjung 5-96: 'མཁས་པ་ངེས་དོན་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་ལ་གནས་པར་རིག་པར་བྱ'; Sanskrit 'sthitu śīlapāramita vedayitavya vijñaḥ' (nominative, gerundive). The English makes 'the wise' the knowers of a bodhisattva, changing who is wise and who abides.
i.fx: that wise one should be understood as abiding in the perfection of ethical discipline (the skilled bodhisattva is to be recognised as abiding in the perfection of ethical discipline)

atts.t:
Even if a bodhisattva indulges in the five qualities of desire, enjoying sensory pleasure,
If they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the noble Sangha,
And direct their mind to omniscience, thinking, "I must become a Buddha,"
One should understand that this wise one abides in the perfection of ethical discipline.

i.sp: enjoying sensory pleasure
i.ev: The Tibetan says only འདོད་ཡོན་ལྔ་སྤྱོད་ཀྱང་ (practises/enjoys the five qualities of desire); 'sensory pleasure' is not a separate item and merely restates the object (bo-mipham 5-96: འདོད་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་ལྔ་ལ་ཞེན་པའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་སྤྱོད་པར་གྱུར་ཀྱང་).
i.fx: delete 'enjoying sensory pleasure'

i.sp: I must become a Buddha
i.ev: སངས་རྒྱས་འགྲུབ་བྱ་སྙམ་ is a resolve 'I shall accomplish buddhahood' (bo-mipham 5-96 and bo-khenrab 5-95: བདག་གིས་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་གོ་འཕང་འགྲུབ་པར་བྱའོ་སྙམ་; Sanskrit buddho bhaviṣyāmi), not an obligation.
i.fx: "I shall accomplish buddhahood"

judge.reason: A correctly identifies 'the wise one' (mkhas pa) as the bodhisattva who abides in discipline, following the commentary, whereas B makes 'the wise' the subject.

atts.t:
Guarding ethical discipline and dedicating it to supreme awakening,
Being without conceit because of it and not praising oneself,
And completely abandoning the perception of a self and the perception of sentient beings—
Such a bodhisattva is said to abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.

i.sp: Being without conceit because of it
i.ev: 'དེ་ཡིས་རློམ་སེམས་མེད' means no conceit about / on account of the ethical discipline, not that discipline causes absence of conceit: bo-mipham 5-98 'ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་དེ་ལ་མཚན་མར་བཟུང་བ་ཡིས་རློམ་སེམས་སུ་གྱུར་པ་མེད'; bo-khenrab 5-98 'ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་དེ་ལ་བདེན་པར་ཞེན་པ་ཡིས་རློམ་སེམས་སུ་གྱུར་བ་མེད'; Sanskrit 'na ca tena manyati'.
i.fx: Not becoming conceited on account of it, and not praising oneself

atts.t:
Guarding ethical discipline and dedicating it to supreme awakening,
Having no conceit on account of it, and not praising oneself,
And completely abandoning the perception of a self and the perception of sentient beings—
Such a bodhisattva is said to abide in the perfection of ethical discipline.

judge.reason: Both translations accurately and clearly render the Tibetan meaning with only slight, inconsequential stylistic variations.

atts.t:
Any pure sentient being who thus possesses ethical discipline
Has no view regarding anything pleasant or unpleasant;
Giving away their head, hands, and feet, they do not even have a discouraged mind,
And giving away all their possessions, they are always free from attachment.

i.sp: Has no view regarding anything pleasant or unpleasant
i.ev: 'ལྟ་བ་མེད' is explained as not regarding things as fixed signs / with attachment-aversion: bo-mipham 5-101 'དེ་དང་དེར་མཚན་མར་ལྟ་བ་མེད'; bo-rangjung 5-101 'ཆགས་སྡང་དུ་བལྟ་བ་མེད'; Sanskrit 'anapekṣaka' (without regard). 'Has no view' reads as a doctrinal view (dṛṣṭi).
i.fx: Has no fixating regard for anything pleasant or unpleasant

atts.t:
Any pure sentient being who thus possesses ethical discipline
Has no fixating regard for anything pleasant or unpleasant;
Giving away their head, hands, and feet, they do not even have a discouraged mind,
And giving away all their possessions, they are always free from attachment.

judge.reason: B's 'fixating regard' better captures the commentary's 'mtshan mar mngon par zhen pa'i lta ba' (fixating view) than the bare literal 'view'.

atts.t:
However many sentient beings there are without exception in the three states of existence,
Taking them fully into consideration, if all of them
To the Knowers of the World, the Buddhas, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas,
Give gifts for infinite eons and properly seek to be a śrāvaka—

i.sp: Taking them fully into consideration
i.ev: 'ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་པ་བཟུང་སྟེ' is glossed as taking the limit/extent of what can be reckoned or imagined: bo-mipham 5-107 'ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་པ་མཐའ་བཟུང་གི་དཔེར་བྱས་ཏེ'; bo-rangjung 5-106 'ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་པའི་མཐའ་བཟུང་སྟེ'. It marks the maximal hypothetical case, not 'taking them into consideration'.
i.fx: Taking them as the utmost extent of what can be conceived

atts.t:
However many sentient beings there are without exception in the three states of existence,
Taking them as the utmost extent of what can be conceived, if all of them
To the Knowers of the World, the Buddhas, arhats, and pratyekabuddhas,
Give gifts for infinite eons and properly seek to be a śrāvaka—

i.sp: properly seek to be a śrāvaka
i.ev: ཉན་ཐོས་ལེགས་ཚོལ་ is glossed in bo-mipham 5-107 as དེའི་འབྲས་བུ་ཉན་ཐོས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ལེགས་པར་ཚོལ་བ (earnestly seek the śrāvaka awakening as the result of the gifts) and in bo-rangjung 5-106 as འབྲས་བུ་ཉན་ཐོས་ཚོལ་ན; Sanskrit śrāvakaguṇān; the object sought is the śrāvaka's fruit, not simply being a śrāvaka.
i.fx: earnestly seek the awakening of a śrāvaka as the result

judge.reason: B accurately reflects the commentary's explanation of 'yongs su brtag pa bzung ste' as 'taking them as the utmost extent' (mtha' gzung gi dper byas).

atts.t:
If any wise bodhisattva, skilled in means,
Rejoices in their basis of meritorious action
And dedicates it to supreme awakening for the sake of sentient beings,
By dedicating it, they outshine all beings.

i.sp: Rejoices in their basis of meritorious action
i.ev: 'དེ་དག་བསོད་ནམས་བྱ་བའི་དངོས་ལ་ཡི་རང' refers to the meritorious bases of those beings of the preceding verse (bo-rangjung 5-108 'འཁོར་འདས་དེ་དག་གི་བསོད་ནམས་བྱ་བའི་དངོས་པོ་ལ་ཡིད་རང་ནས'; bo-mipham 5-107 'བཤད་མ་ཐག་པ་དེ་དག་གི་བསོད་ནམས་བྱ་བའི་དངོས་པོ་དེ་ལ་ཡི་རང'). After 'any bodhisattva', 'their' reads as the bodhisattva's own.
i.fx: Rejoices in the bases of meritorious action of those beings

atts.t:
Any wise bodhisattva, skilled in means,
Who rejoices in their basis of meritorious action
And dedicates it to supreme awakening for the sake of sentient beings,
By dedicating it, outshines all beings.

i.sp: Who rejoices in their basis of meritorious action
i.ev: དེ་དག་བསོད་ནམས་བྱ་བའི་དངོས་ལ་ཡི་རང་ནས: དེ་དག (those) refers back to the beings giving gifts in 5-107, not to the bodhisattva. bo-mipham 5-107: བཤད་མ་ཐག་པ་དེ་དག་གི་བསོད་ནམས་བྱ་བའི་དངོས་པོ་དེ་ལ་ཡི་རང་བར་བྱས་ནས; bo-rangjung 5-108: འཁོར་འདས་དེ་དག་གི་བསོད་ནམས་བྱ་བའི་དངོས་པོ་ལ་ཡིད་རང་ནས; Sanskrit teṣāṃ puṇyakriyāvastu. In the English 'their' can only be read as the bodhisattva's own basis, reversing whose merit is rejoiced in.
i.fx: Who rejoices in those [beings'] bases of meritorious action

atts.t:
Even a great heap of imitation glass jewels
Is completely outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli;
Likewise, all the vast aggregates of generosity of all beings
Are outshone by the rejoicing bodhisattva.

i.sp: imitation glass jewels
i.ev: 'ནོར་བུ་མཆིང་བུ' corresponds to Sanskrit 'kācasya maṇi' (glass jewel); 'imitation' is not in the Tibetan or Sanskrit, and 'glass' and 'imitation' double up.
i.fx: a great heap of glass jewels

atts.t:
Even a great heap of glass jewels
Is completely outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli;
Likewise, all the vast aggregates of generosity of all beings
Are outshone by the rejoicing bodhisattva.

judge.reason: Both versions correctly convey the meaning. B's 'imitation glass jewels' is a bit redundant but acceptable; A is slightly cleaner. Both are good.

atts.t:
If a bodhisattva, having given gifts to beings,
Does not claim it as "mine" and is unsparing of the entity,
From that, their root of virtue will increase with great power,
Like the radiant, cloudless moon disk during the waxing fortnight.

i.sp: Does not claim it as "mine"
i.ev: All three commentaries take what is not claimed as 'mine' to be the merit/result of the giving, while the object is dealt with separately by 'ཕངས་མེད': bo-mipham 5-110 'སྦྱིན་པའི་བསོད་ནམས་དེ་ལ་བདག་གིར་མི་བྱེད'; bo-rangjung 5-110 'སྦྱིན་པ་བྱིན་པའི་བསོད་ནམས་དེ་ལས་བདག་གིར་མི་བྱེད'; bo-khenrab 5-110 'སྦྱིན་པའི་འབྲས་བུ་དེ་ལ་བདག་གིར་མི་བྱེད'. 'It' after 'gifts' reads as the gift itself.
i.fx: Does not claim the merit of it as "mine" and is unsparing of the entity

atts.t:
If a bodhisattva, having given gifts to beings,
Does not claim the merit of it as "mine" and is unsparing of the entity,
From that, their root of virtue will increase with great power,
Like the radiant, cloudless moon disk during the waxing fortnight.

judge.reason: A's explicit addition of 'the merit of it' clarifies the referent of 'de la' exactly as specified by the commentaries.

i.sp: Chapter Six
i.ev: Tibetan 'སྐབས་དྲུག་པ' is 'sixth topic/occasion' (སྐབས), the heading of the sixth of the eight-fold sequence; the commentaries count in སྐབས (bo-rangjung 5-110 'སྐབས་བདུན་པ... བརྒྱད་པ'), not ལེའུ (chapter) which they use for chapter numbers (bo-khenrab 5-110 'ལེའུ'). 'Chapter Six' conflates the two numbering schemes.
i.fx: Sixth topic: teaching the gradual path

judge.reason: A is correct because 'skabs' here refers to the 'Sixth topic' (the gradual path) of the Abhisamayālaṃkāra, not the sixth chapter of the text.

atts.t:
Chapter seven: teaching complete awakening in a single instant.
Having completely perfected these phenomena, that bodhisattva

Chapter Seven: Showing complete awakening in a single instant.

Having fully perfected these qualities, that bodhisattva

Chapter eight: teaching the Dharmakāya.
Fully upholds a perfectly pure field and pure sentient beings,
Fully upholds the Buddha lineage and also the Dharma lineage,
Likewise, fully upholds the lineage of the Sangha and all phenomena.

勝者的聲聞眾無論宣示多少佛法，
進行講解以及具備正理的陳述，
產生殊勝聖者的安樂並證得其果，
這些全都是如來士夫的神力。

i.sp: 產生殊勝聖者的安樂
i.ev: Tibetan 'མཆོག་འཕགས་བདེ་བ་བྱེད' = producing bliss that is itself supreme/exalted; bo-mipham 1-2 glosses 'མཆོག་ཏུ་འཕགས་པའི་བདེ་བ་མི་གནས་པའི་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ' (supremely exalted bliss = non-abiding nirvana), and bo-khenrab 1-2 'སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བདེ་བ'. The Chinese 殊勝聖者的安樂 parses as 'bliss of supreme noble persons', adding a possessor the Tibetan lacks.
i.fx: 產生至高殊勝的安樂

atts.t:
勝者的聲聞眾無論宣示多少佛法，
進行講解以及具備正理的陳述，
產生至高殊勝的安樂並證得其果，
這些全都是如來士夫的神力。

judge.reason: A correctly retains the translation of "འཕགས་" (noble) as "聖者", which B unjustifiably omits from the third line.

atts.t:
具足善知識且具足勝觀者，
聽聞勝者之母將不會心生恐懼，
任何人若具備惡友且仰賴他人，
就如同未燒透的瓦器觸水即毀壞。

i.sp: 將不會心生恐懼
i.ev: Tibetan 'སྐྲག་པར་ཡོང་མི་འགྱུར' uses the intensifier 'ཡོང' (never at all); bo-mipham 1-14 and bo-khenrab 1-14 gloss it 'ཡོངས་ཡེ་མི་འགྱུར' / 'ཡོང་ཡེ་མི་འགྱུར' (absolutely never). 將不會 renders only a plain future negative; english_academic has 'never'.
i.fx: 絕不會心生恐懼

i.sp: 未燒透的瓦器
i.ev: Tibetan 'སྣོད་སོ་མ་བཏང' = a vessel not fired at all (unfired); bo-khenrab 1-14 explains 'རྫ་མེར་མ་སྲེག་པ' (not burnt in the kiln). 未燒透 means 'not fired thoroughly', implying partial firing.
i.fx: 未經燒製的瓦器

atts.t:
具足善知識且具足勝觀者，
聽聞勝者之母絕不會心生恐懼，
任何人若具備惡友且仰賴他人，
就如同未經燒製的瓦器觸水即毀壞。

judge.reason: B accurately translates "ཡོང་མི་" as "絕不會" (never) and "སོ་མ་བཏང་" as "未經燒製" (unfired), improving both fidelity and precision.

atts.t:
常與無常，樂與苦，悅與不悅，
我與無我，真如與同樣的空性；
不住於得果與阿羅漢地，
不住於獨覺地與同樣的佛地。

i.ev: In the Tibetan the verb མི་གནས ('does not abide') in line 3 (ས་ལ་མི་གནས་ཤིང་) governs the whole list, including line 1 (རྟག་དང་མི་རྟག་བདེ་དང་སྡུག་བསྔལ་སྡུག་མི་སྡུག) and line 2 (བདག་དང་བདག་མེད་དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་དང་དེ་བཞིན་སྟོང་). Mipham 2-2 states that one does not abide (མི་གནས་པ) in any of these pairs (permanent/impermanent, happy/suffering, pleasant/unpleasant, self/selfless, suchness/emptiness). In the Chinese the first two lines are a bare list of nouns with no predicate, and 不住於 only appears in line 3, so the central assertion (non-abiding in these dualities) is missing for them.
i.fx:
不住於常與無常，樂與苦，悅與不悅，
不住於我與無我，真如與空性；
不住於得果與阿羅漢地，
不住於獨覺地，亦不住於佛地。

i.sp: 真如與同樣的空性；…不住於獨覺地與同樣的佛地
i.ev: དེ་བཞིན་ in དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་དང་དེ་བཞིན་སྟོང་ and རང་རྒྱལ་ས་དང་དེ་བཞིན་སངས་རྒྱས་སར་ is the adverbial 'likewise/also', not a modifier meaning 'the same'. Mipham 2-2 reads suchness and emptiness as two separate things not grasped at (དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་དུ་འཛིན་པ་དང་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་དུ་འཛིན་པ), and the Sanskrit has तथता तथ शून्यतायाम् / प्रत्येकभूमिस्थितो तथ बुद्धभूमौ. 同樣的空性 / 同樣的佛地 wrongly suggests 'the same emptiness / the same Buddha stage'.
i.fx: 真如與空性；…不住於獨覺地，亦不住於佛地

atts.t:
不住於常與無常，樂與苦，悅與不悅，
不住於我與無我，真如與空性；
不住於得果與阿羅漢地，
不住於獨覺地，亦不住於佛地。

judge.reason: A faithfully translates "དེ་བཞིན་" (likewise) in the second line as "同樣的", which B drops.

atts.t:
凡是心想成為善逝之聲聞，
以及想要成為獨覺，同樣想成為佛法之法王與佛者，
若不依賴此安忍則無法證得，
猶如不見從此岸前往彼岸之渡口。

i.sp: 同樣想成為佛法之法王與佛者
i.ev: The Tibetan has only ཆོས་རྒྱལ ('Dharma King') as the third wish (རང་སངས་རྒྱས་དག་དེ་བཞིན་ཆོས་རྒྱལ་འགྱུར་འདོད་པ), the Sanskrit धर्मराजो likewise; Mipham 2-4 glosses it as one figure, ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་སངས་རྒྱས ('the Dharma King, the Buddha'), and Khenrab 2-4 as ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས. The Chinese 佛法之法王與佛者 reads as two separate aspirants and wrongly pulls in the locked ཆོས→佛法.
i.fx: 同樣想成為法王，即佛者

atts.t:
若思欲成為善逝之聲聞，
或欲成為獨覺，如是欲成佛法之法王與佛，
若不依此安忍則無法證得，
猶如不見從此岸至彼岸之渡口。

i.sp: 佛法之法王與佛
i.ev: Tibetan has only "རང་སངས་རྒྱས་དག་དེ་བཞིན་ཆོས་རྒྱལ་འགྱུར་འདོད་པ" (wish to become pratyekabuddhas, and likewise a ཆོས་རྒྱལ "Dharma King"). Mipham 2-4 glosses it as one figure, "ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་སངས་རྒྱས" (the Dharma King, the Buddha), and Khenrab 2-4 as "ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྒྱལ་པོ་སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས". The Chinese adds 佛法 to the locked 法王 and lists "Buddha" as a second item (與佛), as if two goals.
i.fx: 法王

judge.reason: B correctly frames "གང་དག་...པ" as a relative clause ("凡是...者"), whereas A misinterprets it as a conditional ("若").

atts.t:
怙主於中所行之此般若波羅蜜多，
若有何人恭敬受持並通達，
彼不為毒藥、兵器、火與水所害，
魔與魔黨等黨類亦無法尋得其破綻。

i.sp: 魔與魔黨等黨類
i.ev: Tibetan "བདུད་དང་བདུད་ཀྱི་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱིས" is simply "Māra and Māra's faction" (locked: བདུད་ཀྱི་ཕྱོགས = 魔黨). The translation stacks the locked terms for བདུད་ཀྱི་ཕྱོགས (魔黨) and ཕྱོགས (黨類) and adds "等", producing a redundant, slightly list-like phrase not in the Tibetan.
i.fx: 魔與魔黨亦無法尋得其可乘之機

atts.t:
怙主所行之此般若波羅蜜多，
若有何人恭敬受持並通達，
彼不為毒、兵器、火與水所害，
魔與魔黨等黨類亦尋不得其破綻。

i.sp: 魔與魔黨等黨類
i.ev: Tibetan "བདུད་དང་བདུད་ཀྱི་ཕྱོགས་ཀྱིས" = Māra and the faction of Māra. The locked བདུད་ཀྱི་ཕྱོགས is already 魔黨, so 等黨類 renders ཕྱོགས a second time and adds a redundant "and such factions" not in the Tibetan (Mipham 2-14, Khenrab 2-14 speak only of བདུད and བདུད་ཀྱི་ཕྱོགས/སྡེ).
i.fx: 魔與魔黨

judge.reason: A precisely captures the locative marker "ལ་" (in which) with "於中", accurately rendering "གང་ལ་མགོན་སྤྱོད་པ".

atts.t:
遍計假定於無邊俱胝之剎土，
所有一切安住之有情，
皆不作他業，唯以天花、勝香與
塗香，於三世供養一劫或更長時；

i.sp: 於三世供養一劫或更長時
i.ev: Tibetan "བྱུག་པས་དུས་གསུམ་བསྐལ་པའམ་དེ་བས་ལྷག་མཆོད" — དུས་གསུམ here is the three times of the day, not the three times past/present/future. bo-mipham 2-15 glosses it "ཉིན་མཚན་རེ་རེ་ཞིང་དུས་གསུམ་དུ་མ་ཆག་པར" (at three times every day and night without break), and bo-rangjung 2-15 "དུས་སྔ་དྲོ་གུང་ཕྱི་དྲོ་གསུམ" (morning, noon, afternoon). english_academic has "three times of each day". Rendering with the locked 三世 changes the meaning of the offering schedule (the locked term does not fit this context).
i.fx: 於每日三時供養一劫或更長時

i.sp: 遍計假定
i.ev: Tibetan "ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་བཟུང་" is glossed in bo-mipham 2-15 as "ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་པ་བཟུང་བའི་དཔེར་བྱ་ན" (taking it as a supposition/example). 遍計 is the Yogācāra technical term for parikalpita (imputation), which misleads here; the sense is a hypothetical supposition.
i.fx: 設想

atts.t:
假定於無邊俱胝之剎土，
所有一切安住之有情，
皆不作他業，唯以天花、勝香與
塗香，於每日三世供養一劫或更長時；

i.sp: 於每日三世供養
i.ev: "དུས་གསུམ" here means three times of each day: Mipham 2-15 "ཉིན་མཚན་རེ་རེ་ཞིང་དུས་གསུམ་དུ", Rangjung 2-15 "དུས་སྔ་དྲོ་གུང་ཕྱི་དྲོ་གསུམ" (morning, noon, evening); Skt triyadhva-. Chinese 三世 normally means past/present/future, so 每日三世 is hard to parse and allows a wrong reading. The locked 三世 clashes with the sense; the span should make the daily sense explicit.
i.fx: 於每日三時（晨、午、昏）供養

judge.reason: A fully translates "ཡོངས་སུ་བརྟག་" as "遍計假定", whereas B drops the prefix "ཡོངས་སུ་" (yongs su).

atts.t:
若有何人因導師十力由此出生，
而將此善逝之母亦即佛母書寫於經卷，
受持並以花與塗香作恭敬，
造作佛塔並作供養之福德亦不及此一分。

i.sp: 亦即佛母
i.ev: Tibetan "བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་ཀྱི་ཡུམ་འདི" is just "this Mother of the Sugatas" (locked: 善逝之母); the added "亦即佛母" (from the separate locked entry ཡུམ) is not in the Tibetan and redundant.
i.fx: 將此善逝之母書寫於經卷

atts.t:
若有何人將能出生導師十力之
此善逝之母、佛母，書寫於經卷，
受持並以花與塗香作恭敬，
則造佛塔作供養之福德亦不及此少分。

i.sp: 此善逝之母、佛母
i.ev: Tibetan has one phrase "བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་ཀྱི་ཡུམ་འདི" (this Mother of the Sugatas; Skt sugatamāta). The Chinese stacks both locked entries (善逝之母 and ཡུམ→佛母) as two epithets, adding a second designation that is not in the Tibetan. Rangjung 2-15 reads it as the single "བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པ་བསྐྱེད་པའི་ཡུམ".
i.fx: 此善逝之母

judge.reason: B correctly treats "གང་ལས་" as a relative clause modifying the Mother, while A turns it into an awkward causal clause.

atts.t:
播下種子安住於地將生長，
獲得聚合完全生出眾多形色；
五波羅蜜多與所有菩提功德，
彼等一切亦由般若波羅蜜多生。

i.sp: 獲得聚合完全生出眾多形色
i.ev: Tibetan "ཚོགས་པ་རྙེད་ནས་རྣམ་མང་གཟུགས་དག་རྣམ་པར་སྐྱེ": bo-mipham 2-20 specifies "རང་རང་གི་རྒྱུ་དང་རྐྱེན་གྱི་ཚོགས་པ་རྙེད་ནས" (obtaining the assembly of their respective causes and conditions); bo-khenrab 2-20 likewise. "獲得聚合" leaves the assembled thing unspecified, and "完全" is added for རྣམ་པར་ (which here only means "arise/grow", Skt. virohanti).
i.fx: 遇得因緣聚合，眾多形色即得生起

atts.t:
播下種子安住於地將生長，
遇得因緣聚合，眾多形色即得生起；
五波羅蜜多與所有菩提功德，
彼等一切亦由般若波羅蜜多生。

judge.reason: B clarifies the overly literal and vague "獲得聚合" by specifying "因緣聚合" (based on the commentary), resulting in much better readability.

atts.t:
勝者遍問帝釋，帝釋作答言：
縱使化為如恆河沙數之佛剎土，
彼等皆盈滿勝者之舍利，
我亦唯取此般若波羅蜜多。

i.sp: 縱使化為如恆河沙數之佛剎土
i.ev: Locked: སངས་རྒྱས་ཞིང = 佛剎 (the translation uses 佛剎土, mixing in ཞིང = 剎土). Also "化為" (transformed into) adds a notion of transformation; bo-mipham 2-22 reads "སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཞིང་དུ་གྱུར་པ" simply as "being buddha-fields equal in number to the Ganges sands".
i.fx: 縱使有如恆河沙數之佛剎

atts.t:
勝者遍問帝釋，帝釋作答言：
縱使有等同恆河沙數之佛剎，
且彼等一切剎土皆盈滿勝者之舍利，
我亦唯取此般若波羅蜜多。

judge.reason: A correctly translates 'དེ་ཀུན་' (all of those) as '彼等一切', while B just has '彼等皆' and awkwardly duplicates '剎土'.

atts.t:
若問何故？並非我不恭敬舍利，
然因遍修般若之故而受供養；
譬如依賴國王之人獲得尊敬，
佛舍利亦依賴般若波羅蜜多。

i.sp: 然因遍修般若之故而受供養
i.ev: Tibetan "ཤེས་རབ་ཡོངས་སུ་བསྒོམས་པས་མཆོད་པར་བགྱིད" has Śakra as the agent ("I make offerings"). bo-mipham 2-23 explains "ཤེས་རབ་འདི་ལྟ་བུས་ཡོངས་སུ་བསྒོས་པས་སྐུ་གདུང་དེ་དག་ཀྱང་མཆོད་པར་བགྱིད་པའི་འོས་སུ་གྱུར" and bo-khenrab 2-23 "ཡོངས་སུ་ཟིན་ཅིང་བསྒོས་པས", i.e. the relics are pervaded by wisdom. The translation drops the first-person agent and leaves unclear who cultivates wisdom (the relics are the object permeated by it).
i.fx: 然因（舍利）為般若所遍熏，故我供養之

atts.t:
若問何故？並非我不恭敬舍利，
然因其為般若所遍熏故我作供養；
譬如依賴國王之人獲得尊敬，
佛舍利亦依賴般若波羅蜜多。

judge.reason: A translates 'བསྒོམས་པས་' (commentary: 'བསྒོས་པས་') properly as '遍熏' (permeated), matching the English and context better than B's '遍修'.

atts.t:
譬如南贍部洲有千萬樹木，
種類繁多、品類無數且形色各異；
除了在陰影數量上作稱說之外，
陰影並無種種區分，亦無差異。

i.sp: 千萬樹木
i.ev: Tibetan "ཤིང་རྣམས་བྱེ་བ་སྟོང་" is thousands of koṭis (Skt. sahasrakoṭī; bo-mipham 2-27 "བྱེ་བ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་དུ་མ"). 千萬 is only ten million and understates the number; elsewhere (2-15) the translation correctly uses 千俱胝 for བྱེ་བ་ཕྲག་སྟོང.
i.fx: 千俱胝樹木

atts.t:
譬如南贍部洲有千俱胝樹木，
種類繁多、品類無數且形色各異；
除了在陰影數量上作稱說之外，
陰影並無種種區分，亦無差異。

i.sp: 除了在陰影數量上作稱說之外
i.ev: "གྲིབ་མར་གྱུར་པའི་གྲངས་སུ་བརྗོད་པ་མ་གཏོགས་པར": གྲངས here is enumeration/designation (Skt saṃkhyā), not a quantity. Mipham 2-27 "གྲིབ་མར་གྱུར་པའི་རྣམ་གྲངས་སུ་བརྗོད་པ་ཙམ" and Khenrab 2-26 "མིང་གི་རྣམ་གྲངས་སུ་བརྗོད་པ་ཙམ": the shadows are merely called "shadow of such-and-such tree" as a nominal classification. 數量 suggests counting shadows.
i.fx: 除了僅被稱說為歸入陰影之列（名言上的分類）之外

judge.reason: B accurately translates 'བྱེ་བ་སྟོང་' (a thousand ten-millions) as '千俱胝', whereas A's '千萬' drops the thousand multiplier.

atts.t:
菩薩若於未善了知之狀態下，
將色、想、受、行、識，
遍開示為無常，即是行於造作；
智者從不毀壞諸法。

i.sp: 即是行於造作
i.ev: Tibetan 'བཅོས་ལ་སྤྱོད་པ་སྟེ' means practising a counterfeit/fabricated imitation; bo-mipham 2-29 glosses it as 'ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པའི་གཟུགས་བརྙན་ནམ་ཤེར་ཕྱིན་བཅོས་མ' (an image/counterfeit of the perfection of wisdom), and bo-khenrab 2-29 likewise 'ཤེར་ཕྱིན་བཅོས་མ'. Chinese '造作' in Buddhist usage means volitional making/karmic fabrication and does not convey 'counterfeit', nor what is counterfeited.
i.fx: 即是行於偽造（仿似般若波羅蜜多）之物

atts.t:
菩薩若於未善了知之狀態下，
將色、想、受、行、識，
遍開示為無常，即是行於偽造之物；
智者從不毀壞諸法。

judge.reason: A translates 'བཅོས་' accurately as '偽造之物' (counterfeit), matching the commentary and the English translation better than B's '造作'.

atts.t:
何以故？此等殊勝說者於此修學後，
於此開示一切諸法皆為空性；
聽聞此法，聲聞速疾觸證解脫，
亦能觸證獨覺菩提與佛菩提。

i.sp: 亦能觸證獨覺菩提與佛菩提
i.ev: Tibetan 'རང་རྒྱལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་དང་ནི་སངས་རྒྱས་བྱང་ཆུབ་རེག' has no stated subject; the Chinese '亦能' attaches both awakenings to the śrāvakas just mentioned. bo-mipham 2-32 and bo-khenrab 2-32 distribute them by faculty: śrāvakas swiftly reach liberation; those of middling faculty reach pratyekabuddha awakening ('དབང་པོ་འབྲིང་གིས་...རང་རྒྱལ་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཐོབ་པ'); those of sharp faculty reach buddha awakening ('དབང་པོ་རྣོན་པོས་...སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ལ་རེག་པར་འགྱུར'). The Chinese makes śrāvakas attain all three.
i.fx: 聲聞速疾觸證解脫，獨覺（中根者）觸證獨覺菩提，利根者觸證佛菩提

atts.t:
何以故？此等殊勝說者於此修學後，
於此開示一切諸法皆為空性；
聽聞此法，聲聞速疾觸證解脫，
亦有觸證獨覺菩提與佛菩提者。

judge.reason: A uses '亦有...者' to correctly distinguish the subjects attaining the latter two enlightenments, whereas B incorrectly makes '聲聞' the subject for all.

atts.t:
譬如無熱惱池若無龍主，
此南贍部洲何能有河川流注？
若無河川，則不生起花朵與果實，
大海之中亦將無有眾多寶色。

i.sp: 眾多寶色
i.ev: Tibetan 'རིན་ཆེན་གཟུགས་མང་' (Sanskrit 'ratanā nekarūpāḥ'): many kinds/forms of jewels. bo-mipham 2-35 'རིན་ཆེན་སྣ་ཚོགས་ཀྱི་གཟུགས་མི་འདྲ་བ་མང་པོ' and bo-khenrab 2-35 'རིན་ཆེན་སྣ་ཚོགས་པ...གཟུགས་མི་འདྲ་བ་མང་པོ' (many dissimilar forms/kinds). Chinese '寶色' reads as 'colour of jewels', which narrows gzugs here.
i.fx: 眾多種種不同形色之寶

atts.t:
譬如無熱惱池若無龍主，
此南贍部洲何能有河川流注？
若無河川，則不生起花朵與果實，
大海之中亦將無有眾多不同形色之寶。

judge.reason: A accurately renders 'རིན་ཆེན་གཟུགས་མང་' (many forms of jewels) as '眾多不同形色之寶', whereas B compresses it to '眾多寶色'.

atts.t:
諸聲聞眾盡其布施與持戒，
以及具足修習所生福德聚，
相比菩薩求證菩提一念隨喜之心，
聲聞眾之福德蘊不及一分。

i.sp: 菩薩求證菩提一念隨喜之心
i.ev: Tibetan 'བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་སེམས་གཅིག' is simply a bodhisattva's single mind of rejoicing; 'བྱང་ཆུབ་' belongs to 'བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ' (bodhisattva). The phrase '求證菩提' has no counterpart; bo-mipham 2-38 and bo-khenrab 2-38 describe the rejoicing as a single moment of mind, not a mind seeking awakening.
i.fx: 相較於菩薩一念隨喜之心

atts.t:
諸聲聞眾盡其所有布施與持戒，
以及修習所生具足之福德聚，
然於菩薩迴向菩提之一念隨喜心，
聲聞眾之福德蘊皆不及一分。

i.sp: 菩薩迴向菩提之一念隨喜心
i.ev: Tibetan "བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་སེམས་གཅིག" = a bodhisattva's single mind of rejoicing; nothing says it is dedicated to awakening. 迴向菩提 interpolates a dedication that Khenrab 2-38 brings in only as commentary ("བླ་མེད་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་བསྔོ་བའི་ཐབས་མཁས") and Mipham 2-38 does not state in the verse; the English academic also has no such qualifier. It also pushes བསྔོ་བ into a verse that is about རྗེས་སུ་ཡི་རང་ alone.
i.fx: 菩薩之一念隨喜心

i.sp: 福德蘊
i.ev: ཕུང་པོ in "བསོད་ནམས་ཕུང་པོ" is a heap/mass of merit (Mipham 2-38 "བསོད་ནམས་ཕུང་པོ"), and the line before uses 福德聚. 蘊 is the technical rendering of skandha (the five aggregates), so it is inconsistent and misleading here.
i.fx: 福德聚

atts.t:
從最初發心、發殊勝菩提心起，
直至諸導師正法滅盡之時，
於此期間彼等勝者所有福德，
具足波羅蜜多以及諸佛法與佛功德，

i.sp: 諸佛法與佛功德
i.ev: Tibetan 'སངས་རྒྱས་ཆོས་གང་' is a single item, 'whatever buddha-qualities' (locked 佛功德); the list is merit, what is endowed with the perfections, and buddha-qualities. The Chinese gives two items, '諸佛法' and '佛功德', duplicating the one term.
i.fx: 具足波羅蜜多以及諸佛功德

atts.t:
從最初發殊勝菩提心、生起此發心起，
直至諸導師之正法滅盡之時，
於此期間彼等勝者所有之福德，
以及具備波羅蜜多之佛法與任何佛功德，

i.sp: 具備波羅蜜多之佛法
i.ev: Tibetan "ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་དང་ལྡན་དང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཆོས་གང་དང" = what is endowed with the perfections, and whatever buddha-qualities. Mipham 2-39 reads the first as "སྦྱོར་བ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་དང་ལྡན་པ" (the practice endowed with the six perfections) and the second as "འབྲས་བུ་... སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས". The Chinese inserts 佛法 as the thing endowed with perfections and then adds 佛功德, so a "buddha-dharma" item is added.
i.fx: 具備波羅蜜多者，以及任何佛功德

judge.reason: A translates 'གང་' (whatever) as '任何', accurately reflecting the Tibetan, while B leaves it out.

atts.t:
若取為相則非迴向，
若無有相即是菩提迴向。
猶如食用混雜毒藥之佳餚，
勝者宣說以善法功德為所緣亦復如是。

i.sp: 善法功德
i.ev: Tibetan 'དཀར་པོའི་ཆོས' is a single locked term (善法, 'white/virtuous phenomena'). The Chinese appends 功德 (the locked rendering of ཆོས་ in other contexts), producing a conflated compound '善法功德' with no counterpart in the Tibetan.
i.fx: 以善法為所緣

atts.t:
若執取為相則並非迴向，
若無有相方為菩提迴向。
猶如食用混雜毒藥之佳餚，
勝者宣說以善法與功德為所緣亦復如是。

i.sp: 善法與功德
i.ev: Tibetan "དཀར་པོའི་ཆོས་ལ་དམིགས་པ" = apprehending white/virtuous dharma (one item). Mipham 2-44 "དཀར་པོའི་ཆོས་ཡིན་ཀྱང་དེ་ལ་བདེན་པར་ཞེན་པའི་འདུ་ཤེས་ཀྱིས་དམིགས་པ". The Chinese splits it into two objects, 善法 and 功德 (the glossary entry ཆོས→功德 was applied on top of དཀར་པོའི་ཆོས→善法), adding a second item.
i.fx: 以善法為所緣

judge.reason: A treats 'དཀར་པོའི་ཆོས་' properly as a single concept '善法功德', whereas B inappropriately splits it into '善法與功德'.

atts.t:
若思「我當修習勝者之般若，
並解脫無數為苦所觸之有情」，
如是遍計有情想、求菩提之菩薩，
並非修習殊勝之般若波羅蜜多。

i.sp: 求菩提之菩薩
i.ev: Tibetan has only བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ (locked: 菩薩), a single term for 'bodhisattva'; 'seeking awakening' is not a separate word in the Tibetan or in Sanskrit bodhisattvo.
i.fx: 遍計有情想之菩薩

atts.t:
若思維「我當修習勝者之般若，
並解脫千百億受苦之有情」，
如是妄計有情想、志求菩提之菩薩，
此並非修習殊勝之般若波羅蜜多。

i.sp: 志求菩提之菩薩
i.ev: Tibetan "སེམས་ཅན་འདུ་ཤེས་ཡོངས་རྟོག་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ" = the bodhisattva who conceptualizes the perception of sentient beings; བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ is the single term 菩薩 (Mipham 2-50, Khenrab 2-50 use just བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ). 志求菩提之 is a gloss on the name, not in the Tibetan.
i.fx: 菩薩

judge.reason: A is better because it accurately translates "རེག་པ་" (spṛṣṭa) as "所觸" (touched by), whereas B generalizes it to "受苦" (suffering).

atts.t:
如是善入勝菩提者，
應知聽聞此勝者之般若波羅蜜多；
縱然未獲導師現前授記，
「我不久將觸證佛菩提」。

i.sp: 「我不久將觸證佛菩提」
i.ev: The quoted clause སངས་རྒྱས་བྱང་ཆུབ་རིང་པོར་མི་ཐོགས་བདག་རེག་འགྱུར་ is left without a governing verb, so it hangs after the semicolon. bo-khenrab 4-6 reads it as the person's own knowledge: 'བདག་གིས་རེག་པའམ་ཐོབ་པར་འགྱུར་རོ་སྙམ་དུ་ཤེས་ཏེ' (knows 'I will touch/attain...').
i.fx: 縱然未獲導師現前授記，亦知「我不久將觸證佛菩提」。

atts.t:
如是善入勝菩提者，
應知聽聞此勝者之般若波羅蜜多；
縱然未獲導師現前授記，
亦知「我不久將觸證佛菩提」。

judge.reason: A is better because it includes the verb "亦知" to introduce the final quote, making the sentence grammatically complete and clear.

atts.t:
欲求恭敬且欲求利養，
以伴隨見之心親近俗家，
捨棄佛法而從事非佛法之行為，
捨棄道而走向歧路，此乃魔事。

i.sp: 以伴隨見之心
i.ev: The Tibetan 'ལྟ་དང་བཅས་པའི་སེམས' (Skt sāpekṣacitta) is not 'view' in the doctrinal sense. Mipham (bo-mipham 4-16) glosses it 'ཕྱི་རོལ་ཡུལ་ལ་ལྟ་བར་འདོད་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་སེམས' (a mind with desire to look at external objects), and Khenrab (bo-khenrab 4-16) 'གཟུགས་དང་ཡུལ་གྱི་བཀོད་པ་སྣ་ཚོགས་བལྟ་བར་འདོད་པ་དང་བཅས་པའི་སེམས' (desire to gaze at varied forms and scenes). Rendering ལྟ as 見 (the locked term) in the Chinese phrase 伴隨見之心 reads as 'a mind accompanied by views', i.e. wrong views, which is a different meaning; the English reference also reads 'longs to view external objects'.
i.fx: 以帶著觀望外境之欲求的心親近俗家

atts.t:
欲求恭敬且欲求利養，
以欲求見外境之心親近俗家，
捨棄佛法而從事非佛法之行為，
捨棄道而走向歧路，此乃魔事。

將貪求恭敬以及貪求利養，
以伴隨貪看之心親近俗家，
捨棄佛法而從事非佛法之行，
捨棄道步入歧路此乃魔事。

i.sp: 捨棄道步入歧路此乃魔事
i.ev: Tibetan ལམ་བོར་ལམ་གོལ་འགྲོ་བ། འདི་ནི་བདུད་ཀྱི་ལས། has two clauses (abandoning the path and going astray; 'this is the work of Mara'). The Chinese runs them together with no punctuation, unlike the other three lines, which makes the line harder to parse. The meaning is intact.
i.fx: 捨棄道而步入歧路，此乃魔事。

judge.reason: B is better because "欲求見外境之心" clearly conveys the commentary's "desiring to view external objects," whereas A's "伴隨見之心" is awkwardly literal.

atts.t:
世間真如與阿羅漢真如，
獨覺真如與勝者之子真如，
皆是同一、離實事且非他異的真如；
如來了知此般若波羅蜜多。

i.sp: 如來了知此般若波羅蜜多
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན་པ་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་མཁྱེན' (Skt prajñāya pāramita ... tathāgatena): the perfection of wisdom is the means by which the Tathagata knows the suchnesses listed in the preceding lines (English reference: 'By the perfection of wisdom, the Tathāgata knows this'); Mipham's section heading around 4-22/4-23 is 'ཤེར་ཕྱིན་ལ་བརྟེན་ནས་འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་བདེན་གཉིས་ལ་མཁས་པ' (relying on the perfection of wisdom, being skilled in the world's truths). The Chinese makes the perfection of wisdom the object known and drops the suchness as the thing known, changing the logic.
i.fx: 如來藉由般若波羅蜜多而了知此（真如）

atts.t:
世間真如與阿羅漢真如，
獨覺真如與勝者之子真如，
皆是同一、離實事且非他異之真如；
如來藉由般若波羅蜜多而了知此真如。

i.sp: 如來藉由般若波羅蜜多而了知此真如
i.ev: The Tibetan line is 'shes rab pha rol phyin pa de bzhin gshegs pas mkhyen': the perfection of wisdom is the object known by the Tathagata (so also the approved English). The Chinese turns it into an instrumental ('by means of the perfection of wisdom, the Tathagata knows this suchness') and supplies 'this suchness' as object. This is a possible reading (Skt prajñāya pāramita ... tathāgatena; bo-rangjung 4-22 'relying on the perfection of wisdom, the Tathagata knows as it is'), but it is not what the Tibetan says on its face and bo-mipham 4-22 glosses the perfection of wisdom itself as the nature of all phenomena that the Tathagata knows.
i.fx: 如來了知般若波羅蜜多。

judge.reason: A is better because it correctly treats "般若波羅蜜多" as instrumental ("藉由..."), matching the Sanskrit and context, whereas B incorrectly makes it the object.

atts.t:
如是行持之善海與語中明月，
乃為眾生之歸依、守護者與住處；
為所依、覺慧、洲與尋求義利之導師，
為照明之燈與不傾動之殊勝佛法宣說者。

i.sp: 為照明之燈
i.ev: Tibetan lists two separate epithets, "གསལ་བྱེད་སྒྲོན་མ" (illuminator, lamp); bo-mipham 4-45 glosses "གསལ་བྱེད་དུ་གྱུར་པ" (becoming the illuminator, by teaching person-selflessness) separately from "ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྒྲོན་མ་ཆེན་པོ" (the lamp, by teaching phenomena-selflessness). The Chinese fuses them into one "照明之燈", dropping the separate item.
i.fx: 為照明者、為燈

atts.t:
如是行持之善海與語中明月，
乃為眾生之歸依、守護者與住處；
為所依、覺慧、洲與尋求義利之導師，
為照明者、為燈與不傾動之殊勝佛法宣說者。

judge.reason: A is better for fidelity because it accurately preserves "illuminators" and "lamps" as two distinct items, whereas B merges them into a single term.

atts.t:
具大名聲者為難行而披甲，
然此非蘊、界與處之鎧甲；
彼等遠離三乘想且無執取，
具不退轉、無動搖與不傾動之法性。

i.sp: 具不退轉、無動搖與不傾動之法性
i.ev: Tibetan ends "མི་ལྡོག་གཡོ་བ་མེད་ཅིང་མི་འཁྲུགས་ཆོས་ཅན་ཡིན"; "ཆོས་ཅན" (Skt. -dharmāḥ) here means 'of such a nature / possessing' (bo-mipham 4-46: "མི་འཁྲུགས་པའི་ཆོས་ཅན་ཡིན"; bo-rangjung 4-46: "ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཆོས་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་དང་ལྡན་པས..."), not dharmatā. 法性 is the locked rendering of ཆོས་ཉིད, so using it here suggests a different term, and it makes 'irreversible' and 'unwavering' appear as a 'nature' rather than predicates of the subjects.
i.fx: 不退轉、無動搖，且為不可擾動之本性者

atts.t:
具大名聲者為難行而披甲，
然此非蘊、界與處之鎧甲；
彼等遠離三乘想且無執取，
不退轉、無動搖，且為不可擾動之本性者。

judge.reason: A is better because it correctly translates "ཆོས་ཅན་" (dharmin) as having a nature, whereas B mistakenly translates it as "法性" (dharmatā).

atts.t:
諸導師之此佛法甚深極難見，
無任何人能證悟亦無從獲得，
是故慈悲施益者證得菩提已，
思量有情眾中孰能知而少顧念。

i.sp: 少顧念
i.ev: Tibetan "ཐུགས་ཁྲལ་ཆུང་བར་མཛད" means he became reluctant or little disposed to teach; bo-mipham 4-48: "ཆོས་སྟོན་པ་ལ་ཐུགས་ཁྲལ་ཆུང་བར་མཛད" (little inclination toward teaching the Dharma); Skt. "alpotsuko". "少顧念" can be read as 'cared little about beings', which contradicts the compassionate benefactor named in the same verse.
i.fx: 於說法興致微薄

atts.t:
諸導師之此佛法甚深極難見，
無任何人能證悟亦無從獲得，
是故慈悲施益者證得菩提已，
思量有情眾中孰能知而於說法興致微薄。

judge.reason: A is better because "於說法興致微薄" accurately clarifies the specific meaning of having little inclination to teach Dharma, supported by the commentary.

atts.t:
善逝菩提遠離各異之法，
任何菩薩若欲獲得此者，
具足方便當修般若，若無導師之般若則無法獲得。

i.sp: 具足方便當修般若，若無導師之般若則無法獲得
i.ev: The Tibetan line is "ཐབས་དང་ལྡན་པས་ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་འདྲེན་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་མེད་ན་ཐོབ་པར་འགྱུར་མ་ཡིན"; commentary bo-mipham 4-52 and bo-khenrab 4-52 gloss it as "འདྲེན་པ་རྒྱལ་བའི་ཡུམ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕར་ཕྱིན" (the perfection of wisdom, mother of the Guides/Victors) and say one must apply oneself to "ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ". The Chinese drops "perfection" (ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ) and "mother" (ཡུམ), and "導師之般若" reads as the wisdom belonging to the guides rather than the wisdom that is their mother. english_academic: "the perfection of wisdom, the mother of the Guides".
i.fx: 具足方便者當勤修般若波羅蜜多；若無此導師之母般若波羅蜜多，則無法獲得

atts.t:
善逝菩提遠離各異之法，
任何菩薩若欲獲得此菩提，
具足方便者當勤修般若波羅蜜多；
若無此導師之母般若波羅蜜多，則無法獲得。

judge.reason: B is better because it preserves the four-line verse structure and appropriately incorporates "母" (mother) as implied by the commentary and context.

atts.t:
若有飛鳥身大一百五十由旬，
羽翼盡毀而無勢力，
彼從三十三天之處向此南贍部洲，
自行躍下於彼必遭毀滅。

i.sp: 必遭毀滅
i.ev: "ཉམ་ཉེས་གྱུར་པ" means suffering harm/injury; bo-khenrab 4-52 glosses it as "ལུས་རྨས་པ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ཉམས་ཉེས་ཆེན་པོ" (body injured and the like, great harm). "毀滅" (destruction/annihilation) overstates it.
i.fx: 於彼必遭損傷

atts.t:
若有飛鳥身大一百五十由旬，
羽翼耗竭而無勢力，
彼從三十三天之處向此南贍部洲，
自行躍下於彼必遭損傷。

judge.reason: B's "耗竭" and "損傷" are more accurate translations for "ཟད་" and "ཉམ་ཉེས་" than A's stronger "盡毀" and "毀滅".

atts.t:
無有財物貪求，為眾生宣說佛法，
唯一喜愛佛法，且恆時具備柔和語；
於行走、經行、睡眠與安坐時皆極具正知，
行走時僅視一軛之量，且心無錯亂。

i.sp: 唯一喜愛佛法
i.ev: "ཆོས་ལ་གཅིག་ཏུ་དགའ་ཞིང" means being single-mindedly/exclusively delighted in the Dharma (bo-mipham 4-57: "རྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ་དགའ"); "唯一喜愛" reads as "the only thing they love" and is awkward.
i.fx: 一向專心喜樂佛法

atts.t:
無有財物貪求，為眾生宣說佛法，
一向專心喜樂佛法，且恆時具備柔和語；
於行走、經行、睡眠與安坐時皆極具正知，
行走時僅視一軛之量，且心無錯亂。

judge.reason: A's "唯一喜愛" is a more concise and literal translation of "གཅིག་ཏུ་དགའ་" than B's expansive "一向專心喜樂".

atts.t:
不求名譽，心未被瞋恚纏縛，
縱為在家者，亦恆不貪著一切事物，
不為謀生而以險惡手段尋求受用，
不修威猛行咒，亦不修女人和合咒。

i.sp: 女人和合咒
i.ev: "བུད་མེད་སྦྱོར་སྔགས" is explained in bo-mipham 4-60 and bo-khenrab 4-60 as mantras that bring women under one's power or control through desire ("བུད་མེད་དབང་དུ་བྱེད་པའམ་རང་དབང་དུ་སྦྱོར་བའི་སྔགས"); "和合" (harmony/union) does not convey subjugation.
i.fx: 令女人受制之咒

atts.t:
不求名譽，心未被瞋恚纏縛，
縱為在家者，亦恆不貪著一切事物，
不為謀生而以險惡手段尋求受用，
不修威猛行咒，亦不修令女人受制之咒。

judge.reason: B's "令女人受制之咒" accurately reflects the commentary's explanation of "སྦྱོར་སྔགས་" as mantras used to bring women under one's control.

atts.t:
不為具欲業者預言將生為男或女，
於極寂靜之般若波羅蜜多中遠離爭鬥與諍論，且慈心堅固，
欲求一切智，且恆具趨向教法之心。

i.sp: 於極寂靜之般若波羅蜜多中遠離爭鬥與諍論
i.ev: "རབ་ཏུ་དབེན་པའི་ཤེས་རབ་ཕ་རོལ་ཕྱིན" with Sanskrit "pravivikta prajñavarapāramitā-abhiyuktāḥ" (utterly secluded, devoted to the perfection of wisdom); bo-mipham 4-61/4-60 reads "རབ་ཏུ་དབེན་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་མཆོག་ལ་བརྩོན་པ" (striving at the perfection of wisdom while utterly secluded), and bo-rangjung 4-59 lists striving at the perfection of wisdom as a separate sign from being free of fighting and disputes ("འཐབ་པ་དང་རྩོད་པ་དང་བྲལ"). The Chinese makes "極寂靜" modify the perfection of wisdom, drops the devotion/striving, and puts freedom from conflict "within" the perfection.
i.fx: 極為寂靜，專注於般若波羅蜜多，遠離爭鬥與諍論

atts.t:
不為具欲業者預言將生為男或女，
極為寂靜且專注於般若波羅蜜多，
遠離爭鬥與諍論且慈心堅固，
欲求一切智，恆具趨向教法之心。

judge.reason: B aligns with the commentary and Sanskrit by including "專注於" (devoted to/engaged in), which is implied in the Tibetan syntax here.

atts.t:
任何菩薩若如是趨於甚深，
於勝義無貪之乘中，蘊與
界、處皆無有，證悟此佛法者，
其真實成就之福德更有何能超越？

i.sp: 無貪
i.ev: "ཆགས་མེད" is non-attachment (bo-khenrab 4-64: "མངོན་ཞེན་གྱིས་ཆགས་པ་མེད་པ"); "無貪" (non-greed, alobha) is a different technical term.
i.fx: 無著

i.sp: 若如是趨於甚深
i.ev: "དེ་ལྟར་ཟབ་གྱུར་ཅིང" "having thus become profound" qualifies the dharma realized (bo-mipham 4-64: "རྟོགས་བྱ་ཆོས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན་... དེ་ལྟར་ངོ་བོས་ཟབ་པར་གྱུར"); "趨於" (tending toward) suggests a bodhisattva progressing toward profundity.
i.fx: 若如是已成甚深

atts.t:
任何菩薩若如是已成甚深，
於勝義無著之乘中，蘊與
界、處皆無有，證悟此佛法者，
其真實成就之福德更有何能超越？

judge.reason: A's "無著" is the standard and more precise rendering for "ཆགས་མེད་" (unattached) in this context than B's "無貪".

atts.t:
譬如行於貪欲法之士夫，
與女人相約卻未與之相會，
其於一日之中生起多少心之分別，
菩薩將能獲得爾許劫之成就。

i.sp: 爾許劫之成就
i.ev: bo-mipham 4-65 says the bodhisattva obtains the virtue/merit accumulated over that many eons ("བསྐལ་པར་བསགས་པའི་དགེ་བ་... ཐོབ་པར་འགྱུར"), and bo-khenrab 4-65 says "བསོད་ནམས་དང་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་བསགས་པའི་དགེ་བ". "成就" (accomplishment) is vague and loses "merit" (བསོད་ནམས་ locked 福德 elsewhere); english_academic: "the merit accumulated over that many eons".
i.fx: 爾許劫所積之福德

atts.t:
譬如行於貪欲法之士夫，
與女人相約卻未與之相會，
其於一日之中生起多少心之分別，
菩薩將能獲得爾許劫所積之福德。

judge.reason: A correctly specifies "福德" (merit) based on the commentary and preceding verse context, whereas B's "成就" is vague.

atts.t:
任何菩薩於多千俱胝劫，
縱向阿羅漢獨覺布施且持戒，
若人宣說具殊勝般若波羅蜜多之佛法，
彼布施持戒不及此宣說之善一分。

i.sp: 阿羅漢獨覺
i.ev: The Tibetan lists two separate recipients, "དགྲ་བཅོམ་རང་རྒྱལ" (bo-rangjung 4-66: "དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་དང་རང་སངས་རྒྱས"); without a conjunction the Chinese can be read as a single compound.
i.fx: 阿羅漢與獨覺

atts.t:
任何菩薩於多千俱胝劫，
縱向阿羅漢與獨覺布施且持戒，
若人宣說具殊勝般若波羅蜜多之佛法，
彼布施持戒不及此宣說之善一分。

judge.reason: The only difference is the minor addition of the conjunction "與" in B, which does not significantly affect fidelity or clarity.

atts.t:
猶如水滴從最初直至最後，
漸次一點一滴將其完全充滿；
如是最初之心亦為殊勝菩提因，
漸次圓滿善功德而成佛。

i.sp: 將其完全充滿
i.ev: Tibetan line 2 'ཆུ་ཡི་ཐིགས་པས་བུམ་པ་དང་པོ་ཐ་མའི་བར། རིམ་གྱིས་ཉུང་ངུ་ཉུང་ངུས་དེ་ཡོངས་འགེངས་པ་ལྟར' names the object being filled, the vase (བུམ་པ). The Chinese drops 'vase' and has only the pronoun 其 with no antecedent, so the simile's object is missing (bo-mipham 4-74: 'བུམ་པ་བཀང་བ...བུམ་པ་དེ་ཡོངས་སུ་འགེངས་པ་ལྟར').
i.fx: 猶如以水滴從最初直至最後，漸次一點一滴將瓶完全充滿

atts.t:
猶如以水滴從最初直至最後，
漸次一點一滴將瓶完全充滿；
如是最初之心亦為殊勝菩提因，
漸次圓滿善功德而成佛。

judge.reason: A correctly and explicitly translates "བུམ་པ་" as "瓶" (vase), whereas B reduces it to a pronoun ("其").

atts.t:
如是彼時善巧菩薩亦復然，
於諸有情界中廣大生起悲，
徹底超越四魔以及二地後，
安住勝三摩地不觸及菩提。

i.sp: 二地
i.ev: Tibetan 'ས་གཉིས' (two levels) is, per bo-mipham 4-80 ('ཉན་རང་གི་ས་གཉིས') and bo-rangjung 4-79 ('ཉན་ཐོས་དང་རང་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ས་གཉིས'), the Śrāvaka and Pratyekabuddha levels. In Chinese Buddhist usage bare 二地 normally means the second bodhisattva bhūmi, a reading the commentaries exclude.
i.fx: 聲聞與緣覺二地

atts.t:
如是彼時善巧菩薩亦復然，
於諸有情界中廣大生起悲，
徹底超越四魔與聲聞緣覺二地後，
安住勝三摩地不觸及菩提。

judge.reason: A is more faithful to the Tibetan root text, whereas B adds "聲聞緣覺" (Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas), which is absent in the source.

atts.t:
風依虛空而水蘊依於彼，
此大地依彼且眾生依彼；
有情受用業之因即如是，
當思惟此義：虛空依何處？

i.sp: 水蘊
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཆུ་ཡི་ཕུང་པོ' means a mass or heap of water (the water layer of the world-system; bo-mipham 4-82 and bo-khenrab 4-82 describe it as the water layer supporting the great earth). 蘊 is the glossary rendering of ཕུང་པོ as 'aggregate' (skandha), so 水蘊 reads as a water-skandha and misleads.
i.fx: 水聚

atts.t:
風依虛空而水聚依於彼，
此大地依彼且眾生依彼；
有情受用業之因即如是，
當思惟此義：虛空依何處？

judge.reason: A translates "ཆུ་ཡི་ཕུང་པོ" as "水聚" (mass of water), which is contextually better than B's "水蘊" which usually denotes the skandhas.

atts.t:
譬如比丘具足勝神通力，
住於虛空頓時化現神變，
示現行走、經行以及坐臥，
彼無厭倦亦無有疲勞。

i.sp: 頓時
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཅིག་ཆར' means 'simultaneously'; bo-mipham 4-88 glosses it 'དུས་ཅིག་ཆར' and bo-khenrab 4-88 'དུས་ཅིག་ཆར་ཏུ' (at one and the same time). Skt 'yamaka' is the twin miracle. 頓時 means 'suddenly/instantly', a different nuance.
i.fx: 同時

atts.t:
譬如比丘具足勝神通力，
住於虛空同時化現神變，
示現行走、經行以及坐臥，
彼無厭倦亦無有疲勞。

judge.reason: A correctly uses "同時" for "ཅིག་ཆར" (simultaneously), whereas B's "頓時" means suddenly or immediately.

atts.t:
如是菩薩前往空性珍寶之
洲，獲得靜慮、諸根與諸力，
並非僅喜悅於觸涅槃，
而將有情置於受苦之心。

i.sp: 珍寶之
i.ev: Tibetan "རིན་ཆེན་གྱི། གླིང་དུ་སོང་སྟེ" is the same jewel-island (རིན་ཆེན་གླིང) rendered 寶洲 in 4-92 and 4-94 (locked term); here it appears as 珍寶之洲, breaking term consistency (Mipham 4-92 also reads "རིན་ཆེན་གྱི་གླིང" for the same image).
i.fx: 前往空性寶洲

atts.t:
如是菩薩前往空性寶洲，
獲得靜慮、諸根與諸力，
並非僅喜悅於觸涅槃，
而將有情置於受苦之心。

i.sp: 並非僅喜悅於觸涅槃，而將有情置於受苦之心
i.ev: Tibetan 'mya ngan 'das la reg pa 'ba' zhig mngon dga' zhing / sems can sdug bsngal yid du 'jog par 'gyur ma yin': the negation ('gyur ma yin) covers both clauses, i.e. the bodhisattva neither delights in touching nirvana for himself alone nor leaves beings in suffering (bo-mipham 4-92, bo-khenrab 4-92: does not leave other beings in a mind tormented by suffering). In the Chinese, '並非...，而...' can be read as 'not merely X, but rather does Y', i.e. as if the bodhisattva does place beings in suffering; 置於受苦之心 is also obscure.
i.fx: 既不獨自僅喜悅於觸證涅槃，亦不棄有情於苦中

judge.reason: B is better formatted; A awkwardly splits the compound "珍寶之洲" (jewel island) across two lines.

atts.t:
何時以慈相繫眾生後，
行空性無相無願三摩地，
謂彼將會證得於涅槃，
或能施設為有為？無有是處。

i.sp: 以慈相繫眾生後
i.ev: Tibetan "འགྲོ་ལ་བྱམས་པས་རྗེས་སུ་འབྲེལ་བྱས་ནས" (Mipham 4-96: བྱམས་པ་ཆེན་པོས་བཟུང་བའི་སྒོ་ནས་རྗེས་སུ་འབྲེལ་བར་བྱས) means "being accompanied/held by loving-kindness toward beings"; 慈相 can be read as a noun "sign of loving-kindness", colliding with 相 = nimitta in the very next line (無相).
i.fx: 以慈而與眾生相隨相繫之後

atts.t:
何時以慈而與眾生相隨相繫之後，
行空性、無相、無願三摩地，
謂彼將會證得於涅槃，
或能施設為有為？無有是處。

judge.reason: B is more concise and metrically sound, avoiding A's redundant "相隨相繫" for "རྗེས་སུ་འབྲེལ་".

atts.t:
若於廣達五百由旬山谷中，
充滿毒蛇之處安住千萬年，
不知此遠離之彼菩薩，
獲得增上慢而安住於混雜。

i.sp: 千萬年
i.ev: Tibetan "ལོ་མང་བྱེ་བ" = "many ten-millions of years" (Sanskrit bahuvarṣakoṭī; Khenrab 5-8 "ལོ་མང་པོ་བྱེའི་བར་དུ"). 千萬年 states a single koṭi (10 million) and drops "many".
i.fx: 多個千萬年

atts.t:
若於廣達五百由旬山谷中，
充滿毒蛇之處安住多個千萬年，
不知此遠離之彼菩薩，
獲得增上慢而安住於混雜。

i.sp: 若於廣達五百由旬山谷中，充滿毒蛇之處安住多個千萬年，不知此遠離之彼菩薩
i.ev: Tibetan 'gnas byed kyang ... mi shes pa'i byang chub sems dpa' de' is concessive: even if a bodhisattva stays physically secluded for many tens of millions of years, he who does not know this (inner) solitude acquires superior pride (bo-mipham 5-9, bo-rangjung 5-9: bodily solitude alone yields pride). The Chinese opens with a plain conditional 若, losing the concession, and adds 毒 to 'snakes' (Tib. sbrul; bo-mipham's 'gdug pa'i sbrul' is a gloss).
i.fx: 縱使於廣達五百由旬、滿布蛇類的山谷中安住多個千萬年，不知此遠離之彼菩薩

judge.reason: A correctly translates "མང" (many) as "多個", which is entirely omitted in B.

atts.t:
無論安住於村莊或阿蘭若，
若遠離二乘之心並定於殊勝菩提，
此即趣入眾生利益者之遠離；
衡量彼等之菩薩即毀壞自身。

i.sp: 遠離二乘之心
i.ev: Tibetan "ཐེག་པ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་སེམས་བྲལ" uses བྲལ (be free of), not དབེན་པ; 遠離 is the locked rendering of དབེན་པ (seclusion), used in the next line, so the same word here blurs two different Tibetan terms.
i.fx: 離二乘之心

atts.t:
無論安住於村莊或阿蘭若，
若離二乘之心並定於殊勝菩提，
此即趣入眾生利益者之遠離；
衡量彼等之菩薩即毀壞自身。

judge.reason: B correctly reserves the locked term "遠離" for "དབེན་པ", using "離" for "བྲལ" (free from), whereas A misapplies the locked term.

atts.t:
極度飢餓之有情希求於飲食，
具貪著輪迴之心者恆常流轉，
我與我之法二者不真實且空，
愚夫卻憑藉自身於虛空中打結。

i.sp: 極度飢餓之有情希求於飲食
i.ev: Tibetan has སེམས་ཅན་ཡོངས་སུ་ལྟོགས་པ་ཟས་ལ་འདོད་བྱེད་, but all three commentaries read the word as full conceptualisation/misconception, not physical hunger: bo-mipham 5-16 "ཚུལ་བཞིན་མ་ཡིན་པའི་ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོག་པ་ཅན་དུ་གྱུར་པ ... འདོད་པའི་ཡོན་ཏན་གྱི་ཟས་ལ་འདོད་པ་སྐྱེ་བར་བྱེད", bo-rangjung 5-16 "ཡོངས་སུ་རྟོགས་པས་འདོད་ཡོན་གྱི་ཟས་ལ་འདོད་པར་བྱེད", bo-khenrab 5-16 similar; the Sanskrit has parikalpayamāna (conceptualising) and the approved English reads "fully conceptualizing". "Food" is the food of sense pleasures, not literal food; the translation instead says beings are extremely hungry.
i.fx: 有情由全面分別計執而貪求（欲樂之）食

atts.t:
有情由全面分別計執而貪求於食，
具貪著輪迴之心者恆常流轉，
我與我之法二者不真實且空，
愚夫卻憑藉自身於虛空中打結。

i.sp: 愚夫卻憑藉自身於虛空中打結
i.ev: Tibetan བྱིས་པ་བདག་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་ནི་མཁའ་ལ་མདུད་པ་བོར། means the fool, of his own accord / himself, ties knots in the sky (Mipham 5-16: བྱིས་པ་བདག་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་ནི་མེད་པ་ལ་ཡོད་པར་བཟུང་བ). 憑藉自身 reads as 'by means of oneself' (instrumental), which blurs the reflexive emphasis.
i.fx: 愚夫卻自己於虛空中打結

judge.reason: A follows the commentary's correction of "ལྟོགས་པ" (hungry) to "རྟོག་པ" (conceptualizing), matching the intended meaning.

atts.t:
譬如因疑慮之想而引發中毒，
縱使彼毒未入體內亦會昏厥；
愚夫如是主張有我與我所，
憑藉彼我之想，實為無常，而歷經生死。

i.sp: 因疑慮之想而引發中毒
i.ev: Tibetan དོགས་པའི་འདུ་ཤེས་ཀྱིས་ནི་དུག་བསླང་བ with next line "the poison has not gone inside". bo-mipham 5-17: "དུག་ཁོང་དུ་སོང་ངོ་སྙམ་དུ་དུག་གི་རྟོག་པ་མངོན་གྱུར་དུ་སྐྱེས་པ" and bo-khenrab 5-17 "དུག་ཁོང་དུ་སོང་ངོ་སྙམ་པའི་རྣམ་རྟོག་མངོན་གྱུར་སྐྱེས": the thought of having taken poison arises. "引發中毒" can be read as actually causing poisoning, which the next line denies.
i.fx: 因疑慮之想而生起已中毒之念

i.sp: 實為無常
i.ev: Tibetan ཡང་དག་མི་རྟག་ is glossed by the commentaries as an unreal (ཡང་དག་པ་མིན་པ) perception/conception of self: bo-mipham 5-17 "བདག་ཅེས་བྱ་བའི་ཡུལ་དེར་འདུ་ཤེས་པ་ཡང་དག་པ་མིན་པའི་རྟོག་པ་འབྱུང་ཞིང་དེའི་དབང་གིས་སྲིད་པར་སྐྱེ་ཞིང་འཆི་བ", bo-khenrab 5-17 "ཡང་དག་པ་མིན་པའི་ཀུན་རྟོག"; Sanskrit has sadā abhūto (constantly, unreal). The Chinese "實為無常" has no clear subject and drops the point that the self-perception is unreal, replacing it with "truly impermanent".
i.fx: 憑藉對彼我之不真實想，於無常中不斷生死

atts.t:
譬如因疑慮之想而生起已中毒之念，
縱使彼毒未入體內亦會昏厥；
愚夫如是主張有我與我所，
憑藉對彼我之不真實想，於無常中不斷生死。

judge.reason: B correctly translates "དུག་བསླང་བ" as arising the thought of poisoning, matching the commentary, whereas A implies actual physical poisoning.

atts.t:
正如具有執取，如是即被宣說為雜染；
對我與我所無所緣，則被宣說為清淨；
於此無有任何法轉為煩惱或完全清淨，
菩薩如是了達般若波羅蜜多。

i.sp: 於此無有任何法轉為煩惱或完全清淨
i.ev: Tibetan འདི་ལ་གང་ཡང་ཉོན་མོངས་རྣམ་དག་འགྱུར་མེད་པར; ཉོན་མོངས་ is a verb (be afflicted), and the agent is a person: bo-mipham 5-18 "གང་ཟག་གང་ཡང་ཉོན་མོངས་པར་གྱུར་པ་དང་ ... རྣམ་པར་དག་པ་ཉིད་དུ་འགྱུར་བ་ཡང་མེད་པར"; Sanskrit kaścid yo kliśyate śudhyate vā. The Chinese makes a "法" turn into 煩惱 (a noun), which shifts the referent and the sense.
i.fx: 於此無有任何者被煩惱所染或成為完全清淨

atts.t:
正如具有執取，如是即被宣說為雜染；
對我與我所無所緣，則被宣說為清淨；
