Whatever teaching the listeners of the Victorious One share, they explain it clearly with good reasons. Their words bring great joy and good results. All of this comes from the power of the Thus-Gone One.

i.sp: Their words bring great joy and good results.
i.ev: Dharma 'producing supreme noble bliss and attaining its fruit' (the practice yields noble bliss and its fruit); not that the words bring joy
i.fx: Following it brings noble joy and its good results.

atts.t: They also ask, "What is this wisdom? Whose is it? Where does it come from?" They see that all these things are empty. They look at them closely without feeling sad or afraid. That awakening hero is close to awakening.

i.sp: without feeling sad or afraid
i.ev: 'without discouragement or fear' (not losing heart)
i.fx: without losing heart or being afraid

atts.t: Others do not practice in form, feeling, idea, or intention. They do not practice in awareness. They practice without staying anywhere. They do not grasp at what is called "practicing." Instead, they rely on wisdom. With a mind that knows what is never born, they touch the highest, peaceful deep calm.

i.sp: Others do not practice in form
i.ev: 'Whoever does not practice in form...' refers to the same bodhisattva type described; 'Others' wrongly suggests a different group
i.fx: Whoever does not practice in form, feeling, idea, or intention

atts.t: By practicing like this, they practice the wisdom of the Well-Gone Ones. They truly understand that not practicing is the real practice. They do not grasp at any of the things they practice. This is the practice of the highest perfect wisdom.

i.sp: They truly understand that not practicing is the real practice.
i.ev: 'Because they thoroughly understand that non-practice is the practice': the understanding is the reason they practice the wisdom of the Sugatas; 'real' is added
i.fx: They practice the wisdom of the Well-Gone Ones because they fully understand that not practicing is the practice.

atts.t: You might ask, "Why is this person called an awakening hero?" They cut off clinging. They want to completely end clinging to everything. They touch the awakening of a Victorious One, which is a state of not clinging. Because of this, they get the name awakening hero.

i.sp: the awakening of a Victorious One
i.ev: 'the unattached awakening of the Victors' (plural)
i.fx: the awakening of the Victorious Ones, which is free of clinging

atts.t: Imagine a magician creates a fake crowd at a crossroads and then cuts off all their heads. The awakening hero knows that all beings are just like those illusions. Because they know this, the awakening hero has no fear.

i.sp: cuts off all their heads
i.ev: 'tens of millions of heads of a large crowd of people'
i.fx: cuts off millions of heads from a huge crowd

i.sp: just like those illusions
i.ev: beings are known 'to be like emanations' (conjured appearances), not 'illusion' (sgyu ma)
i.fx: just like those conjured people

atts.t: Form, idea, feeling, intention, and awareness are not tied up or set free. They do not truly exist. You must enter into awakening this way without losing heart. This is the best armor for holy persons.

i.sp: You must enter into awakening this way
i.ev: 'Entering into awakening in this way without a discouraged mind, this is the supreme armor' (a description, not a command)
i.fx: Entering into awakening this way without losing heart is the best armor for holy persons.

atts.t: Someone might hold the idea of living beings and the idea of suffering. They might think, "I will help beings and end their suffering." That makes them an awakening hero who only imagines a self and living beings. This is not the practice of highest perfect wisdom.

i.sp: only imagines a self and living beings
i.ev: 'a bodhisattva who conceptualizes self and sentient beings' (clings to them as real); 'only imagines' may suggest beings do not exist at all
i.fx: who holds on to the idea of a self and of living beings

atts.t: You should know that all living beings are just like the self. Know that all things are just like all living beings. Do not think about arising or no arising. This is the practice of highest perfect wisdom.

i.sp: Do not think about arising or no arising.
i.ev: Academic: 'Not conceptualizing either non-arising or arising' - the point is not holding a fixed idea, not refusing to think.
i.fx: Do not hold on to any fixed idea about arising or no arising.

atts.t: Any awakening hero who practices this way without doubt has true wisdom. You should know they rest in sameness. They completely understand that all things are with no nature of their own. This is the practice of highest perfect wisdom.

i.sp: all things are with no nature of their own
i.ev: Locked term 'with no nature of its own' is forced into an ungrammatical clause; academic: 'phenomena are devoid of intrinsic nature'.
i.fx: They completely understand that all things have no nature of their own.

terms: with no nature of its own

atts.t: The Guide does not stay in the realm not made by causes. He also does not stay in things made by causes. He practices by not staying anywhere. In the same way, an awakening hero rests on a base through a stay without staying. The Victorious One taught that a stay without staying is the true way to stay.

i.sp: rests on a base through a stay without staying
i.ev: Academic: 'abides in a basis by abiding without abiding'; the children's phrase is tangled and 'the true way to stay' adds 'true'.
i.fx: In the same way, an awakening hero rests on a base by a stay without staying. The Victorious One taught that this stay without staying is how to stay.

atts.t: Some people wish to be a listener of the Well-Gone One. Others wish to become a solitary Buddha. Some wish to be a King of the Teaching, a Buddha. But they cannot reach these goals without relying on this patience. It is like trying to cross a river without finding a way to the other shore.

i.sp: trying to cross a river
i.ev: Academic: 'one sees no crossing to go from this shore to the other' - no river is mentioned.
i.fx: It is like not seeing any way to cross from this shore to the other shore.

atts.t: When I spoke the truth of this highest perfection, the highest being of the past spoke to me. He said, 'In the future, you will become a Buddha.' I received this prediction. This is what the Victorious One said.

i.sp: When I spoke the truth of this highest perfection
i.ev: Academic: 'When I spoke in conformity with this supreme perfection' (Tib. mthun par smra) - speaking in accord with it, not 'the truth of' it.
i.fx: When I spoke in line with this highest perfection

atts.t: The Protectors practice this perfect wisdom. This perfection keeps people safe. If anyone respects, remembers, and truly understands it, they will not be hurt by poison, weapons, fire, or water. Mara and Mara's side will never find a chance to harm them.

i.sp: This perfection keeps people safe.
i.ev: Not in the text; protection is stated only for whoever respects, retains and understands it, in the next clause.
i.fx: The Protectors practice this perfect wisdom. Anyone who respects, remembers, and truly understands it will not be hurt by poison, weapons, fire, or water.

atts.t: Imagine all the living beings in those endless millions of lands do no other work. Instead, they make offerings for an age or longer. They offer heavenly flowers, sweet incense, and oils in the past, present and future.

i.sp: in the past, present and future
i.ev: Academic: offerings 'at the three times of each day' (three times a day); the locked term 'past, present and future' conflicts with the context. Also 'sweet incense' for 'supreme incense'.
i.fx: They offer heavenly flowers, the best incense, and oils three times every day.

atts.t: The perfect wisdom of the Victorious Ones is a great spell of knowledge. These words of knowing calm the sadness and suffering in every realm of living beings. Every Protector of the World from the past and in the ten directions trained in this perfection. By learning it, each became a perfect doctor and an unsurpassed king of healers.

i.sp: in every realm of living beings
i.ev: Academic: 'the many realms of sentient beings', not every realm.
i.fx: in the many realms of living beings

i.sp: each became a perfect doctor and an unsurpassed king of healers
i.ev: Academic: only 'unsurpassed kings of physicians'; 'perfect doctor' is an added second title.
i.fx: each became an unsurpassed king of healers.

atts.t: For example, there are billions of trees in Jambudvipa. They have many different forms and kinds. We might talk about counting their many shadows. But the shadows themselves are not really different from one another.

i.sp: But the shadows themselves are not really different from one another.
i.ev: Says there are no diverse shadows, nor any differences, except as a spoken number of shadows; the children's text drops the claim that varied shadows do not exist.
i.fx: The trees have many kinds and shapes. But the shadows are not many different kinds. They are only counted and named as many.

atts.t: Imagine someone travels to lands as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges. They help all the living beings there become a worthy one. But suppose someone else writes down this perfect wisdom and gives the book to a great person. That second person earns much more stored-up goodness. Sharing this perfection of wisdom is much better.

i.sp: Sharing this perfection of wisdom is much better.
i.ev: The verse only says that the one who writes the text and gives it to a supreme being has far more merit; it does not generalize to 'sharing' as such.
i.fx: The person who writes it down and gives it to a great person earns much more stored-up goodness.

atts.t: If a tree has no sprout, it will never grow in the world. Without a tree, how could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit ever appear? It is the same without the wish to awaken. Without it, a Victorious One would never appear in the world. And without their awakening, how could the good fruits, like Shakra, Brahma, and the listeners, ever appear?

i.sp: Without a tree, how could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit ever appear?
i.ev: The question is: without a sprout, a tree never emerges, so how could branches, leaves, flowers and fruits emerge on it? The children's text replaces the sprout with the tree, losing the sprout-to-tree analogy for the wish to awaken.
i.fx: If a tree has no sprout, it never grows in the world. Then how could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit ever appear on it?

i.sp: And without their awakening, how could the good fruits, like Shakra, Brahma, and the listeners, ever appear?
i.ev: The analogy is: without the mind of awakening (wish to awaken), a Victor does not emerge, so how could the fruits (Shakra, Brahma, listeners) emerge. The children's text swaps the wish to awaken for 'their awakening' and adds 'good'.
i.fx: And without the wish to awaken, a Victorious One does not appear, so how could the fruits, like Shakra, Brahma, and the listeners, ever appear?

atts.t: If there is no sprout, a tree could never grow in the world. Without a tree, how could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit ever appear? In the same way, without the wish to awaken, a Victorious One would never appear in the world. Without a Victorious One, how could the fruits—like Shakra, Brahma, and listeners—ever appear?

i.sp: Without a Victorious One, how could the fruits—like Shakra, Brahma, and listeners—ever appear?
i.ev: The text says: without the mind of awakening, how could the fruits (Shakra, Brahma, and shravakas) emerge. The fruits depend on the wish to awaken, not on the Victorious One as a middle step; the second question is parallel to the first (sprout / tree-and-fruit).
i.fx: In the same way, without the wish to awaken, a Victorious One would never appear in the world. So how could the fruits—Shakra, Brahma, and listeners—ever appear?

atts.t: When the sun shines its light, living beings go to work. It is the same when wise people bring the wish to awaken into the world. They do this to know true awakening. Because of their deep knowing, living beings gain every good quality and wonderful quality.

i.sp: They do this to know true awakening.
i.ev: The text says only 'in order to know' (ཤེས་ཕྱིར); it names no object such as 'true awakening'.
i.fx: They do this in order to know.

i.sp: living beings gain every good quality and wonderful quality
i.ev: Sentient beings become endowed with qualities; 'every' overstates it and 'good quality and wonderful quality' doubles the one compound ཡོན་ཏན་ཆོས.
i.fx: living beings come to have good qualities.

atts.t: All the listeners might gather a huge pile of stored-up goodness. They build this through generosity, good conduct, and meditation. But an awakening hero only needs a single thought to rejoice. The stored-up goodness of all those listeners cannot match a tiny part of the awakening hero's rejoicing.

i.sp: But an awakening hero only needs a single thought to rejoice.
i.ev: The comparison is of merit: the shravakas' heap of merit cannot match a fraction of a bodhisattva's single mind of rejoicing. 'Only needs' turns the comparison into a claim about what the hero needs.
i.fx: But compare this with the single thought of rejoicing of an awakening hero.

atts.t: Think of the billions of Buddhas from the past. Think of those living right now in endless millions of lands. Think of all the Protectors of the world who have passed into the peace beyond sorrow. They all share the jewel teaching to end suffering.

i.sp: billions of Buddhas from the past
i.ev: The Tibetan gives a vast number, tens of millions of hundreds of billions, so 'billions' understates it.
i.fx: countless Buddhas from the past

atts.t: If you make a sign of it, you do not really dedicate it. But if there are no signs, it is the dedication to awakening. Think of eating excellent food that is mixed with poison. The Victorious One taught that seeing good things or any quality as something to hold onto is just like that.

i.sp: seeing good things or any quality as something to hold onto
i.ev: Only the apprehension of virtuous (white) qualities (དཀར་པོའི་ཆོས) is likened to poisoned food; 'or any quality' widens it.
i.fx: holding onto good things as something real to hold onto

atts.t: If you dedicate stored-up goodness to awakening like this, it has no poison. You stay close to the Buddha. You speak exactly what the Victorious One has said. A hero who dedicates in this way shines very bright. They outshine every awakening hero in the world who is one who holds onto something.

i.sp: You stay close to the Buddha.
i.ev: The text says one does not abandon the Buddha (སངས་རྒྱས་མི་སྤོང).
i.fx: You do not abandon the Buddha.

atts.t: Imagine millions of blind people with no guide. They do not even know the path. How could they ever find the city? Without wisdom, these five perfections have no eyes. Because they have no guide, they cannot reach awakening.

i.sp: millions of blind people
i.ev: The Tibetan gives tens of millions of hundreds of billions of blind people; the number is understated.
i.fx: countless blind people

atts.t: Someone might think, "I will practice the wisdom of the Victorious One. I will free billions of living beings touched by suffering." An awakening hero seeking awakening who holds onto the idea of living beings is not practicing the highest perfection, perfect wisdom.

i.sp: An awakening hero seeking awakening who holds onto the idea of living beings is not practicing
i.ev: The bodhisattva who thinks 'I shall liberate many beings' is the one who conceptually constructs the perception of sentient beings; the children's text separates the thought from the fault and says 'Victorious One' for 'Victors'.
i.fx: An awakening hero who thinks like this is building up an idea of living beings in their mind. This is not practicing the highest perfection, perfect wisdom.

atts.t: These beings are stuck in the mud of name and form. They wander in the cycle of rebirth like a spinning wheel of wind. Confused beings are like deer caught in a trap. But those with wisdom fly freely like birds in the sky.

i.sp: But those with wisdom fly freely like birds in the sky.
i.ev: The wise roam freely because they know beings are like deer caught in a snare; the 'knowing' is dropped.
i.fx: Knowing that confused beings are like deer caught in a trap, those with wisdom fly freely like birds in the sky.

atts.t: All things are totally pure and pure by nature. When an awakening hero looks through perfect wisdom, they do not find a doer. They also do not find things. This is the highest practice of perfect wisdom.

i.sp: They also do not find things.
i.ev: Text says they do not apprehend all phenomena (ཆོས་ཀུན་, 'all things'); 'all' is lost.
i.fx: They do not find any of the things either.

atts.t: Some living beings hear that these things are like magic creations and illusions. They have no doubt. They keep working at their training. You should know they entered the Great Vehicle long ago. They have already served billions of Buddhas.

i.sp: They have already served billions of Buddhas.
i.ev: 'Many tens of billions' of Buddhas (བྱེ་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་མང་), not simply billions.
i.fx: They have served many, many billions of Buddhas.

atts.t: Imagine a person walking on a wild path for many leagues. Then they see beautiful forests where the cowherds work. They think, "These are signs that a village or city is near." They feel relieved and have no fear of robbers.

i.sp: beautiful forests where the cowherds work
i.ev: Excellent forests at the cowherds' boundary (མཚམས), i.e. the edge of their land, not where they work.
i.fx: beautiful forests at the edge of the cowherds' land

atts.t: Just like that, those who fully enter the highest awakening hear this perfect wisdom of the Victorious Ones. The Guide may not have given them a direct prediction yet. But they still know, "Before long, I will touch a Buddha's awakening."

i.sp: those who fully enter the highest awakening hear this perfect wisdom
i.ev: Such people 'should be known as hearing' this perfect wisdom (རིག་པར་བྱ); the 'should be known' is lost.
i.fx: You should know that those who fully enter the highest awakening are hearing this perfect wisdom of the Victorious Ones.

atts.t: If people do not know this, they throw away the root. In their confusion, they look for branches and leaves instead. This is like finding an elephant and then looking for its footprints. Hearing the perfect wisdom and then searching for other scriptures is exactly like that.

i.sp: searching for other scriptures
i.ev: Text says searching for sutras (མདོ་ཚོལ); 'other' is not there.
i.fx: searching for scriptures

atts.t: Some people only desire respect and gain. Their minds want to view outside things, so they spend too much time with households. They throw away the teaching and do things against the teaching. They leave the path and walk on a wrong path. This is Mara's work.

They will want respect and gain. With a mind wanting to look around, they will become close to householders. After leaving the teaching, they will do things against the teaching. Leaving the path and going on a wrong path is Mara's work.

Priceless jewels are very hard to find. They are rare, and they are always in danger. It is the same with the perfect wisdom of the Victorious Ones. This precious teaching is also rare and always in danger.

i.sp: always in danger
i.ev: Text says 'always subject to much harm' (འཚེ་བ), i.e. often harmed, not merely in danger.
i.fx: often harmed

atts.t: When a mother with many children gets sick, they all feel sad and take care of her. In the same way, the Buddhas of the worlds in the ten directions keep this holy wisdom in mind. She is their Mother in every world system.

i.sp: She is their Mother in every world system.
i.ev: Wisdom 'who has become their Mother' (ཡུམ་གྱུར); 'in every world system' is not said of the Mother.
i.fx: She has become their Mother.

terms: Buddhas of the worlds in the ten directions

atts.t: Guides with the ten powers rely on perfect wisdom as a beautiful garden. This is their home. They completely save living beings from suffering and the three lower realms. Even so, they never hold the idea of living beings.

i.sp: This is their home.
i.ev: The Guides have the perfection of wisdom as their domain (their range of activity), not a home.
i.fx: Perfect wisdom is the place where they move and work, like a beautiful garden.

atts.t: Think of the sun shining in the sky. Its rays dry up the earth and perfectly show all forms. In the same way, the King of the Teaching relies on perfect wisdom. He dries up the river of craving and strong wanting. He perfectly shows the teaching.

i.sp: the river of craving and strong wanting
i.ev: The text has only the river of craving (srid pa'i chu klung); 'strong wanting' is a gloss of the same word, not a second thing.
i.fx: He dries up the river of craving, which is strong wanting.

atts.t: A king might not visit the towns and lands of his kingdom. But he still collects all the wealth from his country. The true nature of things for an awakening hero is like that. It does not go anywhere, but it gathers every good quality of the level of a Buddha.

i.sp: A king might not visit the towns and lands of his kingdom.
i.ev: The king does not go to the villages or provinces; it is a fact, not a possibility.
i.fx: A king does not go to the towns and lands of his kingdom.

atts.t: This is how you should teach a beginner. Tell them, "Dedicate generosity, good conduct, patience, and steady effort to awakening! Dedicate deep focus and wisdom to awakening, too! Do not hold on to the heaps of awakening. Do not have any clinging to the supreme!"

i.sp: Do not hold on to the heaps of awakening. Do not have any clinging to the supreme!
i.ev: One single instruction: do not cling to the supreme by being attached to the aggregates of awakening. Splitting it into two commands loses the 'by' link.
i.fx: Do not cling to the supreme by holding on to the heaps of awakening!

atts.t: Those who practice like this are oceans of goodness. They are moons among speakers. They are the refuge, the defender, and the dwelling place for beings. They are the support, the mind, and the island. They are Guides who help everyone. They are bright lamps who stay completely calm. They speak the highest teaching.

i.sp: They are bright lamps who stay completely calm. They speak the highest teaching.
i.ev: 'Illuminators' is dropped, and 'imperturbable' belongs to the speakers of the supreme Dharma, not to the lamps.
i.fx: They light up the way and are lamps. They speak the highest teaching and cannot be shaken.

atts.t: These famous heroes put on armor for hard deeds. This is not the armor of the heaps, elements, and sense doors. They are free from the idea of the three vehicles. They have no holding on. They are never turning back. They never waver, and their nature is perfectly calm.

i.sp: They are never turning back.
i.ev: Ungrammatical use of the locked phrase; the Tibetan says they are irreversible.
i.fx: They are ones who never turn back.

i.sp: These famous heroes
i.ev: 'Those of great renown'; 'heroes' is added and may be confused with 'awakening hero'.
i.fx: These very famous ones put on armor for hard deeds.

atts.t: This teaching of the Guides is deep and hard to see. No one can just figure it out or reach it. So, when the Kind Helper reached awakening, he paused. He thought, "Who among all the living beings will understand this?"

i.sp: No one can just figure it out or reach it.
i.ev: No one realizes it, and there is no attaining of it. The children's text turns 'not realized/no attaining' into 'cannot easily figure out or reach', which changes the logic.
i.fx: No one has realized it, and there is nothing to be reached.

i.sp: he paused
i.ev: He felt little inclination (to teach), thinking no one would understand.
i.fx: he felt little wish to teach

atts.t: This teaching of the Guides is deep and hard to see. No one has realized it, and there is nothing to be reached. So, when the Kind Helper reached awakening, he paused. He thought, "Who among all the living beings will understand this?"

i.sp: there is nothing to be reached
i.ev: Academic: 'It is not realized by anyone, nor is there any attaining of it' - no one attains it. The children's wording says there is no thing to attain, a different claim (and one that could be read as a doctrinal statement the verse does not make).
i.fx: No one has realized it, and no one has reached it.

i.sp: he paused
i.ev: Academic: the Kind Helper 'felt little inclination' (to teach), thinking 'Who among the masses of sentient beings will understand?' - a reluctance, not just a pause.
i.fx: he felt little wish to teach it.

atts.t: This teaching of the Guides is deep and hard to see. No one has realized it, and no one has reached it. So, when the Kind Helper reached awakening, he paused. He thought, "Who among all the living beings will understand this?"

i.sp: he paused
i.ev: The Kind Helper 'felt little inclination' (to teach), thinking no one would understand; 'paused' loses the sense of reluctance.
i.fx: he felt little wish to teach it. He thought, "Who among all the living beings will understand this?"

atts.t: They teach the teaching to beings without wanting any reward. They find great joy in the teaching. They always speak gentle words. They are staying alert while going, walking, sleeping, and sitting. They walk looking ahead only the length of a yoke. Their minds are free from confusion.

i.sp: looking ahead only the length of a yoke
i.ev: A yoke (a wooden bar for oxen) is an unexplained hard word; the text means they look only a short distance ahead.
i.fx: They walk looking only a short way ahead, about as far as the wooden bar that goes across an ox's neck.

atts.t: They make themselves clean and wear clean clothes. The three are kept quiet and pure. These great leaders do not want to gain things. They always want the teaching. They have passed beyond the world of Mara. They do not depend on anyone else. They practice the four kinds of deep focus, but they do not stay stuck in that deep focus.

i.sp: The three are kept quiet and pure.
i.ev: Academic: 'the three are isolated and pure'; 'the three' is unexplained and 'kept quiet' is imprecise for 'secluded'.
i.fx: They live apart from the crowd, and their body, speech and mind are pure.

atts.t: They stay completely away from any rough borderland. They have no doubts about their path. They always stand as firm as Mount Meru. They would even give up their lives for the teaching. They work very hard at their training. You should know these are the signs of never turning back.

i.sp: They have no doubts about their path.
i.ev: Academic: 'without doubt about their own stage' (their own level of realization), not their path.
i.fx: They have no doubt about their own stage of practice.

atts.t: Think of an awakening hero who has become this deep. They ride in the highest, free vehicle. In the deepest truth, no heap, element, or sense door exists. When they understand this teaching, they perfect their stored-up goodness. What stored-up goodness could ever be greater than theirs?

i.sp: They ride in the highest, free vehicle. ... When they understand this teaching, they perfect their stored-up goodness.
i.ev: Academic: 'the ultimate, unattached vehicle' and the bodhisattva who realizes this Dharma; the text does not say they 'perfect' goodness by understanding, it asks what accomplished merit exceeds theirs.
i.fx: They ride in the deepest, unattached vehicle. Anyone who understands this teaching has stored-up goodness that nothing can beat.

atts.t: People talk about the perfection of the Victorious Ones. But even those things are said to be just a name. An awakening hero must dedicate their goodness without any self-importance. Then they will not fall back, and they will reach the highest awakening of a Buddha.

i.sp: An awakening hero must dedicate their goodness without any self-importance.
i.ev: Academic: 'A bodhisattva who dedicates without conceit will not decline' (a description, not a command).
i.fx: An awakening hero who dedicates without any self-importance will not fall back.

atts.t: A seed grows into a sprout, then a flower, and then fruit. When the seed is gone, the tree is still there. In the same way, the first thought in your mind is the cause of awakening. When that first thought is gone, it does not mean awakening is gone.

i.sp: it does not mean awakening is gone
i.ev: Academic: 'it is not that awakening is absent' (awakening is not nonexistent), not that something present has vanished.
i.fx: When that first thought has ended, it does not mean there is no awakening.

atts.t: Drop by drop, a vase slowly fills with water. In the same way, the first thought in your mind is the cause of the highest awakening. By slowly building up every good quality, you perfect the quality of goodness and become a Buddha.

i.sp: By slowly building up every good quality, you perfect the quality of goodness
i.ev: Academic: 'by gradually perfecting virtuous qualities, one becomes a Buddha'; the children's line is redundant and tangled.
i.fx: By slowly building up the qualities of goodness, you become a Buddha.

atts.t: They practice the things of emptiness, being without signs, and without wishes. They do not touch peace beyond sorrow, and they do not follow signs. They are like a skilled boatman going back and forth. He does not stay on either shore, and he does not stay in the ocean.

i.sp: They practice the things of emptiness, being without signs, and without wishes.
i.ev: Academic: 'the phenomena of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness'; 'the things of emptiness' is awkward for ages 8-12.
i.fx: They practice emptiness, being without signs, and being without wishes.

atts.t: An awakening hero who practices this way is not proud. They do not think, "I will get a prediction from the ten powers and I will touch awakening." They are also not afraid of awakening. They do not think, "There is nothing here at all." To practice this way is to practice the wisdom of the Well-Gone Ones.

i.sp: They are also not afraid of awakening. They do not think, "There is nothing here at all."
i.ev: Academic: 'nor do they fear awakening, thinking "There is nothing at all here"'; the thought is the cause of the fear, not something they refuse to think.
i.fx: They are also not afraid of awakening, thinking, "There is nothing here at all."

atts.t: This person takes his father, mother, and wife on a journey. They walk on a wild path full of enemies. The skilled person magically makes many brave men to protect them. They travel safely and return home again. It is just like that.

i.sp: to protect them
i.ev: The text only says he emanates many brave men and travels safely; it does not state their purpose.
i.fx: The skilled person magically makes many brave men. They travel safely and return home again.

atts.t: In the same way, the clever awakening hero grows great compassion for the whole realm of living beings. They completely pass beyond the four Maras and the two lower levels. They stay in the highest deep calm. Yet, they do not touch awakening.

i.sp: two lower levels
i.ev: Academic: 'the two levels' (not described as lower).
i.fx: They completely pass beyond the four Maras and the two levels.

atts.t: In the same way, the awakening hero rests in emptiness. They are held up by a wish that understands living beings among all beings. They show many different actions. They do not touch peace beyond sorrow. They also do not just stay in emptiness.

i.sp: They also do not just stay in emptiness.
i.ev: Academic: 'does not abide in emptiness' (plain negation, no 'just').
i.fx: They do not touch peace beyond sorrow, and they do not stay in emptiness.

atts.t: A skilled and bright awakening hero practices this highest deep calm of peaceful emptiness. At that time, they do not build up signs. Resting without signs, they practice pure and perfect peace.

i.sp: pure and perfect peace
i.ev: Academic: 'peace, utter peace' (no idea of purity).
i.fx: they practice peace, complete peace.

atts.t: Think of a merchant who travels to learn the route. They visit every city, town, and village along the way. They do not stay there, and they do not stay on the jewel island. This wise person does not stay at home either, but becomes skilled in the path.

i.ev: Academic: the merchant is 'seeking profit' and goes to learn the route.
i.fx: Think of a merchant who wants to gain wealth and travels to learn the route.

atts.t: These heroes connect with beings through loving-kindness. They practice the deep calm of emptiness, being without signs, and without wishes. Could anyone say they will just reach a peace beyond sorrow? Or that they are made by causes? That is impossible.

i.sp: Could anyone say they will just reach a peace beyond sorrow?
i.ev: Academic: 'Could it be designated that they will attain nirvana'; no 'just'.
i.fx: Could anyone say they will reach peace beyond sorrow?

atts.t: There are many harmful spirits and sicknesses in the human world. A person with compassion can calm them through the blessing of truth. Even so, they feel no self-importance and do not show pride. You should know they have a prediction of never turning back.

i.sp: A person with compassion
i.ev: Academic: 'those endowed with benefit and compassion'; the benefit to others is dropped.
i.fx: A person with kindness and compassion who wants to help others can calm them through the blessing of truth.

atts.t: Mara might approach you and use names to trick you. He will say, 'These are the names of you and your parents. These are the names of your ancestors for seven generations. When you become a Buddha, this will be your name.'

i.sp: use names to trick you
i.ev: Academic: 'Mara approaches on the basis of names'; no stated aim of tricking.
i.fx: Mara might come to you and speak about names.

atts.t: Mara will tell you about your strict practices and your training. He will say, 'You had these same good qualities in the past.' An awakening hero might hear this and feel self-importance. If they do, they are being pushed by Mara and have little understanding.

i.sp: Mara will tell you about your strict practices and your training.
i.ev: Academic: practices and training 'you will come to possess' (future), plus 'conduct'.
i.fx: Mara will tell you about the strict practices and training you will have. He will say, 'You had these same good qualities and conduct before.'

atts.t: A person might live in a village or in a forest. If they are free from the mind of the two vehicles and sure of the highest awakening, this is the quiet aloneness of those who work for the good of beings. An awakening hero who judges them only ruins themselves.

i.sp: free from the mind of the two vehicles
i.ev: Free from the mind of the two vehicles (the arhat and solitary Buddha paths); 'two vehicles' is unexplained for ages 8-12.
i.fx: free from wanting only to become a worthy one or a solitary Buddha, and sure of the highest awakening

atts.t: Where there is clinging, I teach there is complete mental trouble. When you do not find self and what belongs to self, this is becoming completely clean. In truth, nothing gets mental trouble or becomes pure. Knowing this, the awakening hero realizes perfect wisdom.

i.sp: I teach
i.ev: 'Just as there is grasping, so is complete affliction taught' - passive, no first-person speaker.
i.fx: Where there is clinging, complete mental trouble is taught.

terms: self and what belongs to self

atts.t: Imagine every single one of the living beings in Jambudvipa. Suppose they all form the wish for highest awakening. Suppose they practice generosity for millions of years. Then they dedicate all this as a cause of awakening to help beings.

i.sp: for millions of years
i.ev: 'many tens of millions of millennia' (thousands of years times tens of millions); the length is greatly understated.
i.fx: for countless thousands of years, over and over, for tens of millions of ages of a thousand years

terms: form the wish for highest awakening

atts.t: An awakening hero wants to set free the living beings in the god and human worlds and the three lower realms. To show these living beings the wide path to the other shore, they must strive day and night in perfect wisdom.

i.ev: The beings are 'long connected here' to the bodhisattva (ཡུན་རིང་འབྲེལ་པ).
i.fx: An awakening hero who has long been connected with the living beings of the god and human worlds and the three lower realms wants to set them free.

atts.t: Suppose an awakening hero who has not yet received a prediction gets angry. If they start a fight with one who has received a prediction, they lose time. For every single moment they hold onto this bad thought, they must put on their armor and start over for that many ages.

i.sp: they lose time
i.ev: No such statement; the consequence is only that for as many moments as the barren thought lasts, that many ages they must put on the armor again from the beginning.
i.fx: If they start a fight with one who has received a prediction, then for every moment of this bad thought they must put on their armor and start over for that many ages.

atts.t: When doing their training, some might cling to the training itself, but that is not so here. They do not grasp at a learner or at the things to train in. They do not think of training and not training as two different things. Anyone who practices like this is training in a Buddha's qualities.

i.sp: They do not think of training and not training as two different things.
i.ev: The text says one does not conceptualize either of the two, training and non-training (མི་རྟོག); it does not say they are not seen as two different things.
i.fx: They do not hold on to the ideas of training or not training.

i.sp: some might cling to the training itself, but that is not so here
i.ev: Text says whoever trains does not assert any training at all; no contrast with others who cling is made.
i.fx: When someone trains, they do not hold on to any training at all.

atts.t: When doing their training, they do not cling to the training itself. They do not grasp at a learner or at the things to train in. They do not hold on to the ideas of training or not training. Anyone who practices like this is training in a Buddha's qualities.

Think of a person made by magic standing in a crowd. This illusion does not think, "I must make these people happy." But they do it anyway! People see them showing off many magic powers. Yet they have no body, no mind, and not even a name.

i.sp: showing off many magic powers
i.ev: Academic: 'displaying various miraculous powers' - neutral display; 'showing off' implies vanity, which clashes with the point that the illusory person has no wish to please or boast.
i.fx: People see them showing many magic powers.

atts.t: Think of all the living beings in worlds as many as the Ganges. Suppose they all decided to become Maras. Suppose each one made even more Maras from every single hair! Even then, they could not make obstacles for the wise.

i.sp: made even more Maras from every single hair
i.ev: Academic: 'emanated that many more from every single hair' - each hair makes as many Maras as there are beings, not just 'more'.
i.fx: Suppose from every single hair they made that many more Maras!

atts.t: This perfect wisdom is the Mother of the Thus-Gone Ones. When it is taught, an awakening hero might wish to learn it. If they try hard to master it with a true heart, you should know something about this noble person. They have stepped onto the path of knowing everything.

i.sp: you should know something about this noble person. They have stepped onto the path of knowing everything.
i.ev: Academic: 'That noble one should be known to have entered into omniscience' - the point is to recognise that they have entered into knowing everything.
i.fx: you should know that this noble person has entered into knowing everything.

atts.t: When practicing like this, a wise and bright awakening hero does not cling to the mind that understands. They do not cling to a Buddha's qualities. They do not grasp at a teacher, a person who wants the teaching, or someone with a certain view. This is how people live when they want peace and love every good quality.

i.sp: someone with a certain view
i.ev: Academic: 'one who views' (the one who looks/sees), not a person holding a particular view.
i.fx: or someone who sees

atts.t: A listener or a solitary Buddha can rest in deep calm. Their rest is very peaceful and full of joy. But the way an awakening hero rests is even better than all of those. It is the very best, beaten only by the freedom of a worthy one or a Thus-Gone One.

i.sp: the way an awakening hero rests
i.ev: Academic/Tibetan: 'this dwelling' with no named subject; the children's text supplies 'awakening hero' and, by listing a worthy one among the exceptions, sets up a confusing comparison with the listener's rest.
i.fx: This resting place is better than the deep-calm resting places of all listeners and solitary Buddhas. Only the freedom of worthy ones and Thus-Gone Ones is left out of this.

atts.t: This is the supreme treasure of teaching and the holy treasury of the teaching. It is the Buddha family. It is a treasury of happiness and joy for beings. The Protectors of the world live in the past, the future, and the ten directions. All of them are born from this. Yet the expanse of all things never runs out.

i.sp: The Protectors of the world live in the past, the future, and the ten directions.
i.ev: Academic: 'Protectors of the World of the past, the future, and the ten directions' - they are the Protectors of all times and places, not beings who 'live in the past'.
i.fx: The Protectors of the world from the past, the future, and all ten directions are all born from this.

atts.t: They might experience form, sound, smell, taste, and touch. They might fully enjoy these five pleasures of the senses. But they stay away from the vehicle of the worthy one and the solitary Buddha. Instead, they find joy in the wish to awaken. You should know this hero is always resting in steady stillness.

i.sp: They might fully enjoy these five pleasures of the senses. But they stay away from the vehicle of the worthy one and the solitary Buddha. Instead, they find joy in the wish to awaken. You should know this hero is always resting in steady stillness.
i.ev: The verse is conditional: even if they engage intensely in the five sense pleasures, IF they are free of the arhat/pratyekabuddha vehicle and delight in the mind of awakening, THEN the hero is to be known as constantly in equipoise. 'Intensely engage' is also not the same as 'enjoy'.
i.fx: Even if they work hard with form, sound, smell, taste, and touch, the five pleasures of the senses, they are free of the vehicle of the worthy one and the solitary Buddha, and they find joy in the wish to awaken. Then you should know this hero is always resting in steady stillness.

atts.t: The person who practices patience should also think like this: 'There is much suffering in hell, as an animal, and in the world of Yama. I have helplessly suffered harm while chasing a pleasure of the senses. Why should I not practice patience now for the sake of awakening?'

i.sp: while chasing a pleasure of the senses
i.ev: The harm is caused by (because of) the pleasures of the senses, experienced helplessly; the text does not say the person was actively chasing them, and it is an 'if I have helplessly suffered...' argument.
i.fx: If I have helplessly suffered harm because of the pleasures of the senses, why should I not practice patience now for the sake of awakening?

atts.t: Through good conduct, those who want peace become noble. They stay in the realm of the ten powers, and their good conduct is perfect. They follow all the actions of self-control. To help all living beings, they dedicate these actions to awakening.

i.sp: their good conduct is perfect
i.ev: 'their ethical discipline is unimpaired' (Tibetan ཉམས་པ་མེད: not damaged), not 'perfect'
i.fx: and their good conduct is never damaged

atts.t: Imagine all the living beings in the three kinds of life. What if every single one of them gave gifts to a Knower of the World? Imagine they gave gifts to the Buddhas, the worthy ones, and the solitary Buddhas. Imagine they did this for endless ages while trying to become a listener.

i.sp: What if every single one of them gave gifts to a Knower of the World? Imagine they gave gifts to the Buddhas, the worthy ones, and the solitary Buddhas.
i.ev: 'Knowers of the World' is another name for the Buddhas, worthy ones and solitary Buddhas, not a separate group of recipients
i.fx: What if every single one of them gave gifts to the Knowers of the World, the Buddhas, the worthy ones, and the solitary Buddhas?

i.ev: 'Taking them as the utmost extent of what can be conceived' (all beings that can be imagined) and 'properly seek' (ལེགས་ཚོལ)
i.fx: Imagine as many beings as anyone could possibly picture, all trying hard and properly to become a listener.

atts.t: Chapter seven teaches full awakening in one moment. That awakening hero has made all these things completely perfect.

Chapter Seven: Showing full awakening in one moment.

After fully perfecting these qualities, that awakening hero...

Chapter eight teaches the teaching body. The hero fully holds a perfectly pure land and pure living beings. They fully hold the line of Buddhas and the line of the teaching. They also fully hold the lineage of the community and all things.

Chapter Eight: Showing the teaching body.

They fully embrace a perfectly pure land and pure living beings. They fully embrace the line of Buddhas and the line of the teaching. In the same way, they fully embrace the lineage of the community and all qualities.
請你們帶著開心、恭敬和最大的信任。我們要消除阻礙和心裡的煩惱，洗淨一切的污垢。這是溫和的人為了眾生的好處而學習的圓滿的智慧。勇士們就是以此作為生活方式，你們要專心聽啊！

i.sp: 請你們帶著開心、恭敬和最大的信任。我們要消除阻礙和心裡的煩惱
i.ev: The verses describe the state of those who have generated joy, respect and supreme faith and eliminated obscurations and afflictions; the children's text turns this into a request to the listeners and a 'we must' resolve, shifting speaker and mood.
i.fx: 你們已經生起了開心、恭敬和最大的信任，也消除了阻礙和心裡的煩惱，超越了一切污垢。

atts.t:
得勝者的聽法的弟子們，無論講了多少佛法，
無論他們怎麼為大家解說，怎麼講述正確的道理，
甚至為大家帶來最棒的快樂，讓人得到美好的成果。
這一切，其實都是如來的神奇力量。

i.sp: 得勝者的聽法的弟子們
i.ev: Awkward stacked possessives ('得勝者的聽法的弟子們'); source says the Victor's hearers (śrāvakas) teach whatever Dharma.
i.fx: 得勝者的弟子們，也就是聽法的弟子，無論講了多少佛法，

atts.t:
我們找不到固定不變的形體和感受，
也找不到固定不變的想法和意願。
就連讓覺知停留的地方，也連一粒微塵那麼小都找不到。
菩薩不會停留在任何事物上，做事時心裡無拘無束。
因為什麼都不緊緊抓著不放，他就能得到走向安樂的人的覺悟。

i.sp: 固定不變的形體和感受
i.ev: Academic translation: form, feeling, perception and volition cannot be found; no qualifier 'fixed/unchanging' is in the text.
i.fx: 我們找不到形體和感受，也找不到想法和意願。

atts.t: 就像名叫先尼的四處遊走的求道者，他用他的智慧，把無法抓住的身心的組成部分徹底放下了。如果有哪位菩薩，也能這樣了解一切事物，他就不會急著進入超越憂傷的安寧，而是安穩地停留在智慧之中。

i.sp: 他就不會急著進入超越憂傷的安寧
i.ev: Academic: the bodhisattva does not touch/realize nirvana (and abides in wisdom); 'not hurrying to enter' turns a negation of touching nirvana into a timing matter and implies he will enter later.
i.fx: 他不會去碰觸超越憂傷的安寧，而是安穩地停留在智慧之中。

i.sp: 徹底放下了
i.ev: Academic: the unapprehendable aggregates are thoroughly destroyed/dissolved (rnam par 'jig pa), not merely 'let go of'.
i.fx: 徹底看穿並消除了那些抓不住的身心的組成部分

atts.t: 就像名叫先尼的四處遊走的求道者，他用他的智慧，把無法抓住的身心的組成部分徹底放下了。如果有哪位菩薩，也能這樣了解一切事物，他就不會去碰觸超越憂傷的安寧，而是安穩地停留在智慧之中。

i.sp: 徹底放下了
i.ev: The aggregates with no object of focus are utterly destroyed/dismantled (rnam par 'jig pa); '放下' (let go of) loses the sense of destruction.
i.fx: 把無法抓住的身心的組成部分徹底瓦解了

atts.t: 如果能這樣去做，就是在練習走向安樂的人的智慧。因為他深深明白，什麼都不去抓取，才是真正的練習。無論他練習什麼事物，都不會去執著。這就是在練習最棒的圓滿的智慧。

i.sp: 什麼都不去抓取，才是真正的練習
i.ev: Academic: he knows that 'non-practice is practice' (無所行持即是行持); the children's text replaces this with 'not grasping at anything is the real practice', losing the stated point.
i.fx: 因為他深深明白，沒有任何可練習的東西，這樣才是真正的練習。

atts.t: 如果能這樣去做，就是在練習走向安樂的人的智慧。因為他深深明白，沒有任何可練習的東西，這樣才是真正的練習。無論他練習什麼事物，都不會去執著。這就是在練習最棒的圓滿的智慧。
我們的形體、想法、感受、意願和覺知，其實沒有被綁住。它們沒有被解開，也不是真的存在。帶著這種態度邁向覺悟，心裡一點都不害怕。這就是聖潔的人穿上最棒的盔甲。

i.sp: 我們的形體、想法、感受、意願和覺知，其實沒有被綁住。它們沒有被解開，也不是真的存在。
i.ev: Academic: form, perception, feeling, volition and consciousness are neither bound nor liberated, and do not (truly) exist; 'our' is added and 'not truly existing' on its own risks sounding as if one's body and mind are nothing.
i.fx: 形體、想法、感受、意願和覺知，既沒有被綁住，也沒有被解開，本來就沒有可以抓住的真實樣子。

atts.t: 搭上這個乘不管去哪個方向，心裡都沒有執著。雖然說是走向超越憂傷的安寧，但其實找不到真正的去處。就像過世的人已經沒有地方可以去一樣。因為這樣，這才被大家叫做超越憂傷的安寧。

i.sp: 不管去哪個方向，心裡都沒有執著
i.ev: Academic: no direction of going can be apprehended/found (去向無所緣取); the children's text says the mind has no attachment, shifting from 'no destination found' to 'no clinging'.
i.fx: 搭上這個乘，不管往哪個方向去，都找不到真正要去的地方。

atts.t: 明白自己是什麼樣子，就會明白所有的眾生也是這個樣子；明白所有的眾生是什麼樣子，就會明白所有的事物也是這個樣子。對沒有出現和出現都不去分別，這就是在練習最特別的圓滿的智慧。

i.sp: 明白自己是什麼樣子，就會明白所有的眾生也是這個樣子
i.ev: The verse says that knowing how oneself is, all beings are likewise, and knowing how beings are, all things are likewise (sameness). The children's text turns this into a cause-and-effect 'if you understand X, you will understand Y'.
i.fx: 知道自己是什麼樣子，所有的眾生也是這個樣子；知道眾生是什麼樣子，所有的事物也是這個樣子。

atts.t: 不管世界上給事物取了多少名字，只要對這一切不再執著出現和消失，就能得到最特別、永遠不死的深刻的領悟，再也沒有其他的能超過它。所以，這就叫做圓滿的智慧。

i.sp: 只要對這一切不再執著出現和消失
i.ev: Academic translation: having cut off (abandoned) arising and ceasing with respect to all of them; 'no longer cling' softens 'abandon' and adds a conditional 'as long as'.
i.fx: 對這一切都不再有出現和消失的想法，就能得到最特別、永遠不死的深刻的領悟。

atts.t: 他們學習不是為了增加形體。不為減少或抓住形體。也不為抓住各種事物而學。他們這樣學並掌握無所不知。去尋找這樣的出路。喜愛美好的品質的人，就會這樣學習。

i.sp: 去尋找這樣的出路
i.ev: Academic translation: 'whatever is this definite emergence (出離) is the training of those who delight in good qualities' — a statement, not an instruction to go and look for a way out.
i.fx: 這樣的學習就是出路。喜愛美好的品質的人，就會這樣學習。

atts.t: 得勝者是這樣說的：「當我為大家講解這無比珍貴的圓滿時，過去那位最崇高的人告訴我：『未來你一定會成為佛陀。』我就這樣得到了預言。」

i.sp: 當我為大家講解這無比珍貴的圓滿時
i.ev: Source says 'when I spoke in accord with (相順宣說) this supreme perfection'; there is no audience ('for everyone') and no 'explaining'.
i.fx: 當我照著這最崇高的圓滿來說法時

atts.t: 守護者們都在學習這圓滿的智慧。如果有人恭敬地學習並真正懂了，毒藥、武器、大火或大水都無法傷害他。就連魔王和魔王一方的同夥，不管從哪一邊攻擊，都找不到他的弱點。

i.sp: 守護者們都在學習這圓滿的智慧
i.ev: Academic translation: the perfection of wisdom in which the protectors practise/conduct themselves (行持), not merely 'study'.
i.fx: 守護者們都在實踐這圓滿的智慧。

i.sp: 不管從哪一邊攻擊
i.ev: The source only says the Mara and Mara's side cannot find an opening; 'from whichever side they attack' is not in it.
i.fx: 就連魔王和魔王一方的同夥，也找不到他的弱點。

atts.t: 想像一下，有人為了紀念已經得到最終超越憂傷的安寧、走向安樂的人，用七種珍寶建造了供奉佛的塔。這些塔就像恆河的沙子那麼多，裝滿了千百萬個國土。

i.sp: 為了紀念
i.ev: Academic translation: making offerings (作供養) to the Sugata who has passed into nirvana, not commemorating.
i.fx: 為了供養已經得到最終超越憂傷的安寧、走向安樂的人

i.sp: 千百萬個國土
i.ev: Source: a thousand koti (千俱胝) of lands, a much larger number than 'thousands of millions'.
i.fx: 裝滿了數不清的國土（千俱胝個國土）

atts.t: 假設在無邊無際的國土中，所有的眾生什麼其他事都不做。他們在過去現在未來的時間裡，每天只用天上的花朵和最香的香料獻上供養。這樣一直持續一個漫長的時代，甚至更久。

i.ev: Source lists three offerings: celestial flowers, excellent incense and ointment/scented paste (塗香). The children's text mentions only flowers and 'the most fragrant incense'; the ointment is dropped.
i.fx: 他們只用天上的花朵、最香的香和香膏獻上供養。

atts.t: 得勝者的這個圓滿的智慧，就像是一道知識的大咒語。它能消除眾生的領域中許多的憂傷與痛苦。不管是過去還是十個方向裡，所有世界的守護者，都是因為學習了這道知曉的咒語，才成為最了不起的醫生中的王，受到像國王一樣的尊敬。

i.sp: 受到像國王一樣的尊敬
i.ev: The source only says they became the supreme 'king of physicians'; the idea of being respected like a king is not in the verse or the academic translation.
i.fx: 才成為最了不起的醫生中的王。

atts.t: 得勝者這圓滿的智慧，是知識的大咒語。它能平息許多眾生的領域裡的悲傷與痛苦。無論是過去，還是十個方向的世界的守護者，他們都學習這個知曉的咒語，因此成為無上的國王，也就是最厲害的醫生中的王。

i.sp: 成為無上的國王，也就是最厲害的醫生中的王
i.ev: The protectors become the supreme king of physicians (one title); saying '無上的國王' first suggests a separate king, which is confusing.
i.fx: 因此成為最厲害的、醫生中的王

atts.t: 那些為別人帶來好處和慈悲的人，只要是有智慧的人，學了這個知曉的咒語，就能得到覺悟。世上所有由原因造成的快樂，以及不是由原因造成的快樂，你要知道，這一切的快樂都是從這裡產生的。

i.sp: 那些為別人帶來好處和慈悲的人
i.ev: Academic translation: those who practise (行持) with benefit and compassion — the practitioners act with these, they do not 'bring compassion to others'.
i.fx: 那些帶著好處他人的心和慈悲去行動的人

atts.t: 在展現「慷慨」之前，必須先有「智慧」來帶路。培養「良好品行」、「耐心」、「持續的努力」和「深度專注」，也是一樣的道理。為了不讓「善良的特質」白白浪費，我們要好好把它們記在心裡。這能讓我們明白，所有的「事物」都包含著相同的道理。

i.sp: 為了不讓「善良的特質」白白浪費，我們要好好把它們記在心裡。
i.ev: In the verse, wisdom is what holds/upholds the virtues so they are not wasted; the children's text makes 'we' the agent who memorises them.
i.fx: 為了不讓「善良的特質」白白浪費，「智慧」會把它們好好守護住。

atts.t: 有人以為，只要教大家東西都會壞掉就好，其實不是這樣。如果「菩薩」在還沒有真正明白的時候。就把「形體」、「想法」、「感受」、「意願」和「覺知」，都當作「不斷變化」來教給別人，這就是在學習虛假的東西。真正有智慧的人，絕對不會去破壞任何「事物」。

i.sp: 有人以為，只要教大家東西都會壞掉就好，其實不是這樣。
i.ev: The segment does not mention anyone holding this belief; it says a bodhisattva who teaches the five aggregates as impermanent without proper understanding is practising something fabricated.
i.fx: 如果「菩薩」還沒有真正明白，就把「形體」……都當作「不斷變化」來教給別人，這就是在學習虛假的東西。

atts.t: 如果我們不去抓住「形體」或「感受」。也「找不到」「想法」、「覺知」和「意願」。並且清楚明白，所有的「事物」都是「從未出生」，也都是「空的」。能夠這樣做，就是在學習最棒的「圓滿的智慧」了。

i.sp: 如果我們不去抓住「形體」或「感受」。
i.ev: The verse says form and feeling are not (found), and no apprehension of perception, consciousness, intention; it is not about 'not grasping' form and feeling while 'not finding' the others.
i.fx: 如果我們「找不到」「形體」和「感受」，也「找不到」「想法」、「覺知」和「意願」。

atts.t: 當太陽散發出耀眼的光芒時，眾生就會勤奮地開始工作。同樣的道理，如果有智慧的人為了追求真理，在世界上生起想要覺悟的心願。眾生就能靠著這種深刻的領悟，擁有很多美好的品質和特質。

i.sp: 為了追求真理
i.ev: The wise one generates the wish for awakening in the world 'in order to know' (so as to gain realisation); 'truth' is not in the text.
i.fx: 為了能真正明白

atts.t: 如果在奉獻的時候，你產生了關於內心的想法。又產生了關於覺悟的想法，以及把它奉獻給眾生的想法。因為有了這些想法，帶著錯誤看法的內心，就會緊緊抓住這三樣不放。有人以為這就是奉獻，其實不是這樣。因為把它們當作可以抓住的東西，這就不能算是真正的奉獻。

i.sp: 帶著錯誤看法的內心
i.ev: The academic translation says the mind clings to 'view' and these three; it does not call the view wrong.
i.fx: 抱著某種「看法」的內心

i.sp: 有人以為這就是奉獻，其實不是這樣。
i.ev: Not in the verse; the next line already states that this is not dedication.

atts.t: 你要明白事物都會停止和消失。接受奉獻的對象也不是永遠不變的。而且絕對不拿事物來奉獻給事物。能徹底明白這些道理就是真正的奉獻。

i.sp: 接受奉獻的對象也不是永遠不變的。
i.ev: The verse says the place/object of dedication is also exhausted (ceased), and the whole is conditional 'if one knows', not an instruction.
i.fx: 如果明白這件事物會停止、會消失，連接受奉獻的地方也會消失。

atts.t: 像這樣把累積的福氣奉獻給覺悟，這就沒有毒。這沒有背棄佛陀，也是說得勝者說的話。這樣奉獻的勇士能勝過世界上所有的菩薩。也就是那些抓著某個東西不放的人。

i.sp: 能勝過世界上所有的菩薩。也就是那些抓著某個東西不放的人。
i.ev: Only the bodhisattvas of the world who have an object of clinging are surpassed, not all bodhisattvas.
i.fx: 能勝過世界上那些抓著某個東西不放的「菩薩」。

terms: 抓著某個東西不放的人

atts.t: 有人以為：「我要學習得勝者的智慧。我要解救千百億受痛苦的眾生。」其實不是這樣。如果一個菩薩心裡有眾生的想法。即使他想要追求覺悟。這也不是在學習最棒的圓滿的智慧。

i.sp: 如果一個菩薩心裡有眾生的想法。即使他想要追求覺悟。這也不是在學習最棒的圓滿的智慧。
i.ev: The text rejects the bodhisattva who conceptualises (fixates on) beings as real while thinking 'I will liberate them'; it does not say that merely thinking of beings or wanting to rescue them is wrong. The children's text can be read as saying that thinking of beings, or wanting to help them, is itself a mistake.
i.fx: 如果一個「菩薩」一邊想著要解救「眾生」，一邊把「眾生」當成真實的東西抓著不放，即使他想要追求「覺悟」，這也不是在學習最棒的「圓滿的智慧」。

atts.t: 如果有人想：「我要學習得勝者的智慧，解救千百億受痛苦的眾生。」如果一個菩薩一邊想著要解救眾生，一邊卻把眾生當成真實的東西抓著不放，有了眾生的想法，即使他想要追求覺悟，這也不是在學習最棒的圓滿的智慧。
第四章：展現各方面的完全領悟。天神之王帝釋問得勝者：「菩薩該怎麼努力修習智慧呢？」得勝者說：「對身心的組成部分和元素，連一點點微塵大的力氣都不花。不把力氣花在身心的組成部分上，這才是菩薩真正的努力。」

i.sp: 得勝者說：
i.ev: The academic translation gives no explicit speaker for the answer; it presents the verse as Indra's question followed by the teaching on not striving for the aggregates.
i.fx: 「對身心的組成部分和元素，連一點點微塵大的力氣都不花。不把力氣花在身心的組成部分上，這才是菩薩真正的努力。」（去掉「得勝者說」）

atts.t: 如果有人在修行時，不去分辨佛陀的特質，不去分辨力量、神奇力量的基礎，以及平靜的覺悟；他心裡沒有固定想法，並且遠離虛構的想法，靠著祝福來修行，這就是殊勝的圓滿的智慧的修行了。

i.sp: 不去分辨
i.ev: The text says the practitioner does not conceptualize (rnam par mi rtog / 不分別) the Buddha's qualities, powers etc.; 'distinguish/tell apart' is a different, imprecise sense.
i.fx: 如果有人在修行時，不去執著想著佛陀的特質，不去執著想著力量、神奇力量的基礎，以及平靜的覺悟；

atts.t: 須菩提向被稱為言說者的月亮的佛陀請問：「喜歡美好的品質的人，會遇到什麼阻礙呢？」大師回答他說：「將會遇到很多阻礙，我先簡單告訴你們其中的一小部分吧。」

i.sp: 我先簡單告訴你們其中的一小部分吧
i.ev: Subhuti asks and the Teacher replies about the obstacles; the text does not address a plural audience.
i.fx: 我先簡單告訴你其中的一小部分吧。

atts.t: 抄寫得勝者的圓滿的智慧時，可能會突然覺得自己很有口才。但這口才卻像閃電一樣短暫，馬上就消失了，完全沒有幫助到眾生。這其實是魔王的作為。

i.sp: 可能會突然覺得自己很有口才
i.ev: The text says many different kinds of eloquence will arise; the children's text drops 'different kinds' and recasts it as merely feeling eloquent.
i.fx: 抄寫得勝者的圓滿的智慧時，可能會冒出各種不同的口才。

atts.t: 有人聽別人講這個道理時，心裡可能會產生懷疑。他們想：「導師沒有提到我的名字，也沒有說我的家族和出生的地方。」於是他們就不想聽了，把它丟在一旁。這也是魔王的作為。

i.ev: The academic translation lists three items the doubter says were not mentioned: caste/family (種姓), birthplace (生處) and clan (氏族); the children's text gives only two.
i.fx: 他們想：「導師沒有提到我的名字，也沒有說我的家族、出生的地方和氏族。」

atts.t: 有人心裡想要得到尊敬，也貪圖得到的財物。帶著錯誤的看法去親近別人家。他們丟掉佛法，跑去做違背佛法的事。就像離開了正確的道路，走上了走錯的路。這也是魔王的作為。

i.sp: 帶著錯誤的看法去親近別人家
i.ev: The academic translation says they associate with laypeople's homes with a mind that desires to see outer things (欲求見外境之心); it does not say 'wrong views'. 'Wrong' is added and changes the fault described.
i.fx: 帶著想要看看外面事物的心，常常去親近別人家。

atts.t: 有人心裡想要得到尊敬，也貪圖得到的財物。帶著想要看看外面事物的看法，常常去親近別人家。他們丟掉佛法，跑去做違背佛法的事。就像離開了正確的道路，走上了走錯的路。這也是魔王的作為。

i.sp: 帶著想要看看外面事物的看法
i.ev: The mind is driven by a wish to see/fixate on outer things (views); the phrase is awkward and hard for children.
i.fx: 心裡想著外面的東西，抱著這樣的看法

i.sp: 這也是魔王的作為
i.ev: The text says simply 'this is the work of Mara'; '也' implies an additional item not stated.
i.fx: 這些都是魔王的作為

atts.t: 貪求別人的尊敬和得到的財物。帶著想到處看的心去親近一般人的家。丟下佛法，去做違背佛法的事。放棄了道路，卻走上走錯的路。這些都是魔王的作為。
剛踏上這乘的眾生智慧還很小。如果他們沒得到這稀少的珍寶，魔王就會興奮地來製造阻礙。不過十個方向的佛陀會全力保護他們。

i.sp: 剛踏上這乘的眾生
i.ev: '乘' (the vehicle, i.e. the Great Vehicle) is left unexplained and is hard for ages 8-12.
i.fx: 剛踏上大乘這條路的眾生智慧還很小。

atts.t: 過去、未來和十個方向所有的世界的守護者，都是從這圓滿的智慧生出來的。她就像母親一樣，生下了世界的老師、大師與得勝者，還能顯示其他眾生心裡的想法和行為。

i.sp: 生下了世界的老師、大師與得勝者
i.ev: The Tibetan/academic text names one group in apposition: the teachers of the world, the victors. The children's text reads as three separate kinds of beings.
i.fx: 她就像母親一樣，生下了得勝者，也就是世界的老師、大師。

atts.t: 世界真正的樣貌、值得敬重的人眼中事物的真正樣貌、獨自覺悟的人的事物真正樣貌，還有得勝者之子的事物真正樣貌（也就是得勝者的孩子眼中事物的真正樣貌），其實全部都是一樣的。如來透過圓滿的智慧明白，這同一個事物真正的樣貌，全都是沒有真實存在的事物，並沒有任何分別。

i.sp: （也就是得勝者的孩子眼中事物的真正樣貌）
i.ev: The parenthetical repeats the same phrase, and the long list of four 'true nature' phrases is hard for ages 8-12. Meaning is intact.
i.fx: 把四種人眼中的樣貌分成短句列出，並刪去括號裡重複的解釋。

terms: 值得敬重的人眼中事物的真正樣貌
獨自覺悟的人的事物真正樣貌
得勝者之子的事物真正樣貌

atts.t: 就像國王不用親自跑到村莊或國家。他只要待在自己的地方，就能收齊所有的財物。菩薩了解事物的本性也是這樣。他哪裡都不去，卻能收集佛的階段所有的美好的品質。

i.sp: 菩薩了解事物的本性也是這樣。他哪裡都不去
i.ev: The subject that goes nowhere yet gathers all qualities of the buddha grounds is the bodhisattva's dharmata (nature of things). The children's text makes the bodhisattva the one who 'understands' it and adds that idea.
i.fx: 菩薩的本性（事物的本性）也是這樣，哪裡都不去，卻能收集佛的階段所有的美好的品質。

atts.t: 就像國王不用親自跑到村莊或國家，他只要待在自己的地方，就能收齊所有的財物。菩薩的事物的本性也是這樣，哪裡都不去，卻能收集佛的階段所有的美好的品質。
如果這些巧妙的方法的美好的品質，都能被智慧完全帶領。他們很快就能親自體會極為稀有的、走向安樂的人的覺悟。

i.sp: 這些巧妙的方法的美好的品質
i.ev: Stacked possessives are tangled for children; the academic text says the qualities of skillful means are fully embraced by wisdom.
i.fx: 如果這些靠巧妙的方法得來的美好品質，都被智慧完全包住、守護著。

atts.t: 菩薩也是這樣。雖然有滿滿的信任。如果失去智慧，很快就會失敗。要是信任能有智慧來帶領。就能超越前面的兩個階段。得到最高的覺悟。

i.sp: 超越前面的兩個階段
i.ev: The two grounds are the hearers' and solitary realizers' grounds; 'front two stages' leaves them unidentified and adds 'front'.
i.fx: 就能完全超越聽法的弟子和獨自覺悟的人這兩個階段。

atts.t: 菩薩也是這樣。雖然心裡充滿信任。如果沒有智慧，就會失去覺悟。如果擁有最棒的圓滿的智慧。就不會退縮。能得到得勝者的覺悟。

i.sp: 如果沒有智慧，就會失去覺悟
i.ev: The text says that without wisdom one quickly falls away from awakening; the speed is dropped.
i.fx: 如果沒有智慧，很快就會失去覺悟。

atts.t: 老師應該這樣教導初學者：「你要把慷慨、良好品行、耐心、持續的努力、深度專注和智慧，全都奉獻給覺悟！不要把覺悟當作身心的組成部分來貪戀，也不要執著於最高的。」

i.sp: 也不要執著於最高的
i.ev: 'Do not cling to awakening as a heap/aggregate and make it supreme' is one prohibition; the children's text splits it and leaves 'the highest' dangling and unclear.
i.fx: 不要把覺悟當成一堆東西來貪戀，也不要把它當成最高的而緊抓不放。

atts.t: 有大名聲的人，為了困難的任務而穿上盔甲。但這並不是為身心的組成部分、元素或感官之門穿的盔甲。他們沒有關於三乘的想法，也不會對任何事物緊抓不放。他們永不退縮、不會動搖，有著不會被擾亂的本性。

i.sp: 他們沒有關於三乘的想法
i.ev: 'Three vehicles' is left unexplained for ages 8-12; the text says they have no fixed notion of the three paths.
i.fx: 他們不會緊抓著聽法的弟子、獨自覺悟的人和菩薩這三條道路的想法。

atts.t: 不論是過去的事物真正的樣貌，還是未來的事物真正的樣貌；現在的事物真正的樣貌，還是值得敬重的人的事物真正的樣貌；所有事物的事物真正的樣貌，還是得勝者的事物真正的樣貌；這個事物的事物真正的樣貌，這一切全都沒有差別。

i.sp: 所有事物的事物真正的樣貌，還是得勝者的事物真正的樣貌；這個事物的事物真正的樣貌
i.ev: Academic: the suchness of all dharmas, of the Victors, and of this dharma; the repeated locked term makes "事物的事物真正的樣貌" tangled for ages 8-12.
i.fx: 所有事物真正的樣貌，還是得勝者真正的樣貌；這個教法真正的樣貌，這一切全都沒有差別。

atts.t: 得勝者的這五種圓滿，雖然經過許多漫長的時代才修成，他們在世間也一直抱著廣大的願望。可是，如果沒有巧妙的方法，又缺少智慧的話，他們就會掉下來，變成聽法的弟子。

i.sp: 他們在世間也一直抱著廣大的願望
i.ev: Academic: the practitioner who perfects the five perfections over many eons and always relies on boundless vast aspirations falls to the Hearer level without skillful means and wisdom; "他們" is unclear and could be read as the Victors, who do not fall.
i.fx: 修行的人雖然經過許多漫長的時代才修成這五種圓滿，也一直抱著廣大的願望。可是，如果沒有巧妙的方法，又缺少智慧，他們就會掉下來，變成聽法的弟子。

atts.t: 他們把自己打理得很乾淨，穿著乾淨的衣服。他們的行為、說話和想法這三者都很清淨。這些偉大的領袖不求好處，只是一直追求佛法。他們已經超越了魔王的地盤，不依賴其他人。雖然他們會練習四種深度專注，卻不會停留在這種深度專注裡。

i.sp: 他們的行為、說話和想法這三者都很清淨
i.ev: Academic says only "the three are secluded and pure" (三者遠離且清淨); it does not name body, speech and mind.
i.fx: 他們把自己打理得很乾淨，穿著乾淨的衣服；那三者也都遠離過失、很清淨。

atts.t: 形體、感受、想法、意願和覺知，這一切都很深奧。它們的本質是沒有記號的，而且非常安靜。這就像用箭去尋找大海的底部一樣。如果用智慧去觀察，根本找不到這些身心的組成部分的盡頭。

i.sp: 找不到這些身心的組成部分的盡頭
i.ev: Academic: one cannot find the bottom (底) of the aggregates, like probing the sea floor with an arrow; "盡頭" (end) loses the depth image.
i.fx: 根本找不到這些身心的組成部分的底部。

atts.t: 當菩薩變得這麼深奧，在最深的真理中學習不執著的乘。他明白這裡沒有身心的組成部分，沒有元素，也沒有感官之門。誰要是明白了這個佛法，他真正累積的福氣，還有什麼能超過呢？

i.sp: 在最深的真理中學習不執著的乘。他明白這裡沒有身心的組成部分，沒有元素，也沒有感官之門
i.ev: Academic: in the vehicle of non-attachment in the ultimate sense, aggregates, elements and sense-bases do not exist; the "ultimately" scope is not clearly tied to the absence, so it may read as the aggregates simply not existing.
i.fx: 在最深的真理裡，他明白身心的組成部分、元素和感官之門都不是真的存在。

atts.t: 就像一個追求想要的事物的男人，跟一個女人約好卻沒有見面。他在一天之內，心裡會生起多少紛亂的念頭啊！菩薩也能獲得這麼多個漫長的時代所累積的福氣。

i.sp: 追求想要的事物的男人
i.ev: Academic: a man who engages in the dharma of desire/lust (貪欲法) who arranged to meet a woman; "想要的事物" loses the desire/lust meaning.
i.fx: 一個被慾望牽動的男人

atts.t: 如果有菩薩在非常久的時間裡，對值得敬重的人和獨自覺悟的人展現慷慨，並且保持良好品行。可是，如果有人為大家講解包含圓滿的智慧的佛法。這講解的好處，遠遠超過前面的慷慨與良好品行。

i.sp: 可是，如果有人為大家講解包含圓滿的智慧的佛法。這講解的好處
i.ev: The "如果" clause is left as a sentence fragment, so the comparison is tangled for children.
i.fx: 可是，如果有人為大家講解包含圓滿的智慧的佛法，這講解的好處，遠遠超過前面的慷慨與良好品行。

atts.t: 當菩薩好好練習了美好的智慧。接著他為大家講解清淨的佛法。他為了眾生，把這一切奉獻給覺悟。在整個三世界中，沒有任何事能比得上這份善良。

i.sp: 接著他為大家講解清淨的佛法
i.ev: Academic: the bodhisattva rises from that meditation (從彼出定) and then teaches the stainless dharma; "rising from meditation" is dropped.
i.fx: 菩薩好好練習了智慧，從禪修中起來後，為大家講解清淨的佛法。

atts.t: 就像種子長出嫩芽，然後開花結果。雖然種子消失了，樹木卻依然存在。同樣的，我們心中最初的念頭，也是獲得覺悟的原因。即使這個念頭過去了，覺悟也不會因此消失。

i.sp: 即使這個念頭過去了，覺悟也不會因此消失
i.ev: Academic: even though the first mind has ceased, it is not that there is no bodhi (bodhi still arises from it); "消失" implies bodhi already existed and is lost.
i.fx: 即使這個念頭過去了，覺悟還是會從它長出來，不是沒有覺悟。

atts.t: 他帶著父母和妻兒一起出門。他們走進一條充滿壞人的荒野小路。這時，他變出許多勇敢的戰士來保護大家。他們一路平安前進，最後又安全地回到家裡。

i.sp: 妻兒
i.ev: The text mentions parents and wife only; no children.
i.fx: 他帶著父母和妻子一起出門。

i.sp: 來保護大家
i.ev: The text says he emanates many brave men; it does not state the purpose (protection).
i.fx: 這時，他變出許多勇敢的人。

atts.t: 聰明的菩薩也是像這樣。他們在眾生的領域中，生起廣大的慈悲。他們完全打敗了四個魔王。他們也超越了兩種修行的階段。他們停留在美好的深度安定中，卻不急著去接觸覺悟。

i.sp: 卻不急著去接觸覺悟
i.ev: The text says the bodhisattva does not touch (realize) enlightenment; 'not in a hurry' turns a negation into a delay, implying he will soon do so.
i.fx: 卻不去接觸覺悟。

i.sp: 完全打敗了四個魔王
i.ev: The text says the bodhisattva has completely transcended the four maras, not defeated them.
i.fx: 他們完全超越了四個魔王。

atts.t: 聰明的菩薩也是像這樣。他們在所有眾生的領域中，生起廣大的慈悲。他們完全打敗了四個魔王，也超越了兩種修行的階段。他們停留在美好的深度安定中，卻不去接觸覺悟。
菩薩也是像這樣安住在空性中。他們了解眾生，並依靠著幫助眾生的願望。菩薩為大家展現出各種不同的行動。他們不去接觸超越憂傷的安寧，也不會只停留在空性之中。

i.sp: 也不會只停留在空性之中
i.ev: The text says the bodhisattva does not abide in emptiness at all; 'only' weakens this.
i.fx: 也不會停留在空性之中。

atts.t: 當聰明的菩薩修習這種空性又平靜的絕佳深度安定時，他在這段期間絕對不去認取任何記號。他停留在沒有記號的狀態，心裡非常非常平靜。

i.sp: 認取
i.ev: 'Not meditating on signs'; 認取 is a hard word for ages 8-12.
i.fx: 他在這段期間完全不去想著任何記號。

atts.t: 天空中飛翔的鳥兒沒有固定的住處。牠沒有停在空中，也沒有掉到地上。同樣的，菩薩走進通往自由的門。他不去觸碰超越憂傷的安寧，也不去追求任何記號。

i.sp: 也不去追求任何記號
i.ev: The text says he does not practice/engage in signs, not that he does not seek them.
i.fx: 也不照著任何記號去行動。

atts.t: 厲害的菩薩也是這樣。他們心中懷著慈悲。雙手撐著兩把傘。這就是巧妙的方法與智慧。他們觀察一切事物都是空的。是沒有記號和沒有願望的。他們看見一切事物。卻不會獨自進入超越憂傷的安寧。

i.sp: 卻不會獨自進入超越憂傷的安寧
i.ev: The text says the bodhisattva does not touch nirvana at all; 'alone' adds the idea that he might enter it together with others.
i.fx: 卻不去接觸超越憂傷的安寧。

atts.t: 聰明的菩薩也是這樣。他們心中懷著慈悲，雙手撐著兩把傘，也就是巧妙的方法與智慧。他們觀察一切事物都是空的，沒有記號，也沒有願望。他們看見一切事物，卻不去接觸超越憂傷的安寧。
有人以為自己能給出各種真實的祝福，就產生了自大。他們覺得「我已經得到了預言」。或者因為聽了其他菩薩的預言而感到自大。你應該知道，心裡充滿自大的人其實懂得很少。

i.sp: 以為自己能給出各種真實的祝福
i.ev: The text says arrogance arises because he has accomplished the various true blessings, not because he merely believes he can give them.
i.fx: 有人成就了各種真實的祝福，就產生了自大。

atts.t: 有些山谷廣達五百個古印度的長距離單位。裡面充滿毒蛇。就算在那裡住上千萬年。如果這位菩薩不懂得真正的安靜獨處。他就會變得自認高人一等。其實他一直處在混亂之中。

i.sp: 其實他一直處在混亂之中
i.ev: Academic text says he dwells in 'mixing' (混雜, i.e. mingling with company), not in 'confusion/chaos'.
i.fx: 其實他一直跟別人混在一起，沒有真正獨處。

atts.t: 佛陀和追求最高的覺悟的菩薩。我們應該連同圓滿一起。把他們當作有智慧的朋友。他們會順著道理來教導我們。這就是成就的階段。透過這兩個原因。我們就能很快得到佛陀的覺悟。

i.sp: 他們會順著道理來教導我們
i.ev: Academic text says they are those who teach/guide in accordance (隨順開示者); 'following reason' is not stated.
i.fx: 他們會一步一步指導我們。

atts.t: 過去和未來以及十個方向的得勝者。他們的道路全都是這個圓滿。沒有別的道路了。走向最高的覺悟的人。這個圓滿就是他們的明亮。它是燈，也是光亮。更是最棒的老師。

i.sp: 這個圓滿就是他們的明亮
i.ev: Academic text: the pāramitā is the light, lamp, radiance and supreme teacher of those who enter supreme awakening; 'their brightness' is awkward for children.
i.fx: 對走向最高的覺悟的人來說，這個圓滿是明亮，是燈，是光亮，也是最棒的老師。

atts.t: 眾生因為心裡有執著而貪求食物。貪戀輪迴的人會一直流轉不停。其實自己和自我的事物都不是真的，而且是空的。不明智的人卻靠著自己，就像在天空中打結一樣。

i.sp: 不明智的人卻靠著自己，就像在天空中打結一樣
i.ev: Academic text: the foolish by themselves tie knots in empty space (a futile act); 'rely on themselves' is unclear and the image is unexplained.
i.fx: 不明智的人卻自己在天空中打結，這根本是白費力氣。

atts.t: 練習最高的圓滿智慧的修行的人，雖然心裡充滿偉大的慈悲，卻沒有執著於眾生的想法。這樣有智慧的人，成了所有眾生值得接受布施的人，他們吃別人施捨的食物非常有意義。

i.ev: Academic text says they 'always' (恆常) make meaningful use of the alms food of the land (國土之施食); 'always' and 'country/land' are dropped.
i.fx: 他們一直都能吃各地人們施捨的食物，這些食物吃得很有意義。

atts.t: 菩薩為了解救長久以來結緣的眾生，不管是天神和人，還是在三個較低的去處的眾生。菩薩想為他們指出通往彼岸的寬廣的道路，所以日夜不停，努力學習圓滿的智慧。

i.sp: 所以日夜不停，努力學習圓滿的智慧
i.ev: Academic text gives an instruction: the bodhisattva should (應當) strive day and night in the perfection of wisdom; the children's text states it as a plain fact.
i.fx: 所以菩薩應該日夜不停，努力學習圓滿的智慧。

atts.t: 就像有人以前沒看過最高的寶物，後來終於找到了，心裡非常高興。但如果剛找到，就因為粗心大意而弄丟了，他就會為了找回這個珍寶，心裡一直覺得痛苦。

i.sp: 以前沒看過最高的寶物
i.ev: Academic text: had not previously obtained (未得) the supreme jewel, not merely 'not seen' it.
i.fx: 以前從來沒有得到過最高的寶物

atts.t: 沒有烏雲遮擋、發出耀眼光芒的太陽，升起的時候，會趕走所有濃濃的黑暗。太陽的光非常明亮，會蓋過螢火蟲和小生物發出的微光，也會蓋過滿天星星和月亮的光芒。

i.sp: 螢火蟲和小生物發出的微光
i.ev: Academic text: all fireflies and all living creatures are eclipsed; 'all' is lost and 'small creatures that give faint light' is an addition.
i.fx: 會蓋過所有螢火蟲和生靈，還有滿天星星和月亮的光芒。

atts.t: 同樣的，菩薩學習圓滿的智慧，安住在空性之中，明白事物是沒有記號的。有智慧的人打破了深重錯誤的看法後，他的光芒會蓋過一切眾生，也會蓋過值得敬重的人、獨自覺悟的人，以及許多菩薩。

i.sp: 深重錯誤的看法
i.ev: Academic text says 'dense views' (濃密之見); 'wrong' is not stated.
i.fx: 打破了濃濃的看法

atts.t: 善於運用智慧的菩薩也是這樣。菩薩把不死的甘露分給大家，讓天神和人們都很高興。菩薩光是這樣做，就努力幫助了許多眾生。當菩薩成為佛法的國王時，大家一定更開心！

i.sp: 大家一定更開心！
i.ev: Academic text: the bodhisattva already works to benefit many beings; how much more once established as Dharma king. The comparison concerns benefit, not happiness.
i.fx: 當菩薩成為佛法的國王時，能幫助的眾生就更多了，更不用說了！

atts.t: 有些眾生追求善良，並且想要幫助別人。對於他們累積的福氣，我們也要為別人高興。因為他們得到得勝者的美好品質之後，為了消滅所有的痛苦，就會在這個世界送出佛法的禮物。

i.sp: 有些眾生追求善良，並且想要幫助別人。對於他們累積的福氣，我們也要為別人高興。
i.ev: Tibetan/academic: ALL sentient beings who seek virtue and wish to benefit others themselves rejoice in the whole heap of merit of all; therefore, having obtained the Victors' qualities, they give the gift of Dharma in the world. The children's text says 'some' beings and makes 'we' (the reader) the one who rejoices in their merit, changing the subject of the rejoicing and the logic of 'therefore'.
i.fx: 所有追求善良、想要幫助別人的眾生，也都為大家累積的福氣高興。因此，他們得到得勝者的美好品質之後，為了消滅所有的痛苦，就會在這個世界送出佛法的禮物。

atts.t: 所有追求善良、想要幫助別人的眾生，對於大家累積的福氣，他們也都為別人高興。因此，他們得到得勝者的美好品質之後，為了消滅所有的痛苦，就會在這個世界送出佛法的禮物。
就算數量像恆河裡的沙子一樣多的眾生，全都產生了錯誤的想法而變成魔王；甚至從他們每一根毛髮，又變出同樣多的魔王，這些魔王全都無法對聰明的修行人造成阻礙。

i.sp: 數量像恆河裡的沙子一樣多的眾生
i.ev: Academic: all beings in world-fields (剎土) equal in number to the Ganges sands; the 'fields' are dropped, so the count applies to beings rather than to the worlds they live in.
i.fx: 就算像恆河裡的沙子那麼多的世界裡，所有的眾生

atts.t: 除了值得敬重的人與如來的自由之外，這種安住是最棒的。比起聽法的弟子與獨自覺悟的人，他們在平靜的深度安定中所得到的極大安靜與快樂，這種安住是最特別、最至高無上的。

i.sp: 比起聽法的弟子與獨自覺悟的人，他們在平靜的深度安定中所得到的極大安靜與快樂，這種安住是最特別、最至高無上的。
i.ev: Academic: this abiding is supreme and unsurpassed among all the peaceful samadhi abidings, very calm and blissful, of hearers and solitary realizers; the children's sentence is long and 'they' is ambiguous.
i.fx: 聽法的弟子與獨自覺悟的人，也有平靜的深度安定，很安靜、很快樂。但這種安住比他們所有的都更特別、更至高無上。

atts.t: 鳥兒飛在空中卻不會掉下來。魚兒住在水裡，也不會因為水流翻攪而死掉。同樣的，菩薩靠著深度專注的力量到達對岸。菩薩安住在空性之中，但不會直接進入超越憂傷的安寧。

i.sp: 不會直接進入
i.ev: Tibetan/academic: the bodhisattva abides in emptiness and does not pass into nirvana; 'directly' is not in the text.
i.fx: 菩薩安住在空性之中，不會進入超越憂傷的安寧。

atts.t: 須菩提，關於深刻的領悟的入口，還有巧妙的方法與根源，全都來自最棒的圓滿的智慧。許多幫助的原因聚在一起，會啟動行為的機器。但是圓滿的智慧不會減少，也不會增加。

i.sp: 須菩提，
i.ev: The Tibetan and academic translation contain no address to Subhuti or anyone else; the vocative adds a speaker/addressee not in the segment.
i.fx: 所有深刻的領悟的入口，還有巧妙的方法與根源，全都來自最棒的圓滿的智慧。

atts.t: 所有深刻的領悟的入口，還有巧妙的方法與根源，全都來自最棒的圓滿的智慧。許多幫助的原因聚在一起，會啟動行為的機器。但是圓滿的智慧不會減少，也不會增加。
如果菩薩處於深度安定與深度專注中，卻想要追求值得敬重的人，或是獨自覺悟的人的乘。他們就會變成沒有安定於禪修，陷入心浮氣躁與飄忽不定的心。這樣會完全失去佛陀美好的品質，就像船夫的船被毀壞了一樣。

i.sp: 想要追求值得敬重的人，或是獨自覺悟的人的乘
i.ev: Source: aspiring to the Arhat and Pratyekabuddha vehicle; the children's phrase can be misread as pursuing people.
i.fx: 想要走「值得敬重的人」或「獨自覺悟的人」所走的乘

atts.t: 此外，就算他們正在面對形體與聲音，以及氣味、味道與觸感，很投入在感官的五種快樂中。只要他們遠離值得敬重的人，以及獨自覺悟的人的乘，並且為想要覺悟的心願感到歡喜。大家就應該知道，這位勇士一直處在穩定的寧靜中。

i.sp: 只要他們遠離值得敬重的人，以及獨自覺悟的人的乘
i.ev: Source: being free of (turning away from) the Arhat and Pratyekabuddha vehicles; 'stay away from the worthy people' misreads it, and the sentences are fragments.
i.fx: 只要他們不去走值得敬重的人和獨自覺悟的人的乘，並且為想要覺悟的心願感到歡喜，

atts.t: 缺乏智慧的菩薩，會去計算經過了多少個漫長的時代。如果在追求覺悟時覺得時間太長又充滿痛苦，那麼在修習真正的佛法時，就會承受很久的痛苦。這樣會失去圓滿的持續努力，反而變得懶惰。

i.sp: 去計算經過了多少個漫長的時代
i.ev: Academic translation: the unskilled bodhisattva counts tens of millions of kalpas (number 'ten million' lost).
i.fx: 會去計算要經過千萬個漫長的時代

atts.t: 幫助者曾這樣說：當你對身體、心和眾生，都沒有任何固定的想法。你完全放下這些想法，去實踐不分彼此的教導。對於想要得到平靜、不會退步的最高覺悟的人，這就是圓滿的持續努力。

i.sp: 都沒有任何固定的想法
i.ev: Academic translation: no notion (perception) of body, mind and beings; 'fixed' is not in the text.
i.fx: 都不再有「這是身體、這是心、這是眾生」的想法

atts.t: 只要任何事物能產生覺悟的美好的品質，這就是擁有美好的品質的人所表現的良好品行。相反的，如果任何事物會讓幫助別人的覺悟退步，導師說這就是缺乏良好品行。

i.sp: 產生覺悟的美好的品質
i.ev: Academic: whatever dharma surely brings about the qualities of awakening; the children's phrase stacks two 的 and reads awkwardly, though the meaning is intact.
i.fx: 能讓覺悟的美好品質出現

atts.t: 即使菩薩享受了感官的享樂，也就是體驗了感官的五種快樂。只要他把佛陀、佛法當作庇護處，也把高尚而神聖的僧團當作庇護處。他心裡想著：「我一定要成佛！」並且專心追求無所不知的智慧。我們就應該知道，這個有智慧的人，已經做到了圓滿的良好品行，安住在這份良好品行之中。

i.sp: 即使菩薩享受了感官的享樂，也就是體驗了感官的五種快樂。
i.ev: Academic: even if the bodhisattva enjoys the five sense pleasures (one statement); the children's text states it twice in a tangled way, and the following clauses are fragments that lack a clear main clause.
i.fx: 即使菩薩享受感官的五種快樂，只要他把佛陀、佛法和神聖的僧團都當作庇護處，心裡想著「我一定要成佛」，專心追求無所不知的智慧，我們就應該知道，這個有智慧的人安住在圓滿的良好品行之中。

atts.t: 即使在千萬個漫長的時代裡，努力走在十條善行之路上，如果心裡只想成為值得敬重的人或獨自覺悟的人。那時，他的良好品行就有了過錯，已經失去了良好品行。他這樣許下覺悟的心願，其實比最嚴重的犯戒還要嚴重。

i.sp: 他這樣許下覺悟的心願
i.ev: Academic: 此發心 'this aspiration' refers to the wish for the arhat's or solitary realizer's result, which is worse than a root downfall. 'Making a wish for awakening' can be misread as the bodhisattva's own aspiration being worse than the gravest offense.
i.fx: 他心裡這樣的願望，其實比最嚴重的犯戒還要嚴重

atts.t: 只要有「我」的想法，就會因為把事物當成自己的而產生貪心。這種笨蛋怎麼會想把東西送人呢？小氣的人將來會出生在餓鬼的地方，成為餓鬼。就算將來出生為人，到時候也會變成窮人。

i.sp: 這種笨蛋
i.ev: Tibetan/academic: 愚者 'fools' (those deluded by self-notion); 笨蛋 is a harsh, insulting word for a children's text.
i.fx: 這樣糊塗的人

atts.t: 那時候，菩薩看到眾生很窮苦，就相信分享的好處，總是慷慨地把東西送人。對他來說，充滿寶物的四大洲就像口水一樣不值錢。把東西送人讓他非常開心，就算得到四大洲，他也不會這麼高興。

i.sp: 就相信分享的好處
i.ev: Academic: 信解布施 'is devoted to / inclined toward giving'; the text does not say he believes in benefits of sharing.
i.fx: 就喜愛布施

atts.t: 聰明清朗的菩薩，看著三種存在的領域。他對裡面所有的眾生，心裡這樣想：「我願對大家展現這份慷慨。」菩薩這樣想著去幫助別人。為了眾生的緣故，他把這份善意奉獻給最高的覺悟。

i.sp: 他把這份善意奉獻給最高的覺悟
i.ev: Academic: 彼亦…迴向殊勝菩提 'he also dedicates it (the giving) to supreme awakening'; 'goodwill' replaces the gift/giving itself.
i.fx: 他把這份慷慨也奉獻給最高的覺悟

i.sp: 菩薩這樣想著去幫助別人。
i.ev: Not in the text; the sentence only repeats that he thinks 'may I give this gift to all' and gives.

atts.t: 菩薩展現慷慨之後，不會一直把這件事放在心上。他任何時候都不會期待，想要得到什麼成熟的結果。這樣懂得給予的人，能放下一切。就算只給出一點點，最後也會變成無限大。

i.sp: 不會一直把這件事放在心上
i.ev: Academic: 不住於實事 'does not abide in / fixate on the thing (as real)'; 'keep it in mind' reads as simply not remembering the gift.
i.fx: 不會執著自己給出去的東西

atts.t: 想像在三種存在的領域裡，有著數也數不清的眾生。如果他們在漫長的時代裡，不斷對通曉世界的人，也就是佛陀，還有值得敬重的人與獨自覺悟的人，展現慷慨，只為了努力成為聽法的弟子。

i.sp: 展現慷慨，只為了努力成為聽法的弟子。
i.ev: Academic ends with a semicolon: the sentence is an 'if' clause that continues in the next verse; the children's text ends with a full stop, leaving an unfinished 'if' sentence.
i.fx: …展現慷慨，一心想成為聽法的弟子，（接下一節）

atts.t: 有良好品行，就不會過著當動物的一生。也不會落入八種不自由的處境。菩薩會一直擁有自由修行的機會。因為有耐心，菩薩會變得非常好看。他們散發美麗金光，大家都喜歡看著他們。

i.sp: 他們散發美麗金光
i.ev: Academic: 身色金黃美麗 'the body color is golden and beautiful' (a color, not light radiating).
i.fx: 他們的身體是美麗的金黃色

atts.t: 持續的努力，讓善良的品質不會減少。還能打開得勝者的寶庫，得到無邊深刻的領悟。透過深度專注，就能放下不好的欲望。他們會學會知識，獲得特殊的了知與深度安定。

i.sp: 放下不好的欲望
i.ev: Academic: 捨棄應受呵責之欲妙 'abandon the despised sense pleasures (objects of desire)', not desires in general.
i.fx: 放下不值得貪求的感官享樂

atts.t: 透過智慧，他們完全了解事物的本性。這樣就能真正從三個領域中解脫出來。就像人類中最傑出的領袖轉動了珍寶輪。為了消除大家的痛苦，他們向眾生分享佛法。

i.sp: 就像人類中最傑出的領袖轉動了珍寶輪。
i.ev: Academic: 人中牛王轉動輪寶之後，為盡除苦亦向眾生宣說佛法: the one who has become the supreme leader of humans turns the wheel and then teaches the Dharma (a sequence of actions by the same person). The children's text makes it a simile ('就像') and detaches the leader from the practitioners, dropping the sequence.
i.fx: 他成為人類中最傑出的領袖，轉動了珍寶輪，然後為了消除大家的痛苦，向眾生宣說佛法。

atts.t: 透過智慧，他們完全了解事物的本性。這樣就能真正從三個領域中解脫出來。他們成為人類中最傑出的領袖，轉動了珍寶輪。為了消除所有的痛苦，他們向眾生分享佛法。

i.sp: 從三個領域中解脫出來
i.ev: They pass beyond the three realms without remainder (ma lus pa, all of them); 'without remainder' is lost.
i.fx: 從三個領域中完全解脫出來，一個也不剩

i.sp: 他們成為人類中最傑出的領袖
i.ev: The 'best of humans' is an epithet of the one who turned the jewel wheel, not something the knowers 'become'.
i.fx: 那位人類中最傑出的領袖轉動了珍寶輪

atts.t: 第七篇：在一瞬間完全覺悟。那位菩薩完全圓滿了這些事物後，
第七章 在一瞬間完全覺悟。那位菩薩完全圓滿這些特質之後，
第八篇：講說佛法之身。菩薩會完全照顧完全純淨的國土，以及清淨的眾生。他也會完全照顧佛陀的傳承，還有佛法的傳承。他同樣會完全照顧僧團的傳承，還有所有的事物。

i.sp: 菩薩會完全照顧
i.ev: Academic has no stated subject ('完全攝受…'); the children's text supplies the bodhisattva as subject and uses 照顧 'take care of' for 攝受 'embrace/uphold'.
i.fx: 完全守護並保持完全純淨的國土，以及清淨的眾生

atts.t: 第八章 佛法之身。菩薩完全守護完全純淨的國土，還有清淨的眾生。他也完全守護佛陀的傳承，還有佛法的傳承。同樣地，他也完全守護僧團的傳承，以及所有的特質。

i.sp: 完全守護
i.ev: Tibetan yongs su 'dzin / academic 完全攝受 means fully taking up, embracing or holding; 'guarding' narrows it to protection only.
i.fx: 完全擁有並護持

atts.t: ऐसा क्यों है? क्योंकि विजेता ने जो शिक्षा दी है। सबसे महान पुरुष के शिष्य बनकर वे उसे अच्छे से सीखते हैं। वे उसे समझते हैं और जैसा सीखा है वैसा ही सिखाते हैं। वे ऐसा बुद्ध की ताक़त से करते हैं, अपनी ताक़त से नहीं।

i.sp: वे उसे समझते हैं
i.ev: Academic translation: having realized it directly (sakshat karke), they teach as they learned; 'understand' loses the direct realization.
i.fx: उसे खुद अनुभव करके जैसा सीखा है वैसा ही सिखाते हैं।

atts.t: जिसे सबसे बड़ी पूर्ण प्रज्ञा नहीं मिलती है। जिसे बोधि-वीर नहीं मिलता और बोधि पाने की इच्छा भी नहीं मिलती है। यह बात सुनकर जिसे कोई डर या उलझन नहीं होती। ऐसा बोधि-वीर भली-भाँति गए हुए की प्रज्ञा पर चलता है।

i.sp: जिसे सबसे बड़ी पूर्ण प्रज्ञा नहीं मिलती है। जिसे बोधि-वीर नहीं मिलता और बोधि पाने की इच्छा भी नहीं मिलती है।
i.ev: Text says perfect wisdom, bodhisattva and the wish for awakening are not apprehended (anupalabdha, not found as real things). 'Does not get/find' reads as the person lacking wisdom or failing to attain it.
i.fx: जो सबसे बड़ी पूर्ण प्रज्ञा को भी असली चीज़ की तरह नहीं पकड़ता, बोधि-वीर को भी नहीं, और बोधि पाने की इच्छा को भी नहीं।

atts.t: जो सबसे बड़ी पूर्ण प्रज्ञा को भी असली चीज़ की तरह नहीं पकड़ता। जो बोधि-वीर को भी नहीं, और बोधि पाने की इच्छा को भी नहीं पकड़ता। यह बात सुनकर जिसे कोई डर या उलझन नहीं होती। ऐसा बोधि-वीर भली-भाँति गए हुए की प्रज्ञा पर चलता है।

i.sp: जो सबसे बड़ी पूर्ण प्रज्ञा को भी असली चीज़ की तरह नहीं पकड़ता। जो बोधि-वीर को भी नहीं, और बोधि पाने की इच्छा को भी नहीं पकड़ता।
i.ev: The academic translation is a single 'for whom X, Y and Z are not apprehended ... that bodhisattva practises prajna' sentence; the children's text splits it into several 'who ...' fragments without a main verb until the last line, which is hard for ages 8-12 to follow. Meaning is intact.
i.fx: जो बोधि-वीर सबसे बड़ी पूर्ण प्रज्ञा, बोधि-वीर और बोधि पाने की इच्छा को असली चीज़ की तरह नहीं पकड़ता, और यह सुनकर उसे न उलझन होती है न डर, वही भली-भाँति गए हुए की प्रज्ञा पर चलता है।

atts.t: जैसे श्रेणिक नाम का एक घूमने वाला साधक अपने ज्ञान से समझता है। वह देखता है कि ढेर सच में नहीं मिलते। जो बोधि-वीर इसी तरह चीज़ें समझता है, वह दुख से परे शान्ति को पकड़कर नहीं रुकता। वह हमेशा प्रज्ञा में टिका रहता है।

i.ev: Academic translation: through the knowledge of the wanderer Shreni, the unfindable aggregates are dissolved/destroyed (vinasha); the children's text drops the dissolution and only says the aggregates are not found.
i.fx: जैसे श्रेणिक नाम के घूमने वाले साधक के ज्ञान से ढेर सच में न मिलकर बिखर जाते हैं।

i.sp: दुख से परे शान्ति को पकड़कर नहीं रुकता। वह हमेशा प्रज्ञा में टिका रहता है।
i.ev: Text: he does not touch nirvana; he abides in wisdom. 'Clinging and stopping' and 'always' are not in the source.
i.fx: वह दुख से परे शान्ति को छूता नहीं, वह प्रज्ञा में टिका रहता है।

atts.t: जैसे श्रेणिक नाम के घूमने वाले साधक के ज्ञान से ढेर सच में न मिलकर बिखर जाते हैं। जो बोधि-वीर इसी तरह चीज़ें समझता है, वह दुख से परे शान्ति को पकड़कर नहीं रुकता। वह हमेशा प्रज्ञा में टिका रहता है।

i.sp: दुख से परे शान्ति को पकड़कर नहीं रुकता
i.ev: The Tibetan and academic translation say the bodhisattva 'does not touch' nirvana (mya ngan 'das la mi reg); 'does not stay clinging to it' changes the image to an interpretation.
i.fx: वह दुख से परे शान्ति को छूता नहीं।

i.sp: हमेशा
i.ev: The text says only that he 'abides in prajna' (shes rab gnas); 'always' is not stated.
i.fx: वह प्रज्ञा में टिका रहता है।

i.sp: ढेर सच में न मिलकर बिखर जाते हैं
i.ev: The academic translation says the unapprehended aggregates are destroyed/dissolved; the phrase 'not really found, they scatter' is awkward for children.
i.fx: ढेर, जो असल में कहीं मिलते ही नहीं, बिखर जाते हैं।

atts.t: अगर कोई नासमझी में रूप को पकड़ता है। अगर वह अनुभूति, इरादा और जागरूकता के ढेर में भटकता है। वह भले ही सोचे कि 'ये ढेर खाली हैं', फिर भी ऐसा बोधि-वीर निशान में ही अटका है। उसे कभी न जन्मा हुआ स्थान पर विश्वास नहीं है।

i.sp: उसे कभी न जन्मा हुआ स्थान पर विश्वास नहीं है।
i.ev: Ungrammatical postposition; source: not faithful/trusting toward the unborn state.
i.fx: उसे कभी न जन्मे हुए स्थान पर भरोसा नहीं है।
